title: HC Mike LaFleur Press Conference 9.1.26 | AZ Cardinals
text: you have a guy like Bam who you have a history with. How does that how does that manifest itself when you get to be in a position of head coach and you know dealing with a guy like that? >> Um well I mean it's been a while since I've been with Bam you know so I mean this was just kind of uh luck of the draw if you will. I mean he was on the roster. Um I always had a lot of respect for Bam as a runner. Had him as a young guy. So, he uh as he would contest, you know, he say, he had some learning to do in terms of just getting used to the NFL game, but uh man, he he did some really good stuff for us. I know we went up in his rookie year, went up to Minnesota and he ripped off a 60 yard off of a gun run, ended up having 100 plus yards that game. Um you know, so you could see the talent there and uh did some good stuff a week or two later in Buffalo. So, um, but again, it's been a few years and and just looking at the tape and and knowing what kind of guy and and seeing what kind of guy he's grown into both, uh, just professionally and then as a player, um, you know, I thought it was, uh, pretty simple. You guys see his running style, you know, I mean, it's it's pretty evident. >> You said you said earlier during camp that like it's tough to evaluate running backs during practice, but with BAM, it's not really that hard to evaluate it. In what ways does it kind of stand out? >> Well, let me clarify it because he's done it. like he's been out on the field, you know, he's he's played on Sundays and um but at the same time, the way he runs it, you you would think it's tackle football when it was in in some of those training camp practices. Like he he only knows one way. Not even that he's trying to run you over. His just his body lean is real and that carries over like that that that's what the the tape shows as well, you know. So, the only thing that's really held Bam back is um you know his health. Um just being able to stay healthy and and sometimes the way he he runs and his um his running style. It's it's not conducive to always to to stay healthy, but he's he he puts so much into his body and and and making sure that he can be out there as much as possible. So, um you know, if we can keep him healthy and and he can keep himself healthy, uh you know, the sky's is the limit for him. What are the biggest differences that you've seen from Bam now as opposed to Bam then? >> Uh just I I would just say that the the growth of of prof and again not that there was anything bad but I think it's just been the time on task the amount of years he's been into it. Um just a much better understanding which you would expect from any position in in any player a better understanding of the whole picture uh protections the run game all that kind of stuff. So that's what I'd say. >> You bring up body leaning a lot. What exactly is that? And And when when do you realize that a guy >> he's not he he doesn't run up right? I mean he's his pads are like his pads are always going forward you know. So um yeah that's what it is. >> When you look at the quarterback room obviously there's tons of experience within that room. Well is there any other trait that you maybe admire most about what that room as a whole kind of brings to the table? >> The the quarterbacks. >> I just appreciate that they're all themselves. All three of them. They're all very uh different in in Slovis obviously really happy for him obviously getting to Green Bay. So he didn't know there was a potential audition on that game for that team. But but all these guys understand that you know um that all all other 31 teams are watching. But uh no I mean I I just think um you know you got to be a leader but you got to be a leader you know within your personality and and being authentically yourself. And all three of those guys are very comfortable with who they are as people. you feel like this offense is overall in terms of their operation and their comfort in your system? >> Um, still work in progress. Uh, which I anticipated u you know today we have a pretty loaded practice in terms of of scheme concepts introducing I wouldn't say some new stuff but different ways to do some of the stuff we did uh just to present it to our defense. That was kind of on purpose. I wanted this to be a a a just a loaded day mentally and physically. Um knowing that when we get here next week, it's only the Chargers. Like it's not the Chargers right now. We're introducing some things for the Chargers, but like not showing why we're doing it against them, you know? So, it'll be uh I think they'll be pleasantly uh surprised with how tight it ends up being next week. And then I'll probably have a better answer for you when we leave on, you know, on Friday in terms of those three days, what it looks like. um you know, if you guys can help me out with asking them some questions and and saying what I said that their Saturday walkthrough is going to be like nothing they've ever done before. Um except for Hunter because he did it in LA. Um and it's just a it's just a fine tune. It's not just from a coaching standpoint to make sure these guys are crossing their tees or dotting their eyes. It's so that they can see that their teammates know what what the heck's going on, too. Um so, um right now, not as concerned about how I answer that. Uh, you know, next week I will be because it'll be a tighter plan. It'll be very specific to what we're trying to get done. >> When you say today's a heavy or heavy load day mentally, how will that compare with a game week? Will that will they be equally as heavy or is it a little bit more? >> No, this is this is the last of I would say the heavy practices for the year just in terms of reps. Um, because one, you got to get them to Sundays where they're feeling good. there's that that there's that great balance between getting our work in, practicing the right way, but also making sure that those guys are feeling as good as they can on Sunday, both mentally and physically. So, um, today is what, Tuesday? I mean, we're still 12 12 days away from when we kick it off. They got the three days off. They they'll have tomorrow off from a from a physical standpoint. We'll still come in, we'll get a lift, we'll jog jog through and stuff like that, but the they'll be off and then on Thursday um won't be as as heavy of a of workload in terms of reps is exactly how we scripted this thing out all the way dating back to July where it was low, really high, and then I wouldn't call it medium on that third day, but not as high as that kind of second day of the block. where you are uh in terms of the team you have right now, the couple guys that you might have been that might have been battling for a starting spot or whatever and we know a lot of these guys are all going to play anyways, but like are those decisions made now? Are you still sorting through some of that stuff before you get to next week? Um there there's still probably a couple conversations that need to be had that I'll obviously keep uh within within our staff and stuff like that, but uh you know, for for the mo for the most part, you know, who's going to be out there if everyone stays healthy over these next 12 days, uh which you anticipate that being because there's no live tackling or anything like that, but things happen. Um, you know, and so now it's again it's we're we're kind of fine-tuning some things in terms of where guys are going to be and what roles they're going to fit into, but again, we're not focused on the Chargers, focused on competition right now. >> You've been around long enough that there were still four preseason games at the beginning of your NFL coaching career. Do you like having it be like this where you have this extra time after the last preseason game? Because it used to be a little bit quicker of a turnaround because of the extra game. >> I do. And it it was I was actually explaining this to someone the other day. Not that it totally matters, but I'll go on a soap box real quick. The that fourth uh that fourth preseason game I we could not stand. It was it was every all 32 teams were on a Thursday and then the cut down day was um basically started on Saturday into Sunday, whatever. And then you'd have the bonus Monday leading into the first week. Well, that fourth preseason game, no starters played. You basically didn't practice the day before because you didn't you were already cut down to whatever it was 67 players or whatever it was and you had to get rid of 14 more. But some of those guys had to play that next day. So, you didn't have enough to run an actual practice. So, your starters didn't get any work on that Wednesday. So, they worked on Tuesday. They got no work on that Wednesday. They didn't play on Thursday. You had to give them Friday off. So now you're like, "Oh, like we haven't played football in forever." And then on Saturday, which all the players knew was the cut down day. You just, it was a weird day. It was a weird practice. And then Sunday, you didn't practice. And then Monday, you didn't have your practice squad guys back. So it just was like, you didn't feel, and this was all teams. It wasn't like it was one team or the other. You almost felt like you didn't practice for over a week with your starters. And that sucked. Uh the way this is structured, you end up getting this this extra week. And everyone's doing it a little bit different. There's not like a set in stone. And then obviously there's teams playing Wednesday, Thursday. I think there's a game on Friday as well, uh, or something like that. So, um, there's a lot of different ways you can approach it. I thought it fit really well for us in terms of the our block. We got practice, practice, jog through practice, and they get three days off, then we'll come back and get a a light, you know, Monday bonus day when we get back. >> Short answer, I love it. >> You guys in preseason had had, you know, basically the best offensive numbers in the league. Flip side. You had [clears throat] some of the biggest defensive numbers allowed. Do you put any stock in something like that? >> I didn't I thought that was going to be the answer. So then what do you look for from your defense in terms of what you're actually I know a lot of it is player assessment but as an overall defense >> these defenses are at such a disadvantage in the preseason. You don't show absolutely anything. Um you know and I'm not covering for anything. It's just, you know, I mean, no matter who gets thrown out there, you want to just go execute fundamentally and just, you know, play the call and and and, you know, do the best you can within the call, but, uh, it's it's a a pretty simple deal from an offensive standpoint. When you know they're doing this or that, it's when you don't know if they're doing this, that, the other, and you know, everything in between. Uh, that's when it gets, you know, tough. And what's tough on a defense and a defensive coordinator and a defensive scheme is what's that fine balance between allowing our guys to go play fast. But also making it so we as offensive guys don't know what's coming. Um unless you're just absolutely, you know, uh the most loaded defense ever and then sometimes you can just run a few calls and and they just happen to be better than you. Uh and that kind of is what it is. But uh no, there's um you know there's there's nothing that I put into numbers or any of that kind of stuff. I just want to see our guys uh execute the the call. I want to see us operate and I want to see our play style. I thought we um operated well, not well enough. I thought our play style was was pretty good. Uh there's room for improvement right there and I thought by the player, by the position, there was some good execution. There was a lot to clean up. [snorts] >> What do you hope could be the strengths of this defense this season? >> Well, I mean, there's a lot of guys on that defense that have played a lot of football. Uh uh I mean you think like really you go into that first um game versus the Chargers and I'm I'm kind of thinking as I'm saying this but for the most part every single guy has played on Sundays before and that's a big deal. It's not going to be eye opening the speed of the game what kind you know how different a Sunday feels compared to a preseason game compared to practice. We try to simulate game game like situations as much as possible. It's not a game and the guys know that. they don't their their heart rate's not racing when they get out to practice. They're just executing and hopefully not just trying to survive, but you know what I mean. Um so, uh having that have just knowing that we have a bunch of veterans out there that have done it and and and guys that have done it at a high clip. I mean, Buddha Baker is the easy one that comes out. Well, you guys haven't seen him obviously this camp. Um you know, and a handful of other guys. I mean, Mack played in one, you know, one series of of that the the u the Vegas game there. So, um, that's what I'm most excited about is all those guys. They know what the the speed is and now just go execute the scheme, go execute the call. >> Carson [snorts] been going pretty consistently since he entered the building from the draft and then he had to slow down. What's his return to practice look like? How do you look yesterday? Can he kind of pick up where he left off? >> Yeah, I mean I I don't think anyone can te typically pick up where they left off. U, but I thought he did well. you know, I mean, it's it's been a few weeks since obviously he's played and just like any other position, it'll it'll take time just to kind of get back into that comfort and um you know, and and um just you know, doing his responsibility within what we're asking him to do. >> You mentioned all the days of the week, the games that we played next week. As some of this is part of the NFL, how do you feel about kind of taking over multiple days and Mondays? Didn't Kyle answer something like this and get in trouble or something like that? Um, so I think it's great. No, it's um, hey, listen, it's it's uh, obviously the biggest game um, in the United States by far. There's not even a close second. I think the the closest second is college football. So that I think that speaks volumes of of what football means to this country. Um, you know, and and it's growing globally and that's why you're you're seeing it uh, you know, move over there. Like I don't know if you guys have been over to Europe when you've played over there or at least you know it's it's a really cool environment and um you know so you understand it's it's it it sometimes gets uh choppy in terms of you you love routine and um we got we got routine um we we play 17 Sundays at the daytime and I think we all understand why and if we want to play in in those prime time slots and on Wednesdays and Thursdays and Netflix and all those kind of things well we got to go earn those spots. Uh, we understand that. I think Green Bay, it's like they don't have like a seven-day stretch like hardly at all. Um, their byee is so twisted. They play on a Sunday and then they have their by-week, but then they play the the following Wednesday. So, it's not even a by-week, but then after they play Wednesday, they don't play till the following Sunday. So, it's like the by-week split in two. Like, that's just the way this league is going. You better get used to it if you're a good football team. Hopefully, we have those issues, you know, moving forward. >> You when you were in San Francisco, you were coached with Mike McDaniel. I know you haven't worked on the Chargers that much yet, but can your relationship with him and kind of knowing how he thinks, how can you use that when you start to game those guys? >> Yeah, I mean it's uh obviously from a defensive perspective, our defense with their offense and Yeah, but I I haven't been with Mike since 2020. Just like um when everyone's kind of ventured off and there I mean everyone's gone their own way and there's foundational aspects are the same. I do think there is a fine line between what I tell Nick and the defense because you oversaturate anyone. I don't think that I don't I I personally don't think that helps. I think there's little things that you know through the last six months that Nick and I have talked about that as he's just gathering his thoughts and stuff getting ready for these teams that that you do know some. That's good. But again, I I I'm trying really hard not to oversaturate anyone with with the stuff because again, I don't know what they're changing. I I I don't know exactly what he was saying in Miami. I mean, I know some, but then now he's got Herbert and in a whole new place. Like, who knows, you know, how much they've changed and adjusted. >> You were talking earlier about there's still a few rules that you guys have to have conversations about in the building. As you decide those things, do you have conversations with the player? I mean, obviously some starts some spots the starter plays and the backup doesn't do. you'll have those conversations, but if it's a spot like defensive line or there's a ton of rotation, how much are you having those conversations with guys about their roles and what exactly >> where communication lacks, negativity fills the void. So, I if if it crosses my mind to have to to talk to these guys, then yes, I'm going to talk to them. And and sometimes it might be in passing, sometimes it might be, you know, I ended up having a conversation during a special teams period with a guy that wasn't playing special teams for two minutes yesterday that I kind of had on my notes I want to talk to and it just felt right in that moment, you know. Um, so yeah, if if if there's a conversation warranted, then yes, we are going to have that conversation. >> Carson [snorts] had a pretty impressive training camp. What impressed you the most about him and laying on the 50? >> Yeah, just just going about his business. uh you know, he's been a really good he's always been a really good specialteamer. Um you know, Dayton obviously back to Iowa and stuff like that. And uh just continuing to get more improvement in in um when he's in there at linebacker. I thought he got better as the preseason went on. Um you know, and and and I know he knows this, but but uh what all these guys got to understand is they're one snap away from being starters or maybe two snaps if they're kind of that third guy in, but uh it can happen quick. So don't just lock into being an allp pro specialteamer if you will. Make sure that we're ready in all phases. >> Always difficult for a rookie start. >> Obviously camp is training camp is always going to be difficult for a rookie but with Carson he missed most of spring practices too. What was the kind of ramp up there throughout training camp for him to get acclimated? >> Uh nothing from a physical standpoint. He was if I can gosh it's already been September. We got started in late July. Um but there was nothing from a physical standpoint. He was ready to roll uh pretty quickly I I believe in the summer. Um you know so it was just yeah getting up to speed mentally with everything which didn't from from my vantage point didn't seem like an issue. >> Big can bring on the field but what have you noticed from him maybe in the locker room or just away from the >> call him big Bill. Is that is that his nickname? >> That's what >> that's okay good. >> Good to know little Bill. Um, now he's he he's a he's a he's a really cool dude to work with. He is he is uh even demeanor at all times and he is a big man on the inside and uh you know what you want from him, what you want from Roy is a that first and second down and make it hard as heck on the interior, you know, the center and the guards and and plug in those gaps, allow everyone else to do what they do behind and you know when when it transitions to pass, go do what you can, push that center back right into the quarterback's lap. So, um, he's I thought he had a great year in Chicago last year. I'm we're very fortunate to have him.

title: General Manager Ian Cunningham & Assistant GM Jeff Scott Initial 53-Man Roster Press Conference
text: It's good to see everybody. I feel like I haven't seen you guys in a long time. >> [clears throat] >> Feel free to see us more. >> [laughter] >> But first, um, we just like to say say something to you guys. Um, there's a lot that goes into to training camp and since we haven't had a chance to really talk to you, um, much at all. Um, I feel like with the amount of people, the fans that have come out here to to show us some support, you know, there's a lot that our ops staff, the grounds crew and everybody has to go through. So, so much thanks to our ops staff. Um, with Spence and B-Rube, um, and Nicole and Austin, just getting us prepared for everything and all of our travel. Uh, they're phenomenal. You know, our equipment staff, uh, there's a lot of players that we've brought in during this time, uh, for workouts. Um, some quite a few transactions, obviously going to Indy. Uh, there's a lot of work that has to be done there. So, want to thank Joey and his staff, our performance staff, have done a really good job of coming together, working together uh, to help some of our guys that are returning from play, uh, but also some guys that got injured during training camp. Um, so it's been really good to see those guys work together, uh, for the greater good. So, want to say thank you to them and I'm like I mentioned, our grounds crew. We've, I mean, it's been, you [clears throat] guys have been here, right? It's been hot, it's been muggy, uh, we've had a lot of rain. Uh, for our for our grass to look the way it does, uh, there's a lot of work that goes into it. You know, we joke around up there seeing those guys put a lot of work on that field from early in the morning to late at night. So, want to say thank you to them. And then our IT and video, you know, going to Indy, uh that's a lot of work for them to essentially move our office, our our headquarters up to a hotel. Um so, Will and and Jake and those guys, a lot of credit to them to allow us to to operate and do what we needed to do while we were there and then throughout training camp. Um like I mentioned, you know, we haven't we haven't chatted um since the beginning of training camp. And when we came in for training camp, one of the things that we did, I asked Matt and Austin to kind of put this video together for for our staff uh to really highlight um and from an education standpoint, the history of Atlanta, but wanted to tie in the history of the Falcons as well, right? There's a lot of people that have come before us to to put us in this position and for us to be thankful and grateful for that opportunity, but I feel like it was and we needed that education for us to really understand that. Um I thought it was a really good video, but now it's on us to carry that torch and pull it forward. So, um with that, you know, there was a book that we had our our staff read this summer that was called Chop Wood Carry Water and it was a we always focus on the outcomes. We always want to win the Super Bowl. We want to do these things, but it's really about those daily disciplines that we do along the way and if we can focus on those daily disciplines, the outcome will be the byproduct of that. So, um I want to say thank you to the staff for believing in that and um continuing to work on that. We have to remind each other that because we live in this society, this microwave society where we want things instantaneously >> [snorts] >> um and we want to see the results instantaneously, but um if we focus on those daily disciplines, we'll get the results that we ultimately want. Um you know, these last 72 hours or so have been really tough, right? Um It's it's bittersweet having to say goodbye to people that you built relationships with along the way since the start of OTAs even workouts. And and you have to say goodbye, right? And you don't get to see them anymore. You don't have to you don't get to break bread down in the cafeteria with them anymore. Those those are tough decisions, you know, I've been released. We've had a couple people on our staff that have been released. So you know, there's there's empathy that goes into that. There's understanding. But those are those are some of the tough decisions that we have to make throughout um throughout this time. The roster gymnastics of have been challenging to say the least. Sorry, there's a >> Yeah. >> All right, you're good. You're good. >> Been challenging. But they're also fun, right? And feel really good with what we've come out with our 53. But also our 16 players on our practice squad as well. So with that we'll open it up for questions. >> What was the thought process behind keeping four quarterbacks? You know, when we first when we got into training camp you know, we came in with four quarterbacks and three of those four were were banged up, were injured. And so you know, you try to come in with a mindset of like all right, the sky's not falling. But you have three of your four quarterbacks that are injured the first day of training camp. We were fortunate enough to have a guy like Cooper Rush that was available at that point. Where is a [snorts] guy that's started games in this league. He's been a really good backup for a number of years. So for us to be able to get a player of his caliber at that point we were fortunate. And then for a kid from D2 Minnesota State Moorhead to come in and be work with the ones and actually do an admirable job. Says a lot about him and his maturity. And then to see Coop and and Jack continue to get better throughout while Tua and Mike were getting healthy. So that kind of put a coming in with that thinking all right, there's a there's some injury risk right with those guys trying to protect against that. There's a little bit of an insurance policy, but there's also these guys have been productive during the preseason. And so if you let a guy like Cooper go, there's a potential that he may be able to get an opportunity to go to another team. If you let a guy like Jack Strango, he is subject to waivers. And the way he played, you know, we like we talk about all the time draft develop retain. In his case he was undrafted but to develop, you know, there's a chance that somebody could have claimed him. So think it's about, you know, living in the now, but also living in the future with Jack. So that that kind of went into the the four quarterback thought process. >> Do you think Jack is here if he doesn't get that opportunity that first week that he got to be the guy to show y'all that? Do you think he Obviously that's a >> Yeah, that's that's a Yeah, it's that's tough to answer. What it did show it wasn't too big for him, you know, to come in [snorts] and and do what he did early on and he's shown the ability to just progress and get get better ever since rookie mini camp till now. >> Now Ian, when when it comes to your starting quarterback, I know you guys make these decisions as a group, and that right all the way down. But but at some point somebody will have to make the final final decision. Who's going to be that guy? >> Yeah, it's still I feel like that's us talking. We we talk constantly. We've talked about every single position. Um you know, every single position on this roster we've we've discussed what we think, but ultimately that that will when they're ready, when the coaches are ready, when the players are ready, we'll we'll make that decision. >> Do you have you guys already identified who your starter is for week one? >> Not yet. No. >> You were in Chicago right when you drafted Gervon Dexter right 2023. What did you like about Gervon then? What do you like about him now? How did that all kind of come together? >> Yeah, Gervon obviously a talented player young to the young to the game of football cuz he was a basketball player coming coming up. You know, you saw the upside and the potential at Florida. He's a big man that's strong that was still growing into his body. I you I don't know if you guys have had a chance to see him, but him and Mase together looked looked it's it's pretty cool to see. But big strong powerful explosive, you know, he he's grown had a chance to see him grow as a man. You know, having a son having a daughter and he's a as he's a family man and for him to be 24 years old and be that mature and care about the game of football and his teammates the way he does. I'm excited. We're excited to be able to get a player like him in the building to help us continue to grow on defense and overall with our team. >> And at one point like 28% of the sack number sorry I think you returned 28% of the sack numbers from last year and I I realized within that there's Walker and James and there's things you can't control about that, but when you got here how much of it was I want to retool what we have in our pass rush was it the plan to retool it as much as you did? >> I didn't really come in with the thought of the how are we going to like the stack piece. You know, we're we're we look at we're trying to win games, right? And um you know, if that's 57 sacks if it's less than that we're the the main goal was to to [snorts] win games to build this team to help these guys uh to create competition on the field and then to help uh develop and then hopefully retain some of these guys moving forward so we can continue to get better. >> You guys have to turn over the defensive line room quite a bit. So, you talk about, you know, Gervon Dexter playing basketball, Jared Ivey even claimed him. He looked like he used to hoop back in the day as well. Like, what are some of the benefits of having some of those long guys that can touch the knees when they're standing up? >> Yeah, I think that's what we we look for big, powerful, rugged, explosive, violent players. Like, that's what that's what we want. Um and, you know, watching Jared Ivey's tape, remember us watching it that that night, all of us in the room, and you you saw some of the plays he plays he plays our brand of ball. And um it's just and put the cherry on top was he's just from right around the corner. So, how cool is that for him to be able to play for a hometown team? Um [snorts] and this is kind of new for me just being uh in Chicago the last few years, but it feels like every >> player you look at is from Georgia, you know? >> And so, it plays to our benefit, too. >> Ian, when you talk about the the depth of the team, I mean, keeping four quarterbacks, the trickle-down effect on the game [snorts] day, you're going to theoretically third quarterback, [clears throat] emergency quarterback that doesn't count against 48, but another quarterback who uh is still on the roster taking up a spot here. So, does that speak to the the comfort you have with the depth, or how did you come to the decision to sacrifice depth in another position in favor of the fourth quarterback? >> Yeah, that's that's good good question. I feel like that's a little bit of the roster gymnastics, right? And it's you know, four quarterbacks and two running backs, right? Um you have to sacrifice some at some position, but also know that we've got 16 practice squad spots. So, being thoughtful in that, too, of who you put on practice squad, where you have certain spots where we feel comfortable about some elevations if we need that. I I that's where you've got to get a little little bit creative. Um and feel like we're we're in that space right now. Um and it it will probably change throughout the season. Just because we start with this 53 now, it may not be the same 53 that it is, you know, week 18. >> What was the rationale in totality in putting that practice squad group together? >> Yeah, uh Dillard, you you know, we have you know, 16 [clears throat] spots, obviously, uh with the potential of adding another one with IPP guy, right? there's six veteran spots that we could use, which we have right now. Um there's a little bit of looking at the positions where we feel like we could add um if we wanted to do an elevation for player at a certain position based off of maybe being a little bit weak there or maybe what they could provide on special teams. Um it's a little bit of development, players that we feel that we can that have a higher upside that could potentially be backups and starters in this league. So, there's a little bit of the guys that are ready-made that you can bring up to the active roster and you know that they can help you right now. And there's a little bit of uh these are guys that you feel that have some developmental upside um that we are confident in in their abilities to develop. >> Jeff, what was what was your part in this this process and your vantage point on just the last few weeks or so? >> Yeah, no, I appreciate that, Will. Um I think one of the big things uh we talk about it all the time, it's process. Uh it's really about focusing in and and driving our process. And I want to give a kudos to our scouting department, our football administration, um football IT, uh analytics, and our coaching staff for being a part of this process. It's something that starts in training camp. And from identification and then the preseason goes, it's a lot of work. There's a lot of work done on players that never actually end up getting released, but at the end of the day, that sets the groundwork and your framework for your work throughout the season. So, um it's driving the process and ensuring that we are uncovering every stone. Um we are pleased with the outcome, but it's not something that will ever stop. We will be relentless in this. Um and continue to push and and try to get better at any opportunity we can. >> Jeff, we saw Billy Bowman get [snorts] kind of activated in the 53. It seems like the thought is he would be nearing a return. >> Yeah, um really really proud of Billy, man. It's a testament to him, um his work ethic, um his resilience, the time in which he's put into his body to uh fight to get back. Uh we the the beauty is we have a lot of players like that. What we're seeing is we have a lot of players that [snorts] um are fighting to get back, that are resilient, that are willing to fight through some nicks. Um but in Billy's case, um he's done a really good job and a lot of credit also goes to our, you know, return to play staff with with Nick and and Aaron, um Jake File and our trainers, our performance staff, strength and conditioning, putting an outstanding plan together in order for him to come back and feel confident. Now, when that time will be, um [snorts] I can't tell you, uh but we do feel comfortable enough to not keep him on PUP, so I think that should say that should say something. >> Guys, how do you evaluate Mike and his health? You know, given his comments about just kind of doing the mental part of it. And I know he's only in a certain number of practices, but how do you evaluate 10 practices versus 12 versus 15? I mean, a game is a game and the only way to sort of figure this out is to put him in a game and see if he's ready, so how do you measure that readiness at this point when practice is just practice? It's never going to be able to simulate a game type situation. >> You Those are the Those are the cards that we were dealt, right? And I think that's where you you've got to be able to evaluate the practice, evaluate, you know, the operation, evaluate the accuracy, the anticipation, the movement, comfortability in the pocket, so, you know, those things are we're going to be evaluating in the game, too. It's just we weren't we didn't have the luxury to do so, right? So, at the end of the day is like we got to evaluate what we can in the in the scope of what we have, and then, you know, when it's when he's ready, when the other guys are ready, we'll >> And is it Can you say honestly this is a you're looking down the years on the road, but also this year, is this a roster that you built with the expectation they can make the playoffs this year? >> We're competing to make the playoffs. That's what we're doing. That's why we we play, right? You want as many shots on net to allow yourselves the opportunity to get into the dance, and once you get in, who knows what may happen. So, we're constantly we're going to continue to invest in the roster. That's the main goal. That's why we do what we're doing, so whatever we can do to continue to push us forward, that's what we're that's what we'll do. >> You know, you got the hair of Perkins and Kendall Daniels seem to have come in and kind of put their stamps on themselves as as rookies. Like, can you talk about that as you see them as to coming in with especially with Perkins being a like a sixth and late round pick, [clears throat] and being able to come in and say, "Hey, I want to be able to play, and put myself in a position to be able to make it have an effect on the team as rookies?" >> Yeah, kudos to those guys, man. They came in, and there's they're they're pros already, just in terms of how they attack it every single day. You know, Kendall was dealing with some injuries during OTAs, but how he approached that, similar to what we were talking about Billy is, you know, he wasn't out there just, you know, sitting there. He was engaged, you know, he was by coach Rude and uh, trying to learn the defense. Um, that says a lot to who he is and then I'm sure you guys have been at practice and see he's a vocal kid, right? It was he's more vocal than what I remember seeing at Oklahoma. Um, so uh, um it's great. We love it. We need as much as much energy as we can out there and he provides it. So, the more guys that we can get like him to create that, um, we we'll get that. And then Perk, you know, I've touched on it before, you know, everybody knew who Harold Perkins was as that freshman at LSU, um, and then he's kind of battled through some injuries, some defensive uh, scheme uh, changes. Uh, and then for him now it's just, you know, we've got the belief in him and he's got the belief in himself and uh, you know, again, a lot of credit goes to him and the work that he's put in, but also coach Ulbrich, uh, coach Hocksable, Barrett and those guys. >> Ian, you brought in Zadarius Smith recently. What did you guys see in him and >> how's he been adjusting? >> Yeah, I mean, I think, um, Zadarius Smith just was an opportunity. I mean, for a player like that to be available at the time, uh, when we brought him in was a huge benefit to us. Um, I obviously I was with Zadarius last year in Philadelphia. Um, coach said coached him in Cleveland and Ian was in Baltimore when when they drafted him. So, uh, I think we have a a good understanding of the player. Excited to have him out here. Um, he's been bringing energy even, uh, as he kind of warms up and and progresses to to get ready to go. Um, and that's what we can ask for. Um, him to be a veteran leader, um, do what he's done and just to continue to build on where he's going. So, we were excited to be able to get a player like that at that time. >> In In your experience, like how often do you does like triangulating a player with relationships like that make the deciding factor in in a moment where certainly free agent where they have some agency in it, but like does it come down to relationships as as often as nothing? >> I I'd like to believe so, right? I like to believe so. I think just as human nature when you know when you know somebody, you you tend to gravitate towards them versus the known versus the unknown, right? And then it helps when there's a need. It helps when there's you know, there's other factors there. So, but I would like to believe that relationships do matter. >> Ian, what what else do you guys feel like you need to see as far as the quarterbacks? Was it just getting Mike more reps, you know, in 11s on in practice? Is that kind of mostly what it is at this point? >> Yeah. Yeah, the more the more reps, the more evaluations we can get, the better, right? Just just like we discussed. Like it's that's that's what the hand that we were dealt. So, the more opportunities that we can to evaluate, the better it is. >> I know you guys have to make hard decisions when you do this. Is there a position that you felt like you needed more depth at and why you went in a certain direction as far as the roster was concerned more than another you were willing to sacrifice it somewhere else? >> In terms of creating the 53 or overall? >> yeah. >> Um I don't not necess- I don't I don't think so. It's just like philosophically knowing that we wanted to invest in the in the front, especially on defense with Brick wanting to be uh multiple, um it requires a little bit more I guess a a little bit more like different different styles, different players. Um so, you need to add some depth to those, right? So, which then requires a couple more bodies. And then when you have a the four quarterbacks, you're going to have to take away from a a few positions. But also on the back end, really happy with the versatility that we have in our back with our corners, our nickels, and our safeties. You know, we've got guys that can play nickel and safety. We have got guys that can play nickel and outside. So, that helps with kind of manufacturing some spots as well. >> Jeff, I'm going to circle back to quarterbacks and I'm addressing you cuz you were with Howie more recently than than Ian. They kept four, too, and I think he basically said it's just a positional value. That's the position that you've got to take care of. I wonder how much in y'all's decision-making this year it was just it's quarterback. You know, we don't we don't care. The consequence is this is quarterback. Nothing else matters if we don't get it right. >> I think the one thing that that needs to be said just in general about it is anybody who makes this 53 earned it. Those guys went out there and earned it. So, um it just so happens that we had four guys who went out and and earned it at that position, and it's a good position to have depth. So, um far as I'm concerned, it's about whoever goes out there, works, and earns it. Ian talked about stacking days and being consistent, and we saw that um throughout camp uh from all those guys. So, it's just an opportunity for us, and I think we're happy with where we are. >> Now, Ian, go go back to starting quarterback. Again, final decision, is that Kevin? Is that you? Is that Matt? Is that Arthur? Or is it somebody else? >> We all talk about it, and we all have been talking about it forever. So, at the end of the day, we'll make the decision, and when it's time to make the decision, we'll let you know. >> And with uh regards to Javon, um you said before just how much you value draft picks, and so it was all of those rises you made that. But it was Is the intent with him that you're open to to extend him and keep him here long term? Or is is that Have you crossed that >> Can you repeat that? You said value >> You value them for like how much you value draft picks and so to send them a fifth say something about his you know we see in in Gervonta. I'm curious like do you see a plan past this year to have another part of the team? >> Yeah and we we always do value we do value draft picks and we value good players and we believe that we'll get some comp picks. So you take that into account as well. So when you can get a player of Gervonta's caliber for the price that we paid we felt that it was in the best interest of us to do that and we'll let this thing play out and see where it goes have a lot of confidence in him and his ability as long with our defensive staff and we'll cross that bridge when we when we get there. >> With the two running backs on the 53 and the two on the practice squad with Woodson be the ready-made and Cat Jones the developmental? >> I believe that's fair to say. >> Yep. >> If you take yourself back to the beginning of OTAs do you see did you see Penix as realistically being ready for week one or how would you kind of characterize the progress he's made to put himself in this position? >> Yeah and feel like you know there's this saying it never put a cap on somebody you know never put a ceiling on somebody so I never went into it thinking that he was or he wasn't going to be ready we never went into it that way things happen you know so again with him for him to be where he's at it shows because he's been working his tail off to get to this point and our staff putting a really good plan together for him to get to the point of 11 on 11 where we're having these conversations where who's going to be the starting quarterback and is he going to be ready it goes to show you like he's put himself in that position because of the work that he's put in. >> Is it safe to say at this point, I mean, you know, given that roster construction is a 12-month-a-year deal, at this point, do you do you anticipate making any more moves before they kick things off in week one? >> On the on >> Do you anticipate >> Are you saying the 53 or back >> I don't I don't envision I don't envision that, but I I yeah, I don't want to say yes or no, but I don't envision that. Yeah. >> were you surprised at like you typically there's a couple of big names every off season who end up not making a 53 that people scurry to. It felt like this off season there wasn't really Were you sort of kind of surprised it was a sort of quieter post-53 cutdown than normal? >> Uh you know, I to that point, um I thought it was I feel like we thought it was actually more active than before just um you know, with the amount of trades that occurred uh towards the towards the deadline um cutdown deadline. Uh which is which is something that we'll go back and look at a little bit more and um maybe learn from but it felt like it was a little bit more active. I don't know if that's uh uh just this year or is this a trend? So, we'll we'll do some research on that and figure that out. >> Jeff, looking at uh um how he went from AGM to general manager, like do you see yourself in that position and what do you feel like you can kind of learn being able to make that transition? Like what does that mean to you? >> I think at the end of the day, I'm I'm really focused on kind of being good at my job here. Uh I think I've had I've been lucky to be in good places, um but the biggest focus is to be good at what you do. And my focus right now is being the best assistant GM I can be. Um and whatever comes down the line, I'm not thinking about it. I'm focused on what's going on here right now at the Falcons. So, I appreciate that, but yeah. >> Yes, he is a future GM. I'll answer that for you. >> Time for a couple more? >> With the decision with the quarterbacks, what Tua has done thus far has been a Would you say it's part of the reason you're still you're still not decided? >> Based off Tua? Just >> Yes, like his like what do you what have you seen from him is part of the reason why you're at the point of not having made a decision on the number one? >> I believe it will we're evaluating all the quarterbacks. It's not It's not just Tua. So, like like I said, Mike's coming back. He just got back in 11-on-11. [snorts] Tua has been here. He came in a little bit banged up. So, he started a little bit behind. Cooper comes in. He's just He wasn't anywhere during OTAs. So, he comes in and he's starting to get, you know, his feet going and Jack showed up. So, again, you're evaluating all the quarterbacks. I wouldn't just put it on Tua uh for for us not making the decision. >> Mike just >> option tag next spring, would it would it help you guys to see him a lot this year? >> Because of the option tag? >> the option tag. >> I just want to see I I would Yeah, I mean, I would Yeah, you don't want to make a decision if you don't see see somebody, but at the end of the day, if you if you're in that position where you don't see a player, um you know, it you're going to have to make that decision and we'll make that decision how we see best for us. >> You just want to follow up. You you mentioned all four quarterbacks. When can you talk about the like the competition? [clears throat] Are all Could any one of those four guys start week one? Is that possible? I I can't answer that. I can't answer that. If in all four quarterbacks could start week one. >> Well, certainly not at the same time, but >> Could be any one of them. >> Yeah. Yeah, exactly. >> And how how pleased were you to get Zach Harrison back? And kind of can you talk a bit about that transaction in particular considering the production he's had at the NFL level in his career? >> Yeah, I I I touched on it at the beginning. It's um those are some of the tough decisions, right? You we put three claims in. Um you're you're guessing uh what the other 31 teams are going to do. Uh not knowing if you're going to get uh one a claim or three. We were fortunate enough to get three. Uh you go through it knowing if you get those three claims, what is what's the decision that you're going to have to make? Um and once we got that, it's like as happy as we were, it was a gut punch, too, personally just because knew that Zack was most likely going to be the the option. Um and you know, a lot of respect for Zack and what he's done. I remember going through um during the spring going back home, flying back home to see my family in Chicago. There was one time where Zack was actually coming back from Chicago and we were on the same flight together and we're talking and um we get back late. It's probably like 6:00 and you know, you get traffic and you get back up here around 7:00. So, I come straight into the office cuz I'm still living in the dorms out there right at the time. Um and so, I'm working in the office and I go down for a workout and it's like 7:30, 8:00. And who's in there? And it's Zack Harrison, right? And it shows that this is right before like OTAs and workouts. So, this is a guy that takes care of his body. He's a pro's pro. He's a great dude and knowing that we're going to have to make that decision and and move on. Um thinking there was a chance that there's a potential that he could get claimed. But um it didn't happen. And look, we got him back on practice squad this morning. Um happy to get him back. again, it gives us we've talked about it. It gives us some veteran um leadership, some veteran guys that on practice squad that have been there, done it. And now we know if in the event that we we need him, he'll be ready and we can elevate him. >> Can you guys speak to more of the bringing Todd McCombs back in and what his role will actually be as far as player development is concerned and what was the impetus for bringing him back? Todd first, great great dude and offensive lineman, right? You can't have You can't have enough offensive linemen in the building, right? Like he's he's awesome. Awesome guy to work with. He gets it. Gets people already can see why he was one of the best leaders for this organization. We're going to really rely on him in terms of the relationships that he builds, but really to help, you know, the development piece along with Jeff and I can let Jeff speak a little bit more about that as well. >> Yeah, no. I think um having Todd in here is awesome. I think same things Ian has said. He's a natural fitting in, building relationships. But one of the biggest things we're really focused on and and Todd in fact we just were meeting maybe 15, 20 minutes ago, um is our development and our development program. And we're going to be intentional about that and the development of our players and use all the resources that we have because at the end of the day if we don't pour into these guys, we bring them in the building, we want them to be the best players and the best people that they can be. So, Todd's going to be a huge part of that. >> All right. Thank you everybody. >> We'll follow up with one one question on uh James Pierce and the off the plan I guess his people have to maintain to you know, while he's away from the team. league rules we can't have contact with with James. We all know that. He's suspended for eight weeks until um after week five. So, um feel really good with the plan that we've given James for him to to do away from the building um and then we'll have a plan for when he is able to come back in the building based off league rules. Thank you guys. >> Appreciate it. >> Thank you guys.

title: D'Andre Swift, Clark Phillips III believe 'best days are ahead' | Press Conference
text: Yeah, Andre Ben said that he thinks you're poised for a really big year. Do you um feel the same way? And you know, you've had a really great camp. How are you feeling heading into this year as opposed to previous years? >> Uh I feel good. Feel like I had a complete camp. Um Feel like one of my better camps as far as taking days, being consistent, and things like that. Um Yeah, just ready for uh week one. >> In your eyes, what are the reasons this running game is fun to be part of? >> Reasons it's fun to be part of? Uh a lot of answers for that. First of all, the O-line up front. Ben and how he sees the run game and the way he calls it, the detail that's in place with the plays, and how it's being blocked, the angles, and things like that. Um how he calls it throughout the game as well. Uh And the variety of runs we have. It's a lot of stuff. Um a lot of answers to that question. >> What makes it special within a game calling it? >> What makes it special? >> Ben, when you say him calling it within a game. >> If he's um if we're having success early on with some, he might stick with that. But then he throws little wrinkles in there to keep defense on his toes and So defense can't really get a beat on what we're doing and how we're doing it. And then we make things look similar. So uh he does a great job of calling it throughout the game. >> How was uh Kyle >> Did you do anything coming into this camp? You said it was one of your better camps. Consistency standpoint, from like off season work, body work. Did you do anything differently? >> Nah, not necessarily. I always train hard and was always a hard worker and things like that when I'm away from the team. Um but just having a better sense of the offense, second year going into it, knowing what Ben wants to see from me, and things like that. So me being very critical of little stuff. Um Landmarks, aiming points, and things like that. Then I can go out there and play fast and uh do what I need to do. >> How was Kyle and not being out there? What conversations were you having with him to kind of help him >> He's doing good. He's in good spirits. I talk to him every day. Uh he's out there working. Um I watched him work running uh today. Look good to me. Um, he's in good spirits but just telling him take one day at a time. Like nobody rushing him. He'll come back when he ready. >> How the last couple weeks since he's been out, it seems like Roshan really >> Yeah. >> taking advantage of an opportunity. How [clears throat] did you see How did you see him do that to make the roster? >> Uh, I've always been a big fan of Ro. Um, he did a great job of just making the most of his opportunities. And I feel like that's what everybody in the running back room has done. Anybody gets an opportunity. Um, Seven included. Um, but Roshan Ro- Ro- he's very critical of himself. So I trained with him in the off season. So we had conversations and things like that. But he's done a great job all off season though making his opportunities count. Not even just on offense, on special teams too. >> What have you learned about him so far? >> What have I learned about him? Uh, we came out the same year. So I I've known him for a while. Um, he's explosive, man. He uh he got that uh one play mentality where he can score from any point on the field any moment. Um, great guy to be around too. Hard worker. Yeah, big fan of his. >> Fans have really noticed a more serious version of Caleb Williams this year. How have you seen that kind of throughout practices? Just the way he owns the offense and holds everyone else accountable. >> Kind of the same thing as been said to piggyback off of his leadership continues to grow. And I see it more the more I'm around him. Um, his second year in the system he Everybody knows what we need to do coming off of last year. Self-scout with everything. And um, you could tell he's doing a great job of just going into that leadership role. And it's And it's effortless for him. Yeah, cuz I see that. >> When the season ended last year, how long did it take you to kind of turn the page and say, "Okay, maybe we can get back there and do even more this year." >> How long did it take me? >> Does it sit with you for a while in the off season or not? >> I'm always looking forward to the next thing. Like season over with, we ain't make it the way we wanted to make it. So I look in the mirror, how can I be better to um, kind of help out the team in uh, any way possible. You know what I mean? That's my doing my own self-scout in the off season, watching film and things like that, just so when opportunities come for me, I'm able to take advantage of it and put the team in the better position to succeed. >> You did that self-scout. I imagine the Eagles tape from last year was kind of what you guys are striving to be more consistently this season. Do you Like how much does that come up or do you guys study that as sort of what you wanted to look like more consistently? >> So, like that game in particular? >> Um it don't really come up too much. That was one of the games where we was kind of clicking from start to finish, especially in the run game. Um Those Those are more of the clips that you might see on like explosive runs and things like that, being able to make things happen, but it don't come up as often as you think it would. >> Andre, a few weeks ago Press said that efficiency isn't something you guys ever talk about in the run game. >> Mhm. >> How do you describe the mindset difference for you guys in that regard? >> Uh I feel like efficiency, when you talk about run game, 4 yards, 5 yards, something like that, being efficient. Staying ahead of the sticks, explosive is where we want to be. Um and I think those is 12 yards plus, and that's that's what we looking for every time. I know that's what I'm looking for anytime I touch the ball, within reason. Um staying within the scheme and things like that, but we have these players on offense, not even just the running back room, to be explosive every time we touch the ball, and that's check-downs and things like that. Um That's what we looking to do. >> One of the Titans players the other day was talking about how >> [clears throat] >> it's play-calling, too, and in that Ben can call plays on first and second down that maybe you know, in situations where maybe other wouldn't >> you know, place and have a chance to really go for something. >> And when you know, ordinarily you'd sit there and go, "Let's get 3 yards." And you get >> whatever. And how much of that explosion is the mindset of the head coach and just kind of the way he dials up plays? >> That's his mindset. He Uh when he first came in last year, he talked about his offense like we have maybe 65 to 70 bullets, and he's not wasting any not looking to waste any of them. So, whatever play call he calls, like we looking to execute it. Now, we know that it can go at any point. So, we we we'd be excited to play for him. Got like that. >> And to see him have the kind of attitude that Do you believe that he thinks every play should be a touchdown? >> As he should. With the guys he's got on his As he should. Yeah. >> Fans take such a pride in the run game. Like, what is he like when he's doing the installs himself? I know not every offense Not every head coach, especially >> Real detailed, real dialed in. cuz that's what the guy That's what it has to be. >> Um >> So, when he's up there installing uh it's just real dialed in, real detailed, and um yeah, so we be following his lead as that go. You know, it's It's rare that a head coach does that and has that type of love for the run game install. You know what I mean? So, when he's up there preaching Not preaching, up there coaching and and um things like that, we we paying attention closely. >> See how much passion he has for it in those moments when he's in the front of the room in front of you. >> 100%. And his pa- his passion for the game is second to none, and I knew that about him since I've known him. >> Caleb has wanted you guys to kind of celebrate the good things during camp. Seems like when there's touchdowns, he's in the middle of the celebrations. >> Why is that important? >> It's I feel like first First downs are hard to come by, first of all. But, um I don't think I'm not going to say we don't do a good job of it. First of all, we be tired out there. And and it take a lot to go ahead and celebrate, but like in game >> It seems like there's been like a concerted effort though to >> Yeah, yeah, yeah. We want to celebrate our guys and make sure like we are celebrating each other when those things come up, especially in practice. You going against the same guys every single day, man. But, it's it's builds that camaraderie, I would say. Yeah. >> Devin Bush called you a complete back. What does that mean to you to hear that from a teammate, [clears throat] but just in general? >> I appreciate I appreciate anything I hear positively about myself. I appreciate it, especially coming from my peers, my teammates. But, um he's made me Him and TJ made me better this camp. It's going against some guys every single day, especially him. His uh his speed and things like that, sideline to sideline speed is something that shows up every single day. It's going to make us better defensively, but now I appreciate that. >> You've been doing this for a while at this point, just based on kind of going off of that question. And the off season that you had, the success you've had thus far, do you still believe your best playing days are ahead of you? >> 100%. I feel like I'm just getting started, if you ask me, but I do feel like that. >> What was your reaction to the uh news about the trade? >> Um honestly, excitement, you know? I was excited to, you know, get in a new building with new guys and you know, learn uh new regime new scheme new regime and you know, uh obviously coming to a place with familiar faces, so it was exciting. >> What has the process been like for you getting used to EA and all the position coaches? >> It's been good, you know? Like biggest thing is just, you know, kind of on boarding right now, so just trying to learn everything um from new faces to new calls, new defense, so um just yeah, just learning, man. >> Can you give some insight into the upheaval that it is to spend all off season, all training camp in one place, in one system and then >> right before the season you're switching? >> Um it's definitely a unique thing, um but I'll say like, being the type of guy I am, feel like I'm prepared for it, you know, obviously body wise, I feel good about it. Um and like I said, I'm just excited to be here, man, like really am, just excited to learn this new defense and you know, get going with the guys and help you guys win this year. >> Was this something you were expecting as a possibility? >> Um I mean, I think as a player in this league, you always have to keep your mind open to, you know, anything, um but I'll say probably not initially, but like as soon as we got the call, it was like, oh, let's go, you know, AJ unless you know, it's like, let's go play. Oh, I'm going over here with Jaylen, I'm going over there with, you know, Hicks and you know, Elijah and all these guys and you know, obviously there's familiarity. I played with Nelson my rookie year, um so obviously he knows and he was with uh DA, so it's I was excited about that. >> When was it you knew Jamal you were going to play with him? >> Mhm. In college, right? >> Just missed him. So like I was early enrolled, so I was getting in like January, late December, and he was leaving cuz he didn't play in the the last bowl game. Um, so it was like I was pulling up and he was dipping, so I like to say he passed the torch, you know? Like >> What's the level of you kept in touch with him though like >> Oh yeah. >> [snorts] >> We probably talked at least once every every year, so you know, um he's always catching up and I'm always asking him questions like my rookie year I had a lot of questions for him like what's this and what's that and how to do this and so he's been someone that I lean on, you know? >> DA minute sound like they may see you maybe play the slot a little bit um kind of once you get settled. Uh what's the challenge of that for you and uh did you do it what a little bit a couple years ago in in Atlanta? >> Yeah, played it in college, uh played it a little bit in the in the league. Um I feel like I'm excited for, you know, whatever I got to do. I just honestly want to help this team win and so uh wherever that is, whether that's outside, whether it's inside, I'm ready to go. >> When you're learning a new defense even if it's a little similar to the one you had before, uh is it easier to focus on one position or do you just learn both at the same time and >> Um, in this case, [clears throat] you know, learning learning both at the same time, you know? Good thing is like you said, uh there's some familiarity with this defense, so I'm just excited, you know, like trying to you know, obviously got a you know, a few days, what is it? 13 days until game one, so you know, trying to put as much on my plate as possible right now and make sure I know everything about this defense. >> It's closer to 11. >> 13, okay, 11. I was wrong. In these last couple of days as you guys know I've been on a night >> [laughter] >> What are the challenges you see to the slot? Like what do you have to be on guard for? >> Um, obviously, you know, guys got a two-way go. You're not able to use the sideline as much as your friend. Um uh and then you know, you're different you're dealing with different body types a lot of the times too, I feel like in the slot, so that's something that um um obviously comes up, so. >> Body types are more rare. >> Um more slot guys, uh I feel like in most situations, and obviously they'll bring in different body types in the slot, so. >> When you got to Utah, I mean, since you said passing the torch, like were were they showing you film of Jaylon? Like was that >> Without a doubt. >> Yeah, without a doubt. Now, it was like he was uh he was somebody that I definitely watched. Obviously would have been in the same defense that I was coming into. It was easy to watch that film with the same calls, the same players. It was like, "Okay, this is where you fit. This is what you're going to do." and you know, go make plays, and we did that. >> So, what what are your conversations been like with him since you got here? >> Um honestly, help me with the defense. I mean, after practice just today we were talking about just the nuances and you know, the fine things in the defense that um I need to be aware of from the inside perspective, from the outside perspective, and um how we fit and all those different things. >> Did you happen to get a rep yesterday or today against Loveman? >> Um I'm not sure. >> What have been your first impressions about Johnson as a head coach? >> Love him. You know, uh great coach. I'm excited to play for him. >> Interesting. Uh I know you haven't been around uh long, but you're if you have any initial uh impressions of some of the personalities in your room, like Xavier Woods or Malik? >> Yeah. Uh so far it's been all good. You know, these guys have welcomed me with open arms. Uh I'm excited to get them know get to know them more. Um I obviously a lot of them I'm meeting for the first time. Actually had the pleasure meeting uh Reek uh Tariq uh at the combine, so some years ago, so I was a lot of guys I already knew knew Hicks, uh knew Jaylon. Um knew a few other guys, but you know, now it's like, "Okay, now we're on the same team. Let's let's get to know each other better." >> Couple more. >> Based on that a little bit, how do you want the Chicago area to get to know you as the player and and person you are? >> I I you know, moments like this, you know, asking questions, obviously. And um you know, obviously guys will get to know me on the field, so uh but yeah, just yeah. Questions and I'm an open book. >> What's uh what's your history in on special teams in the in the league so far? Like what where do you fit in? What do you feel like you're good at? >> No, I can play gunner, um jammer on punt return. I mean, pretty much I played most positions, I feel like, especially on the outside. Um you talk about kickoff, um uh R1, all of that stuff, so I'm willing to play whatever, you know, they're willing to put me at.

title: Dennis Allen on defense's progress throughout training camp | Press Conference
text: Yeah, look, I think it's I think it's been a good camp for us. I think we've we've we've progressed a lot. Um there's still you know, a lot of things that we have to continue to work to improve on, which we'll do. You know, >> [snorts] >> that's always going to be the case. Uh but I'm I'm pleased with the with the progress that we've made. Um and now, you know, here in the next few days we'll start turning our attention to uh Carolina. We got a couple more practices that are really focused on ourselves uh today and tomorrow and then we'll start turning our attention to Carolina. >> You guys have talked about how intrigued you were by Vandenburg's athleticism. >> Yeah. I >> How long did it take before you before you saw kind of how you could apply that in the NFL? Cuz is that the question of he's got all these skills, can he can he play? >> Um yeah, and I think there was just you know, there was a couple of things. Uh the number one thing was just how he came out of his hips when he was striking blocks uh and being able to get his head up um was probably the biggest and still probably the biggest thing that we've got to continue to work on with him. Um because uh he's got all the he's got all the skill set. Um he's got the physicality, he's got the effort. Um you know, I think probably uh you know, coming up with a finishing move, whether that be in the run game, you know, to be able to strike blocks and then at the at the end of the day be able to disengage and shed, get off the block and make the play uh or in the passing game, you know, the finishing move to try to get to the quarterback. I think those are all things, as they are with a lot of young guys, uh things that he's got to uh, got to improve on and and um, you know, I think a lot of times with defensive linemen, um, you can have a lot of hidden production. You know, uh, where you're just so disruptive that you create opportunities for, uh, other players. And And that's probably where he's at right now. Um, and and hopefully, uh, you know, we can continue to work with him and and and develop some of those finishing moves where not only does it does he have disruption, but he also has production. >> And it's connected connected with that, but maybe perhaps broader with Dexter's exit over the weekend. Where is your confidence rooted in the group you have at defensive >> Yeah, I feel really confident with who who we have on the defensive line. I I think, uh, uh, the the style that we want to play, I think we've got guys that, you know, can do the things that we want to do and and, um, you know, I felt like all along, I felt like that was probably our deepest position group. Um, you know, I felt like we had a lot of guys that are NFL caliber caliber football players. Um, and, uh, and so, and you can't keep all of them, you know, so, uh, but we feel good about where we're at. >> What's your thumbnail on Street and what he brings to what you want to [clears throat] do defensively? >> Yeah, I quite honestly, I think he was the most productive tackle we had, uh, throughout the course of training camp. Um, you know, he's got the he's got the the the suddenness and the explosiveness, uh, off the ball that we're looking for to create penetration and, uh, disrupt the line of scrimmage. Um, and and and he's he's really taken to the things that, you know, uh, Jeremy, Bill, Zach, all those guys are are coaching and how how we want to play that position. Um, and, uh, and I I think he's been productive throughout the course of training camp and you know, hopefully we'll be able to continue that. >> Where does Jaden fit in that mix? Is he starting to show similar things as Van Den Berg? >> Yeah, I I think um, you know, both of you know, we made a concerted effort uh, this off season that the guys that we bring into the building here, you know, you wanted to see um, their football character come out on tape. And so you wanted to see guys that that played hard and they played physical and they had great effort to the ball and all those things are things that that they have. Um, and when you're when you're smart, um, and you're willing to freaking work, um, then you're going to you're going to improve and you're going to get better. So there was a skill set with him that we liked. Um, and uh, and I continue to see him developing but the thing that that uh, get gets you the most excited, um, is just how hard he plays. and and look, I effort's a effort's a talent. And um, and and he's got that. >> As an extension of that, how did you see the football character of Dylan start to come out as he's going against Colson, he's going against Cole, he's he's dealing with a lot of talented players every single day. >> Yeah, um, uh, he's another guy that, you know, he comes into work every single day, he works his tail off. Um, he's 100 miles an hour all the time on the practice field. Um, and so and he's smart. So if you have those characteristics and you're willing to work like he is, he's going to continue to improve. As with all of these young guys, you know, every day's a new day. You're going to see something each and every day that's um that you you hadn't seen yet, you know, and uh the key is is can you learn from those experiences um and put that back in your memory bank um so that the next time you see a similar formation, a similar stem, a similar uh you know, motion, whatever the case may be that that you know, you you kind of start to develop that library in in in your brain that allows you to recall uh and then now you're starting to anticipate more than react. >> Brian said that the trade the Dexter trade was about timing and fit. How do the defensive tackles that you opted to go with fit better into your defense than maybe >> Yeah, look look, I mean, I think we we we had a we had a a group of defensive tackles that I all thought were uh were capable of being on our 53-man roster. Um every single one of them. Um and yet I think there's uh you know, a couple of young guys that we feel really good about about, you know, trying to develop uh that I think um you know, could be the future of what we're trying to do inside. >> Did the joint practices tell you or give you more clarity about safety and the goal between Cam, Xavier, and Malik, and then where does Clark Phillips fit in all that? well, the last part of the question, I can't really necessarily answer that part of the question yet because um he's been out there for one practice and that was a special teams emphasis practice. So, I can't really speak to that other than what I saw on tape was um you know, a guy that looked to me like he had some some football savvy uh and some football intelligence. Um actually the majority of the tape we saw, uh, he played a little bit more outside. Um, and yet I see him fitting into that nickel mix a little bit and we'll see how quickly does he pick everything up. and uh, and then kind of go from there. But, you know, we're certainly very early in the evaluation process there. Um, I do think that, you know, with the course of training camp, not just the joint practices or whatever the case may be, I think the pictures uh, becoming more and more clear to us in terms of what guys can do and and where they're going to fit within within the scheme and um, we probably won't go into all that stuff here. We'll we'll kind of wait till we get to the Carolina game and figure out what we're going to do there. >> Hey, you go back to to Dylan real quick. When he cuts off that the deep pass into the end zone and that play he sees the game, is that a good example of the speed, the range and maybe the the instincts that you guys were looking for with with his selection? >> Um, what do you think? Yeah, I mean, yeah, it was uh, it was it was good to see. Um, you know, and that's that's a skill set that I think he has. Uh, that range was something that, you know, showed up on tape. Uh, at Purdue it showed up at Oregon. You know, that that that was something that we always felt like he uh, he could do. So, I think when you have an eraser back there, uh, in the middle of the field that, you know, can cover a lot of ground, um, you know, that presents some challenges and it allows the outside pieces to be a little bit more aggressive if they know that there's somebody back there in the middle of the field that's got the range to, you know, kind of protect them over the top a little bit. >> Three more Pat, Courtney, Dan. >> Oh, I get to go first. >> With in that order? >> In that order? With Cam Lewis, if he played safety and would have to move into the slot on passing downs, is that more complicated than if he played or then if you had to just bring on a new slot corner? Is is that just from a >> Uh well the the answer is yes and yet well, look it's easier when you can just go and play one position and that's the only thing that you do. Right? And and you get all your reps at that one position. Uh the the the progress gets accelerated tremendously when that's the only thing that you do. Uh and yet when you're a veteran player that's played in this league, uh that's played multiple positions in this league, I don't look at it as a a major challenge. >> What do you envision for Kroma as far as how he can get onto the active the game day roster and what kind of role he could have? >> Well, look, I think um what I saw out of him, you know, in the preseason was a guy that played with uh tremendous effort. He's another guy that really took to the coaching and how we wanted to play the defensive line position. Um and so therefore now you've seen him get better. But he's also another guy that plays with tremendous effort. Um so I think look, special teams will be a factor. Um how are all these other players playing will be a factor. Um you know, so as as what it will be with whoever else you want to talk about, you know, Dio or um Booker you know, Hardy like I I I feel like um we've got guys that are deserving of spots. and yet there's only so many guys that you can, you know, bring on game day. But, throughout the course of the season, as um you know, injuries occur, whatever the case may be, you know, all of these guys, we got 69 guys on our roster, all of them at some point time, uh we're going to have to count on to go in there and and play and perform, um you know, at a at an optimal level. >> Just a quick follow-up on that.
