You mentioned the coaching aspect. In the spring, you said that the pass rush would be better because it would be coached better. How do you feel you and your coaches did at achieving that feat? >> Great. >> [laughter] >> Um no, listen, I I think it's still, you know, a work in progress, um but I do think that I've I've seen improvement, um you know, if you want to go back and look at the games, uh typically, to affect the quarterback with a rush, unless you're, you know, a Myles Garrett, you know, or um you know, Von Miller back in the day, it's really right at about 3.1 seconds is where you need to be affecting the quarterback. Um prior to that, you've got to affect the quarterback with your coverage, meaning you got to get him to have to go to his second or third read. and so if the ball's getting out in 2.5 seconds, statistically, you're not going to see, you know, a lot of sacks, a lot of hurries, a lot of hits. Sacks, hurries, and hits need to come, um when the quarterback has to reset, and that typically is going to be, you know, three to 3.2 seconds. Um I felt like when the quarterback had to go to his second or third read, I felt like more consistently, we we were able to to to affect him. >> And this this past month was your first extended up close look at Jaylon Johnson healthy. What did you see? >> Yeah, I I more specifically the last 2 weeks uh you know, when you talk about really the the the joint practice against Cincinnati um his mindset going into the joint practice versus Tennessee um I've seen a guy that's really kind of taken a a step forward. um I think he himself uh probably feels more like himself. um And and I've been I've been really pleased with what I've seen out of him uh in particular over the course of the last 2 weeks. I think his leadership um has started to you know, kind of come to the forefront a little bit. um A- and it that's needed. You know, we need him to play at a very high level um for us to be successful. And um I think he I think he understands that. I think he accepts that challenge. I think he's looking forward to it. All right. Thanks, guys.

title: Ben Johnson shares insights on Caleb Williams, Rome Odunze | Press Conference
text: Hey. >> All right. Um, I'll start [snorts] off by just saying a a thank you to Ryan and his crew. I thought they they did a phenomenal job really ever since we got back from uh from Tennessee there. They they grinded. Um they're going through tape, guys that were coming available, getting cut. Of course, that process had started for them a few weeks prior, but um yeah, I was really really excited to see how they handled I thought they did a great job. Coaches were really pleased with uh the communication that went on and and uh you know, we're still tinkering the the final little bit of our roster right now, but I I think we got a really good core here that uh we'll start this season with. Um with that being said, we're still we're still in week zero. Um just told the guys this morning that these next three days are big for us. Uh it's still about us really. We're not thinking about week one yet. Um we're all about us. So, we'll have a good special teams practice today. We'll have some situational work tomorrow and then uh we'll get after it a little bit with some pads on on Thursday. I'll go ahead and open it up from there. >> Can you uh give us an update on some of the injury statuses of guys like Jaylen Johnson, Tyreek Stevenson, and Kungai? >> Uh yeah, Kyle's Kyle's week to week. Uh and then Jaylen and Tyreek are more dayto-day. And where are you in terms of your uh satisfaction with how the left tackle situation has settled at this? >> Yeah. Uh I think I think we we're going to be good to go for week one. Um you know, we'll talk a little bit more as a staff just to make sure we're all aligned. But uh but yeah, I think we're going to we're going to be in good shape. We're going to be able to operate as an offense. Um and I think we'll be able to score points. It's going to take all 11 of those guys out there in order to get that done. >> Do you think Luther will practice? >> Yeah. And with uh with Rome being able to kind of look at the full training camp, what did you like about his performance this summer? >> Rome. Yeah. Uh Mr. Consistency, you know, there's um this level of I know the dialogue about his foot and all that and yet I mean you didn't see any any setback from that regard. I thought he looked completely healthy. Um, you know, I I showed a highlight of him to the team just the other day, uh, cracking one of the safeties in the joint practice and just how that I mean, that inspires me to not want to get him the football, but I I need to get him the football when I see things like that. And so, um, he's doing all the little things, the things that maybe other people don't notice and, uh, the coaching staff is very appreciative of because it's going to help us win games. And so, he's going to be a key cog of what we do. Where have you seen Caleb's focus on the immediate on the day-to-day rather than getting ahead of himself? >> Yeah. Yeah. I I've seen a very composed uh person every time he steps into the building. This guy um [snorts] you know might have had a little bit of goofy to him a year ago. when I use that that term uh with love and and now you just see a more serious player and intent every time I'm around him and and I think his teammates feel that as well. Um you know, he's getting to the practice field early. He's making sure he his part is taken care of. He's he's warmed up. He's ready to go. He's staying after with the guys after practice. I think you guys see that on a regular basis. Um and so he's taken a lot of pride in in his approach right now. and it it trickles down to everybody around him. Um I think it's a great thing and so I think he continues to grow up and he's going to be a huge leader for us this year. >> How do you define goofy and uh in that case in that context? I'm serious. >> Yeah. No, I mean I you guys >> I I say that lovingly and it's it's like >> No, it's just when when we step on the grass, you can kind of just see it like he's locked in. He's got his blinders on and he's he's only concerned about doing his job at a high level. And uh there there were some times where maybe a year ago you get sidetracked or distracted a little bit and and yet this year that has not been the case. This guy is he's serious about about his approach, his job, and making sure he's taking his game to the next level. >> How does that translate to everybody else? Because Ryan was saying he really noticed that that was a difference this year. Everybody was really locked in. >> Yeah, I Yeah, I don't know why that's the case. I think it's a credit to the type of guys that Ryan's brought into the building. Um, I think we've got some some guys that uh they want to get after it, you know, they they want to work hard. They want to, you know, eventually get the results. We got to earn those results. Um, but the the process in terms of how we're going about our business, like they they are completely devoted to and I think the coaching staff is is held a high standard. I think those guys have answered the the the call every step of the way. You know, I was talking with the coaching staff just yesterday. I I don't know that we've had really a practice or a blimp through training camp where you're really, man, I'm really disappointed. I I don't think we we got better today. And yeah, we've had some some tough ones and you know, the pre- snap penalties or this or that um that that you don't like, but at the same time, like the whole group has brought an intent to get better and um you know, I think that that goes a long way. It's a maturity of the group. We we put up today, you know, congrats to the 70 guys that we had in the room today. And uh we had 21, I believe, with seven years or more of experience, which is which is huge. And I think you feel that with our crew. Um they know what good football looks like, and probably a lot of them, they they know that who knows how many more years they have uh before they can make make a significant impact. And so um you know, the time is now. Then >> with everything you just said about Caleb, is he growing like vocally more as a leader? Like, do you hear his voice more on the practice field amongst his teammates? >> Yeah, I think so. You know, he's uh I think he's getting to the point now when when things aren't right, like he gets pissed off, which which I think that's what the best ones do. Um he's really hard on himself first and foremost, and so he gets he gets upset with himself. Um but now it's to the point where if we if we're that close and somebody didn't get his depth or ran the wrong number of steps or whatever that is, he's not afraid to let them know. And uh I think he's earned that right with with how he's played over the last year and a half. >> That Ryan Ryan mentioned this morning that he's seen an exuberance in this camp from Caleb that that maybe maybe wasn't present a year ago as he's figuring everything out. What have you observed from just sort of that animated nature when he makes a big play and and he's just into it. >> Yeah. No, I I he's 100% right. There's a um [snorts] there's an excitement with him when he plays football and I I felt that from the first day I was in the building. He just he loves this game. He wants to be great. We know that. And then now he's getting to the point where that excitement is is really radiating outside and and the people around him feel that. Um I think that also goes with the comfort level. He knows what he's doing. Um he's executing at a at a much higher clip than than he ever has and I think it's going to continue to grow and and he's going to continue to elevate everyone around him, coaches included. I know that your your defense goes up against Coloulston every day and I'm sure you know they have their troubles with them but they see it every day so they're probably used to it. What was it like watching Coloulston in those joint practices against two defenses that might not have had quite the experience with him that you guys do? >> Yeah. No, he's he's been Mr. Steady, much like Rome. Um the these guys are really phenomenal athletes and uh I think he's a he's a really hard matchup for really any safety in this league, any linebacker in this league that wants to cover him a man. Um that's a tough ask. Uh he's too big for these nickels to cover if if that that's the matchup that ends up dictating itself. And so um no, I'm really pleased with where he's at. Um I can't say necessarily anything from those two practices that that stands out, but no, he's he's a huge huge asset for us. >> You mentioned still being you mentioned still being focused on yourselves as opposed to Carolina this week. So what do you want to accomplish these three days before you guys give the guys the weekend off before we >> Yeah, I mean I just go back. It's going to be special teams today. uh we're going to get better in that phase tomorrow. We're going to hammer home a lot of our situational work that maybe we have not been able to get full speed yet. We've been able to get in walkthroughs. Um so that'll be huge. Shoot, I look back to game one last year. We had a number of situational plays pop up in that game that we didn't execute at a high enough level. And so we're going to make sure we don't fall in that same trap again this year. Um, and then it's for the guys that did not play in the preseason game against uh Tennessee there. You know, they they were in pads on Thursday. They won't be in pads again till next Tuesday. And so we needed another padded practice in between. So that's why that Thursday practice this week is going to be so critical to making sure everything we built up to this point, stamina, endurance, pad level, fundamentals, technique, that we don't we don't lose that as they get some time off this weekend. And you had a number of rookies last year stepping into key roles. You got some rookies that are making an impression on you so far, [clears throat] moving toward key roles. What's the common theme of the players that you've been a part of, identifying and evaluating that's allowed them to to step in and be key parts for you guys here? >> Well, yeah, I think it goes back to Ryan and and his crew in the selection process. The the character um you know, that that really is what stands out the most. We have guys that love football. Uh they they are smart individuals. I think, you know, we we've got a number of undrafted free agents that that ended up making the team this year. I think we had four. That might be the most in the NFL. And uh that's a credit to them. That's a credit to Ryan and his staff for identifying those players. And then of course we feel really strongly about the guys that we selected in the draft as well. Um but we're prioritizing football character and and I think uh I think we've seen that throughout that draft class. >> Last two, Kevin and Dan. >> And one of those undrafted rookies, Jaden Loving. what allowed him to grow to a point where he can he can make this roster. Yeah, I mean I think we we talk about uh the way that we're coaching the defensive line play this year and when you see some young guys come in whether it's Vayenberg Loving um jam at the DN spot when you see them do their best to apply that technique and you see them have results I think I think it's a beautiful thing and so he's one of those guys that you know he's he's young he's impressionable he's trying to do everything the coaching staff asks and you see him have success and results from it. Um, and I think it's it's exciting. He he's a he's a guy that comes around the building, he's got a smile on his face. I don't think I've ever seen him in a bad mood. Um, and yet when he hits the grass, I mean, he he flips a switch and and he he's a darn good defensive player. And so I we think he's got a chance to really grow and develop. And hopefully uh each week we continue to see him ascend to where he's going to be able to to be a productive player for us. And as you get closer uh to gameweek planning and you've got a a greater familiarity of what you guys are good at offensively, where are you at personally with your urges and your comfort to expand creatively, innovatively with everything that you guys can do? >> Yeah, I was just talking with uh Press Taylor about that and I think we're going to we're going to be able to be a lot more organized than what we were. I think there was an element of uh a lot of people in the building a year ago trying to figure things out where they and now we've defined roles and everyone knows where they stand where they can contribute and I think it's going to allow us to be a lot more efficient in our process. Um and to your point the creativity the that's those are things that we want to acknowledge we want to incorporate and and I think we have a number of really smart guys on staff that it's going to come to fruition for us. >> Awesome. Thank you. >> Thank you. for you.

title: Tetairoa McMillan receives PFWA ROY award, speaks on Panthers offense and second-year growth
text: get started. >> Hey yo, >> on behalf of the Professional Football Writers of America, which is the official professional organization and voice for journalists who cover the NFL, I would like to present you with the 2025 Rookie of the Year and offensive Rookie of the Year award. You are the first player in Carolina history to be selected as PFWA's Rookie of the Year. And you are the second Panthers player in the PFWA's offensive rookie of the year uh to win the offensive rookie of the year joining quarterback Cam Newton who won it in 2011. So congratulations. >> I appreciate you. >> You have a speech. >> So So this is voted by you guys? >> Yes. And and people for the league as a whole. >> Damn. Y'all must really like me. [laughter] I like that. No, but you know, it's an honor obviously, you know, just blessed, but um obviously y'all y'all see some in me that a lot of people don't see. So, just want to thank everybody just for voting me. >> What have you done awards? >> I don't I don't know. >> Did you put it into that closet that you told your mom was just for shoes? >> You said what? >> The room that you had designated for just shoes. Have you repurposed that to kind of accommodate some of these awards that you picked? >> No, no, my awards is in storage. >> I just kind of put them away. >> Talk talk us talk us through that. I mean, I'm sure what was your reaction during awards season, if you will, and then this idea that you're kind of putting them away for now. >> Uh, shoot. I mean, honestly, my mom's the one that likes to put the awards up in the house and stuff like that, but I don't really really like having stuff of mine around the house, like pictures and stuff like that. I don't know, just me, I guess. But, um, no, all the awards is cool. You know, I've feel like I've won a been able to been fortunate enough to win a lot of awards in my lifetime. So, um, what's another one, I guess. [laughter] >> Like post football, do you get to enjoy them like after your career? No, I mean most of the time when they go in the stores, I don't really open it up unless I got to move or something. >> Team Mac, how is camp gone for you, would you say? >> Uh, no. Camp has has been good. Um, you know, the offense looks night and day different just from last year. Just obviously the pieces, um, you know, new play caller, you know, things things are going really smooth right now. >> Can you expound on that part? The night and day difference. How would you say what would you say the students? >> Uh I just for the most part, you know, a lot more people are stepping up. You know, there we have a lot of dudes that can uh do a bunch of different things and are able to make plays wherever. You know, we got a a deep tight end room, running back room, receiver room, obviously. Um so, everybody can make plays no matter who it is. >> T-Mac, last year you ran about 16% of your your routes from the slot. Um, I'm curious, what do you like about running running those routes from from the inside? And also, how does it free you up to maybe kind of move around in this offense? >> Yeah, I mean, like like you just said, it just opens up the offense. Um, you know, allows me to play decoy sometimes. It allows me to get open. Um, allows everybody just the offense just to flow easily. Um, and you know, I I was always a big fan, you know, just all the years that I played football, just to be able to be versatile, play inside, play outside, and just um, just expand the offense in that way. >> Dave brought up the added strength and and added muscle. Does that help going across the middle at all for you, or is that just kind of more of a just an overall health thing? >> Uh, I mean, I don't really feel like it helps. just maybe take less hits on my body, I guess. >> Was it hard to keep your weight up during camp? Just as hot as it was? Like, did you have to be real intentional with it? >> You're talking about this year? >> Yeah, this summer. >> Surprisingly not. It was probably the easiest training camp I've ever had as far as maintaining my weight. >> Why What do you chalk that up to? Were you being intentional with an extra meal or >> uh honestly I can't even tell you, man. Well, I I try to do the same like program every single trainer camp every single year. Some year some years it works, some years it doesn't. This year just happened to be one of the years at work. >> Now that you're officially a vet and you're second year vet, um >> hello. Say that again. [laughter] Like you talked about how surprisingly it wasn't hard for you to keep your your weight up. Were there any other things that surprised you that that were surprisingly easier for you this second go round than they were last year? >> Uh I mean not necessarily. I mean obviously anything with time, you know, you just gain more comfortability uh chemistry with Bryce, you know, comfortable with the offense, just how things work, how the league works for that matter. Um, so just being able to be a lot more confident and, you know, just a lot more comfortable just make things that much easier. >> It's pretty hot out here. Are you pretty stoked about not having to ride uh getting the cart rides to to practice now? >> Yeah, that's that's that's one of the joys right there, man. Going back to going back to Bash's question too, like last year Mike and JC came into training camp and kind of were told like make team work for everything and gave it to you. This year it seems like you kind of gave it back to them a good bit, especially you and Mike. Like how nice was it to be able to push back on them a little bit and what has that rivalry become and how helpful is that just to prepare you for the season? >> I mean, yeah. I mean, I you know, I try my best every single day versus them. I mean, in my opinion, that's the best quarterback duo in the in the league. And I mean, just going off of last year, you know, the stats speak for itself. Just what they're what they were able to accomplish, what they were able to do for this team, this defense. Um, but you know, like just going up against them every day just makes me that much better. Um, and I hope it makes them that much better, too, you know. So, um, you know, I'm really grateful for them and just, you know, the time and effort that they put in just to make sure not just me, but everybody on offense is is on go and make sure that everybody is on top of their game and keeps everybody on their P's and Q's. So, um, you know, shout out to them. >> Teammate, what are your goals this year, >> man? That's an easy one. That's be able to win a playoff game. That's the main goal for sure. Do you fold personal goals into that or do you just kind of let them come? >> Yeah, I mean, you know, whatever happens happens. You know, I just hope that uh well, main thing just to be able to come out the season healthy. That's obviously number one. But just as far as um stats and stuff like that, I don't really care too much. Just as long as, you know, we win games. When every when somebody when we win games, everybody's happy and when one person wins, we all win. I know you just said that you don't really care about stats, but if you literally repeat your production from last year and have the same stat line, you'll be one of five players in NFL history to do that. What does that say about what you did your rookie year, but also what you have to build off of? Um, I mean I mean that that's a cool stat by the way, but you know I feel like No, I feel like at the end of the day, you know, you're not able to achieve those stats if you're not healthy. And I feel like that's a lot of you know, everybody say they got sophomore slumps and you know, people get hurt and stuff like that. So, you know, the main thing to be able to achieve those things just to be healthy and you know, that's all I can wish for. Do you talk to anyone like a Steve Smith or anyone else about what you just referenced, the so-called sophomore slumps? >> No, I I don't really like to think too much about it. You know, whatever happens happens. I don't really believe in that sophomore slump stuff. You know, you can have a slump at any moment in your career. So, uh, you know, I try not to dig too deep into that one. >> You mentioned want to win a playoff game. How how long did that loss to the Rams last year here in the playoffs stick with you? I >> mean, feel like I ain't never left. I feel like it's still here. And I I think I can speak for the rest of the team when I say that as well. You know, I feel like after that game, you know, we all had that that chip on our shoulder just ready to come into, you know, the 2026 season. So, you know, we're looking forward to it. >> Have y'all talked about it though or you just set it behind? But it's something that you know is there that too. >> Yeah, you can you can feel it. You know, everybody just just obviously leaving that locker room, you know, every just everybody was just down. So, um feel like everybody got that that fire in them right now and just ready to go. >> Talked earlier about guys on offense, you know, stepping up. If you had to look specifically at a guy that's made big strides that you've been with the last couple of years, who would that guy be? >> That's too many people, man. There's a lot of people. There's a lot of them. Um, that's a good question. I'll probably just say Jim. You know, obviously that's one of the guys that maybe Yeah, that's the obvious answer. You know, like I feel like, you know, last year maybe you guys or a lot of people didn't really know his name. And um you know now people are kind of picking up on what he's able to accomplish and what he's able to do. So you know that that kid has a lot of talent and you know I'm wishing the best for him. >> T man Dave always talks about the passing game having a focal point and you're you're it. How did you kind of learn to adjust to the pressure that comes with that and being the guy that sort of built around? >> Uh ain't no pressure. you know, they that's what they drafted me me to be. That's what, you know, they pay me all this money to do is to just do my job and do it to the best of my ability. And whether, you know, I'm the focal point one week and whether I'm the decoy the next week, you know, as long as we um, you know, do do what we're supposed to do, I'm not worried at all. >> Over the course of last year though, did you did you notice opponents looking at you differently or treating you differently as you began the staff? >> Uh, yeah. But I feel like I notice a lot more this year just in practice first and foremost is what whatever whatever E coach E is doing over there. But um you know I'm getting a lot more u double coverages and um you know linebackers rotating my way, safeties rotating my way and um to me to me that's a great sign that just allows people to win their one-on-one matchups on the other side. So um like I said that's that's lovely to me. What are you weighing now compared to last year at this time? >> Uh, I'm about almost 20 pounds heavier than what I was last year. >> Have you noticed Have you noticed anything physically changing with that added weight? >> Yeah, for sure. I mean, in college, whenever I was heavier, I was stronger, faster. Um, and that's how I feel right now. Like last year, like I said before, I just I didn't feel like myself. I feel like I wasn't moving as good and didn't feel as powerful and now I feel like I got a lot back. >> Thanks, T. >> All right, y'all. Appreciate you. >> Congrats, man. >> We're my award, man. [music]

title: Dave Canales: 'Very optimistic' Jonathon Brooks will play Week 1 | Carolina Panthers
text: What a day. Great work. Um really competitive day today. Uh ones versus ones, nice competitive um to start it off right there, but got got some good heat, got some good work out there. Uh it was a physical practice, so um felt good about what we did today on the grass. >> With the way that you guys have handled Chuba and obviously Jonathan this week, AJ's getting a lot of run with the ones and and other groups. Uh how much do you think that can benefit him after kind of having an on-and-off year last year? >> I think across the league and you know in in history, you need all your backs. You need them all and um that's why AJ's here. You know, Trevor will come back to us at some point and then we have uh Trey Sermon on the practice squad. So, guys have got to be ready to go, you know, and they have to prepare that way. We try to warn them of that, but it becomes a reality, you know, when when you're out there and you're taking those reps. So, really valuable time for AJ. >> Darren Waller back in practice today, first time that we saw him in the 808. You said, you know, Friday that he's still not ready to take on a full workload yet. What have you seen from him today as he continues to make that progress? >> Yeah, it was good. Just backed him off a little bit yesterday. Uh let him go today. Got RVAs in. Um had a couple of nice targets out there on the field. Um made one catch, another one uh Bryce progressed to somebody else, but he looked fast. Um he looked huge. So, it was good to see his big frame out there moving around. >> Um from the standpoint of roster management, having three running backs and and Tyus obviously on the practice squad, all three of those guys have a history of injuries. How do you kind of keep that in the back of your mind while also preparing them for roles heading into the season? >> You don't really. You just go with what we have. Um attack the game plan that way. Expect all of them to prepare kind of like we talked about, you know, they just you got to stay locked in and you know, again, I just go back to our history. We love calling guys up when they when they earn that opportunity or we can use different guys in certain ways. And so, um it's good, you know, it's good pressure for the guys to feel that, to know they got to be ready to go cuz the minute your number gets called, that's an op, you know, um and we expect all the guys to be ready. >> From a scheduling or structural standpoint, like what does this week look like before the official week one? Are you starting the game plan with Chicago? What are you guys doing? >> Yeah, we've been game planning, you know, pretty much, you know, you start with your first opponents and and so we've been looking at Chicago, you know, a little bit in the off-season, um, over the summer, just kind of peeking at some of the different things and, um, introduce a couple of just concepts and things and walk-throughs throughout camp. Um, with this week we get to actually put the scout team to work, um, get it carted, get a get some live reps against different looks that we think we can see. But it's also an opportunity this week to make sure you hit some different situations, um, different parts of your offense, different parts of your defense, you know, your end of game plays, um, hitting those things. We got to end a half two-minute yesterday, today we got to end a game. Uh, Nick Scott ended the first drive with an interception on the sideline. Fantastic play, was really, you know, batted up in the air by Will Lee and then, you know, Nick's hustling over and got his feet down on the sideline to end that drill pretty quickly and, um, a nice aggressive shot by Bryce down to Metchie along the sideline. And so, um, you know, but just getting those types of situations, getting calls, different parts of third down, tomorrow we'll introduce a few more situations and make sure we're just kind of going through our inventory and covering all the things that don't always come up. Can we get our money field goal, our hurry up field goal unit out there? So we've we've repped things like that and, um, that's the benefit of having this week. >> Dave, we've heard you talk about how you challenge certain players during the off-season or give them a charge to work on something specific. Did you have a conversation like that with T-Mac this year, something specific you'd like to see him come back bigger or stronger or or anything? >> Uh, really wasn't that. It was mostly just kind of, uh, focusing in on, you know, at the line of scrimmage releases, some different techniques and and all that and, um, a lot of it was just kind of collecting information. How was this year for you now that we look back, um, Um, because I can point back to when we had him here on a 30 visit and he sat my office and I said, "What do you want this conversation to look like a year from now?" And all of a sudden you're about a year from that date. Um, and so I asked him, "How did it go? Is this what you expected?" And um, talking about that as he goes into year two and you know, he kind of was just a man on a mission to, you know, to get stronger, to be able to to fill that power in his game. Um, that really is a part of his game that that um, that needed to be addressed. You know, and he he really wanted to do that and he attacked it, you know, put on some good some good solid mass and um, he's been great at the line of scrimmage, rugged to the ball. Um, and he's still got all the same stuff. So I'm excited to see him this year. >> We we had talked to you back a month ago about maybe him seeing more reps in the slot. Yeah. How did that How do you think that went this summer and what do you Where are you leaning that way? >> And that was stuff we did last year. You know, just moving him to the three spot, this the two spot. Um, he certainly played the single a lot last year as well. Uh, just giving us that big reliable target over there and um, but as you all know, you can do things into the boundary with the single side X to help. You can cloud. You can get a safety dropping in. You can move a linebacker to kind of spy, just take a little bit of space over there. So there's things you can do, but as you move them around in different spots, it gets harder and harder to try to pair up, you know, your best coverage guys or they may have to move a corner inside and then that creates matchups other places. So um, we'll use them. We'll use them that way. We'll use them versatility. Um, be able to take advantage of how comfortable he is in the slot and then also still be able to take advantage of the one-on-one opportunities when they come to us. >> To that to that point, um, I think 16% of his routes were in the slot. Um, this the metrics aren't like there's not like a huge difference either way. But how do you think adding that weight and also kind of preparing how he gets off the line could help you make him a little bit more versatile, especially in the slot? >> Really it's just about making plays. So the the power um, that I've seen him translate is going to help help all across the board. It's going to help him when he has those singles outside, when he goes inside and he's in traffic. He's got great feel inside there for zones and very friendly for Bryce comes back to the ball. Um but all that extra strength, you know, just going to allow him to be in there, get run after catch, finish plays like like I believe he can. >> You have I think you talked about this before, but looking back at the summer and looking ahead to week one, what is it like for you not to call plays and what have you found yourself doing to occupy that time? >> Yeah, it just frees me up to connect with the guys immediately and before, you know, whether it was in practice or the game, I'm getting ready for the next play. I got to get the personnel in. Okay, we're working the call sheet, you know, look figuring out the situation and all that. But now what I get to do is see something live happen and be able to talk to a guy and talk about ball security, talk about keeping their pad level down, getting their cleats in the grass, getting set, you know, um just the little fine things fine parts of football that a head coach can do and and impact, you know, and really what I'm trying to do is just echo the messaging of our position coaches and our coordinators and make sure that it gets solidified and it all gets through to the guys and while they're busy getting ready for the next call, I may I may be able to catch a guy coming off the field and share some with them. Um communicating with the officials, that's been a great thing just being able to gather information as the play's going on. You can't do that when you're calling plays. You got to go to the next play, especially on the offensive side. Um And then I say I would say uh generally like in practice, just being able to seize little situational nuances. We're not getting enough second and one and two. So, if we run the ball on first down, it may look like it was a 3-yard gain. I'm going to make it second and two right here so we can get into that situation or let's get a short yardage up. You know what? We need a little bit more third and medium so I can kind of manufacture situations a little more fluidly with my hands free. So, um I've really enjoyed that part of it. I've enjoyed just being able to bounce around into the different rooms in all three phases and and just collect information and and just be a presence there for the other coaches. >> What's your level What's your difference level in confidence in Ryan having had him all last year compared to last year? >> Just great demeanor. Even even from last year, you know, and and some huge kicks in some critical games for us last year. And that just speaks to his character, the steadiness with which how how he goes about his work, his process, his approach, all those things. I just love having that consistency, you know, and and it's been great to just see Ryan, Sam, and JJ and that bond and that relationship. They spent a lot of time together. But to see that relationship grow and two guys, veteran guys, that are able to talk to Ryan, talk about ball, talk about life, different things like that. So, that's been really good to see. >> Hey, last one. Uh okay, I wanted to do two. >> All right. >> Uh but they're going to be really easy. One is are the players going to be off like is it sort of a bye weekend, Friday through Sunday? Is it >> Yeah, some some of the guys have work to do. Some of the guys are working on their body, doing different things all the way into Friday. Certainly the guys that are on IR, they'll be with us here working all the way through the weekend. We can take advantage of all those days. But for the rest of the group, you know, we practice tomorrow and they'll get Friday, Saturday, Sunday off. We'll come back and get our bonus Monday and get rolling. That's That's game week, you know, so the guys will have a chance to talk to family, to connect, to kind of gather their wits for what's going to be a really long season. And um I love just encouraging them and challenging them to make sure you connect with the people that are important to you in these windows cuz you need high ground for you need high ground for hard days and to me that just looks like connection. That looks like having your support system around you. >> Other thing is I know you don't want to talk specifically about injuries, but did Brooks do anything today we couldn't see? >> just, you know, again, we'll give you guys all the update on when we come back next week. I'm very optimistic he'll be available for week one. >> you, Grover. >> All right. Thank you. >> [music] [music]

title: Panthers Live Press Conference
text: When I anytime I step on the field, you know, I whatever the depth chart is, um if I'm in there at running back, I'm in the RB1 mindset. And that's always how it's going to be and always how you got to be. This game is uh it's you got to go out there and be confident in your play. Um and so that's just kind of what I try to do in every aspect of my game. >> You talked about mindset. How did that develop over the years? What was maybe kind of the moment that got you to shift into that moment? >> Man, I think I mean going back to when I started in Green Bay, um my entire career, high school, college, I'd always been that bell cow. I got drafted in the second round in Green Bay and uh they had Aaron Jones, Jamaal Williams, and you know, those guys are going into year four coming off great years. And uh you know, I'm like, man, you know, I'm a I think cuz I got drafted in the second round, this is going to be my show. And you know, the nature of the NFL, man, is you got to make the most of every opportunity you get. And I remember, you know, there were some games where I'd get seven carries or some I didn't touch the ball for two games. And uh I remember learning then, every time I'm on that field, I got to make the most of it. And so I feel like just understanding how important the opportunity is, how blessed we are to, you know, be able to play this game, how blessed I am to continue to play this game. It's one of those things where when you consistently are trying to make the most of it, you get a lot of gratitude. And that's where I feel that I am, that's where I feel like I can play with the confidence I do because, you know, football is meant to be fun. I feel like as a young guy, you know, everything's coming at you, you're trying to be perfect. And uh you know, I'm just trying to be the best that I can be. I feel like you can learn a lot in the game of football, uh just kind of how to do everything, uh even outside of here. So, yeah. >> And I was talked about how during the off season a focus for you was working on your hands and catching the ball. What was that like for you and then how do you feel like that has paid off through training camp? >> Yeah, I think uh it's one of those things as a bigger back, you know, I'm 6'2" 250. And it's one of those things that guys look at me and say, all right, this guy's only going to run downhill um and pass pro. And so that was a big knock on me when I first came in the league. And um you know, it's one of those things where it's always like been the question, but I caught the ball in Green Bay, caught the ball in Philly. Planning to catch the ball here. So it's one of those things where to be a productive back in this league and last a long time, you cannot just run the ball. You got to be able to do all three. And honestly, you got to be able to play special teams. You got to be able to do everything. And so I'm always trying to get better. So a big focus for me this year was I know and I was when I was watching tape coming in Chuba and those guys would be outside doing some stuff out of empty. So there's some route concepts I've not done yet. And you know, I'm still trying to get better and you know, get in where I fit in. >> AJ, we're talking to T-Mac today, too. And as new guy coming in here who didn't have a lot of experience with him. Wonder what your impressions were of him just having gone through camp with >> Man, wise beyond his years. You know, he like I said earlier, football is fun and he makes it that way. And he kind of has that poise where you would expect from a veteran guy. I know it's only he's going going into year two, tremendous year one. Obviously, the football piece you guys are out there every day, you see that. He's great. But my thing is like his mindset. Nothing really seems to rattle him. He goes out there and he just has fun. And it's one of those things where when I say wise beyond his years you know, I feel like you would think, you know, young guy, a lot of praise. What's going to I mean, the guy goes out there every day and goes all in and looks amazing doing it on the football field. Puts out a great product at work. So great great guy to have on our side of the ball. >> AJ, the Panthers have collected a lot of big targets for Bryce. When there's a big slot or a tight end who can run like a Y option like a wide receiver how much does that impact the box for you as a running back? And what do you see from guys like Waller and JT and even T-Mac and Koker when they're in the slot? >> Man, we we got a lot of weapons. We got a a of weapons and I think we got a really good scheme. Really just trying to get everybody utilized. But yeah, as a running back, obviously, our number one best friend is the O-line, making sure they're firing on all cylinders and supporting them. But I mean, when the box opens up, that's great. Then you throw in the play action, Bryce can run a little bit, evade some tackles. So, you know, when everything starts to complimentary football, everybody always talks about it. When you can get doing that, as a running back, you're just licking your chops cuz by the time the fourth quarter is coming, linebackers start guessing, jumping on things, and then you start to get lanes cuz they're out of position. So, you know, hopefully that's always how you draw it up on paper, that'd be great, but you know, just kind of roll with [snorts] it. >> You've been on some teams that have preseason have had high expectations. I think a lot of guys on this roster maybe aren't in that situation haven't been in that situation a lot where there are those high expectations. How do you manage those? How do you not focus on those? Cuz I think from the outside it's hard for those that aren't aren't in the locker room to say, "Hey, like, they're just going to block it." >> I like it. >> You know what I'm saying? >> Yeah, no, definitely. I mean, the two teams I've been on before it's kind of that that Super Bowl or bust mentality. I feel like Coach Canales did a great job and from his time in Seattle, obviously, had a ton of success out there. But, you know, our first goal, our first championship is winning the division. And I feel like when you kind of compartmentalize and kind of go step by step by step up that mountain, you can kind of really try to hone in on where you're going. I feel like sometimes people look at the the end result. And you know, we are so far away from talking playoffs and all that good stuff. We got to worry about week one. We got to get to week one first. This is a bonus week. So, I think it's really just about buying in and staying present, something that everybody always has to work on, myself included. But, you know, staying present and then just kind of trusting the work that we've been doing and putting in. >> You've had, obviously, major injuries in your career. What have you noticed about the resolve of Jonathan Brooks, kind of as he's coming back from two pretty serious knee injuries. >> Yeah, man. I think you know, he's he he has a lot of mental toughness. I I haven't you know, I'm not going to act like I've known him for forever, but in my three or three or so months knowing the guy, I mean, he is, you know, amazing support not just in the building but at home. Tremendous fiance. I met her once and he talks very highly of her and so, you know, I think that's a really big part. Um you really it very few people can do this game alone and football is going to test you in so many different ways more than you know, more than just on the field and it's it's a lot about resolve like you mentioned and you know, he comes to work every day with a smile on his face and you know, he's in that training room. He's doing the rehab. He's doing the weights, whatever it is to get better and so, you know, I think he's a tremendous talent. You know, I've seen him during OTAs. I remember watching him coming out of college and so, you know, you just root for him to you know, whenever it comes to put it all out there on the field and really get going. Just go ahead and take care of business. >> He catches the ball really cleanly. When when you see a guy that has both his quickness and and his catching ability, how much do you think that kind of helps in the rotation especially on third down? >> Yeah, I think like I said, you got to be able to do it all um to be an elite running back in this league and I think you know, he has a lot of those skill sets to be one of those guys. Um I think the biggest thing is just kind of you know, continually you know, be out there and just you know, sometimes it might be you might be killing them in the run game. Sometimes you might get you know, five carries for 20 yards, but you had a big screen that got a touchdown or you're a decoy this game. So, um it's able to be you know, kind of selfless and just kind of keep showing up in this league. I mean, it's a long season. Um there's a lot of trials and tribulations that are going to happen to every single team and things that are going to be moving around, but yeah, skill set wise, he's got it all. >> AJ, is this the hottest training camp you've ever been to? >> Uh hottest by far. Hottest by far. You know, I'm I'm from the north. I went to Boston College, been in Green Bay, and then Philly. So, yeah, today was a hot one. I uh we had a little break this last week and uh after that last preseason game, and I brought my son to Discovery Place Science. And we walked from the garage to the front of the thing. It was probably like not even a block. And we get into the sun, he's like, "Dad, I can't I can't walk. It's too hot." And you know, like I I know he's fine. We're about to go to AC. I'm like, "No, you're walking." And so, today I was out there, and you know, I'm just sitting there. I'm like, "You know, it's hot." I hear what he's saying, but you know, I What kind of man would I be if I asked him to do something I wouldn't do. So, that for me, whatever you know, you they talk about your why, today that was my why. I told my son he had to walk. So, um it was hot, but you know, pushed through, set a good example. >> Discovery Place, you've kind of jumped in and immersed yourself into the community. You've been on Panthers Twitter and interacting with fans. Is this new for you, or have you done that in previous stops? And just talk about making sure that you're involved on that end as well. >> Yeah, no, I think, you know, for me uh like I said, I really about, you know, gratitude, kind of giving back to the community that's opening up their arms to me. I'm a big believer, I keep saying it every time, I'm asked about it, but being where your feet are. I really believe in that. And uh uh kind of leaving the place better uh in whatever terms than when you found it. And so, uh for me and my wife, we have our foundation. We're trying to figure out what we're going to be doing with the Dylan Family Foundation during the season. Uh you know, whether I'm here for however long, I don't know how the football game goes, but shoot, a lot of people like Charlotte. And if, you know, I want my my son to grow up and his people that he walks into the gas station that would be like, "You know what? I saw your dad, and he helped me, and he held the door for me." Uh you know, that goes a long way. Uh I got two little ones I'm trying to set a good example for. And you know, I think it's it's really just about being a good person. And I enjoy it. Not everybody likes to be, you know, in front of the camera or doing outgoing things. I like it. I enjoy it. And so that's fun for me. And to do it in a positive way positive outlets. There's a lot of them. Mhm. That's a good question. I would probably just say Jaseem. You know, obviously that's one of the guys that maybe yeah, that's the obvious answer. I'm not worried at all. >> Over the course of the last year though, did you did you notice opponents looking at you differently or treating you differently as you began to stack those numbers? >> Uh yeah, but I feel like I notice a lot more this year just in practice. First and foremost is what whatever whatever E coach E is doing over there, but you know, I'm getting a lot more double coverages and you know, linebackers rotating my way, safeties rotating my way and um to me to me that's a great sign. That just allows people to win their one-on-one matchups on the other side, so um like I said, that's that's lovely to me. >> What are you weighing now compared to last year at this time? I'm about >> Have you noticed anything physically changing with that added weight? >> Yeah, for sure. I'm in in college whenever I was heavier, I was stronger, faster. Um and that's how I feel right now. Like last year, like I said before, I just I didn't feel like myself. I feel like I wasn't moving as good and I didn't feel I was powerful and now I feel like I got a lot of back. >> Thanks, team mate. >> All right, y'all. I appreciate you. >> On my word. >> [music] [music] >> Mhm.

title: Matt LaFleur: 'We do have a lot of leaders in that locker room'
text: You have some more veterans this year than you've had in the past years. Does that make your job any easier or change your job at all have some extra veteran leadership around? >> I mean I don't I I don't really think too much about it. I can tell you this. Um we got a great group of guys. Uh I do think that some of the guys that have come in that are veterans have a very good process that some of the younger guys can learn from. So I think that definitely helps. >> So does it mean you're more of a leading on the leading leading by example part of it at least at this point of things? >> Well, I think that's it's I mean guys lead in different ways and um I can tell you we do have a lot of leaders in that locker room. Some are a little bit more vocal than others, but I think the guys have done a good job of trying to take ownership of their team because I'm a big believer in in player-led teams are going to be more effective than coach-led teams. >> For the three new players on offense, what's it like these next week and a half just getting them up to speed before we go on? >> It's like drinking water out of a fire hose. Um there's there's a lot of information that they got to be able to digest and then go out there and we'll see where they're at. Um it's great that we have these three practices. We'll have another you know, walk-through next Monday, but just to kind of try to get them up to speed as as quickly as possible. >> Does that mean a lot of late nights and early mornings for those guys and your position coaches to to get those guys going? >> Absolutely. It's whatever it takes. So I know those guys have spent a lot of time with them up to this point just trying to get them to be able to function through practice. That that's the one thing. Today's a little bit different. We're going to do an unscripted practice, but typically when you get especially when you get into game planning, you kind of pair everything down. It does make it a little bit easier, I would say, to digest it all, and then you can kind of get them ready for practice by going through the script. >> Now, when you have some new assistant coaches, how do you go about deciding on game day who's going to be upstairs, who's going to be on the sideline? >> Uh that's just it's a collaborative effort, I would tell you. Um certainly, like with the defensive side, let JG kind of map it out how he sees best fit, same with Cam. And then we've been together as an offense for a while now, so we've kind of got that that process dialed in. >> JG likes to be on the sideline, right? >> He does. I think it's a lot easier to see up top, but, you know, it's there's there's plusses and minus to to like whether you're down on the sideline, you kind of get a feel of the guys, and you get to look in a guy's face. Um but up top, I think it's it's much easier to see the the whole game progress. >> Does that vary offense to defensive-minded coaches in terms of liking to be up top versus the field? >> Yeah, I would say. There's some guys that we have that like I think Getsy preferred to call it from the sideline. I know when I was a coordinator, I like to be up top where it's nice, calm, cool, and collected, and you don't get I mean, it's just it's a more of a sterile environment. So, um I was joking with him this year that I was going to go up top and and coach from up there and let Joe McKelvey throw the the challenge flag. >> Was that a definite for you, though? Obviously, you [clears throat] have to be on the sideline now. When when you >> Don't have to do anything. Sean Payton, I have if I recall right, when he got injured, he he coached from upstairs. So, you can do whatever you want. >> thought of that? >> Getting getting injured? Yeah. >> [laughter] >> If it was cold on that day, I I sure as hell would be upstairs. >> That might be a good idea. Maybe we'll do it. I know we'll go ahead. >> The Vikings have changed personnel on defense. I mean, there've been some changes on their defense. How does that affect how you kind of try to decide how you're going to handle them? You know, does it change you know his scheme, but now the players are a little bit different. Do you have to try to guess how they're going to be used or >> Yeah, I think you you know, you try to get as much information as possible. You watch some of the preseason stuff. I know they're not showing everything, obviously. We've gone against each other quite I mean, a lot of times now. And I would tell you this that I think Flores does as good as anybody just creating problems for offenses. It's a highly aggressive defense. Um and you kind of especially week one, you're you're not really quite sure what's going to happen, but I I'm pretty sure that I can bank on it that they're going to bring a lot of pressure. >> Do you like having a divisional game week one? >> I don't put too much thought into it, to be honest with you. It's just it's it's the next game and that's the schedule makers decide and and we just show up and try to get prepared and ready to go out and play our best ball. >> Does that help? There's a lot of unscouted looks week one, but you are familiar with the team who's divisional teams more. >> Yeah, I think it goes both ways cuz they could say the same. >> Besides getting a couple days of rest this weekend, can you think of things that it's good to get done now cuz when you get into week after week into week in the schedule, you may not have time. >> Oh, yeah. There's there's a laundry list of things um that we've been working on, you know, as especially with a a short week game coming up in week three. So, you you kind of get a a rough blueprint from for that and that's going to change too, you know, with with the new staff down there, but um yeah, there there's there's a bunch of stuff that you want to try to get done and utilize your time when you just aren't so pressed. There there's always there's deadlines when you get to the regular season regards to when you need to get your plan done by so you have a chance to put it on paper and draw it up and do all that and get it to the players. So, there yeah, I would say there's less of a deadline. >> Now, you guys always like to talk about your two jumps. Um I know he's banged up now, but what did you see from Warren Brinson this off season and through through training camp it seemed like he took a pretty big one. >> Yeah, I think Warren's a really talented player. I think we saw it last year. I think and I've said this a million times, I feel like it just it's the consistency of which you go out there and perform. So, yeah, it's it's a bummer that he's been out. Um but I think he's he's got a bright future. He's just got to keep stacking day after day after day and show that level of consistency that I know he's capable of doing. >> Have you ever seen a story quite like Anthony Campbell? And at what point of this summer did he start to become a factor? >> Yeah, I would say um every time we went out there it's just the guy was making plays in the run game and the pass game. He's getting after the quarterback, affecting the quarterback. Uh batted probably more balls down than anybody we have. Um so, he just he consistently did it. >> Matt, there's you know, you never want to be peaking like right now obviously as the big season begins. Is there a certain point or like percentage that you want the team to be at before you guys go into week one or like a grade like if you were to do like a report card? Is there anything like you would want to get to that point of before week one starts. >> I think I think that's impossible. To be to be able to I don't even understand that to be honest with you. He's been a really big guy this whole help holding everybody accountable across the room. And like him Sauce even like Mooney coming back we have a lot of older guys who do a very good job at the accountability piece so it helps out a lot. >> With you Sauce and Mooney really healthy going into the season what do you expect that group to what impact do you expect y'all to have early on? >> Um I think we'll be a play at a very high level. [clears throat] >> Yeah, I would say just to piggyback on what Ray said, um we will we will sacrifice or compromise on talent for those intangible qualities. Like he he he performed well. He just wasn't He wasn't able to be out there as much, but I would say last week with the practices, the scrimmage, and that preseason game, you know, he earned his spot. And you know, and look, we we still had guys like Scruggs that was going to be in that spot. It's just the unfortunate injury to Cade kind of forced Scruggs into that kind of used to be guard center kind of center only. So, that was kind of one piece of the competition, but it was good to finally see Miles Frazier out there. You know, he's I mean, he's not a rookie, but kind of you know, he just didn't have a whole lot last year. So, this is kind of his first year really having an off season, having a whole training camp, and he was able to show some things. Not just at guard, but some some versatility at tackle as well. >> Just because we won't talk to you for a few months on on the four extensions you were looking to get done this off season. And then are you still you know, hopeful on on Sam and Brian regardless of the timetable? starting with Gibbs, yeah, they're like all all of them are unique, especially when it gets up to that magnitude from a from a financial standpoint. Like we already knew what we wanted to do, you know, and you just had to see who was going to get done first, and you got to kind of adjust and pivot off of that. You know, there's a couple of factors that you know, that we we still got to sort through, but but in terms of us wanting those guys around, absolutely. Look, we we have guys that can play the run, obviously. And look, we say it all the time. He Look, you got to earn the right to pass rush, so you can't just have all pass rushers from out the gate, but you can't stop the run. If you're just getting gashed all day, you don't need to throw the ball. But we've we've done a good job and Shep's done a great job just in terms from a run defense standpoint and there's in his structures and how we deploy that personnel, we wanted to add more juice regardless. Guys like Gil Howard, did you mention Yeah, I just mentioned him. A guy like Gil Howard, that was one of the first thing that you see when you watch his tape. Um My first thought was he's could be an impact you know, what do you call it? Like a DPR kind of sub rusher, but because of his innate violence that he's wired with, then he's actually been a little bit better in the run game than probably what we even anticipated. Not that it was bad in college, but NFL's different story, you know? And so if you have 650 lb coming on you, it's it's hard. But because of how he's built, because he can bend and he's he has this innate violence and hand usage, he gives himself a chance. So, but yeah, that was that was a that was a guy that we always had appreciation for, affinity for. And also I I to give our our our analytics department a shout out too because they were able to find some signal on you know guys like like him and you know a couple of other guys that we were able to acquire. >> [laughter] >> Couple of other guys. Well, um we still have confidence that you know they they can come back. You just can't really give a exact timeline. Um but yeah, I mean they're they're both here. They're rehabbing. They're they're working hard. Just can't offer timeline. But yeah, um yeah, the hopes is to have both of them back at some point. >> Thanks for having us. Thanks, Raheem. >> [music]

title: What We Learned From Brad Holmes’ Comments on the Detroit Lions’ 53-Man Roster
text: Welcome back to Lines Collective. We're live every single Wednesday at 6 PM. We got a three-man crew tonight here to break down Brad Holmes's comments today from his press conference. We'll see you in a second. >> I'm your host Jeff Freddy uh from Crutch Time Ward Sports. Will Birsfield on vacation, but not really at the same time because look at him. He's he's having a good time. >> Check the pore. Check the poor, fellas. >> It's an elite an elite poor. Will Birfield, you know who that is. 97 with the ticket. Justin Rogers, Dark Football Network, Colton Pouncy from the Athletic is not going to be able to make it tonight. He's uh doing some big things right now, but he'll be back next week and joining us. But we have a lot to talk about today. Brad Holmes spoke to the media. Him and Dave Perquette >> little bit little back and forth. Justin, you were there, so this is where your your perspective is important today, >> man. Uh it's it's interesting that the roster cut breakdown became kind of a a Terry Arnold back and forth and um I will tell you right now I went in there with a dozen questions that I wanted answered today or hope to hear answered today and Terry Arnold was absolutely on my list and I know a lot of fans have moved on or want to move on but could I'd like to maybe add a little perspective on first and foremost why I think this is important. Um, you know, it's not just the what, it's it's the why I think that we haven't got answers to um, in terms of the timing of that cut, right? You didn't cut him when the accusations broke in March. You didn't cut him when his acquaintances arrested and charged and plead guilty. You didn't cut him when he was mentioned multiple times in uh, a judge's notes on the case or when a warrant was issued or even when he was arrested. It wasn't until that that pre-trial hearing with two hours of detective testimony that I mean they cut him what felt like minutes after. And so I think at some level you want to know why. Why did the team cut him? Did he lie to the team or did they feel like he lied to the team? Was there new information that was revealed in that pre-trial that they didn't know previously? Was being charged and going to trial the the threshold? And so what what is the organizational line of demarcation? Was ownership involved in this decision? If you're going to be a franchise that wears your culture as a badge of honor and the Lions have earned that right. They've made the culture very good, then you should answer not to the media, but to your fan base when something doesn't meet the smell test of the standard. If you're going to sit there and tell us the standard is the standard on the field and off the field, this didn't meet the standard. And so why didn't it meet the standard? And it matters because it tells you what the threshold of tolerance is for players you may sign in the future, for players you may draft in the future, for other situations that may arise where a player merits getting cut, you know, and um and so that's that's why it matters from that point. And then the secondary point is did the Lions do enough? And we had Brad Holmes on this podcast. So we were very fortunate to have that in March and uh the Terrion news was still fresh at that time. And um it's pretty late in the podcast. You could probably go find it. But I I asked Brad because I figured maybe best case scenario Terran was going to get suspended. you know, the league doesn't take well to just even the optics of things and you'll get thrown into the um the the pool suspension for conduct detrimental to the league. Correct. So, you know, he might have faced a three-game or six game or eight game ban whether nothing came of it. And so, I asked Brad about it like how much do you have to plan for that? And the phrase he used was pessimistic planner, >> right? And we talked about this on our first episode back. I think Will, you missed that one, unfortunately. But I I questioned what was pessimistic about the Lion's plan. You know, if Brad's a pessimistic planner and he was seeing the worst case scenario of this Terry Arnold thing, what what did they do pessimistically, right? They they resigned Rocky, which they should have done anyway. They signed Roger McCreary, which all signs pointed to him being the slot replacement for Meek Robertson. That had nothing to do with Tyrion Arnold. And ultimately they they drafted Keith Abney who I think fell into their laps. Like they didn't go out and trade up for this kid. He fell to their laps in the fifth round and they told us he's going to be a slot guy. And so you just didn't leave yourself um you know a lot of depth options. And so now we get to the regular season, right? And I I think cornerback's a big question mark. I I feel really good really good about DJ Reed and Rocky Sin. I do. I think the floor is very high with those starters. What's one of the most injured position groups year in and year out across this league? His cornerback. And DJ Reid is a durable player. We saw him miss what six games last year, Will. >> Yeah. >> And so you're at this point now where you might be leaning on Rake Straw who's played 46 snaps or you might be leaning on Khalil Dorsy or Roger Mccur who had a pretty rocky camp and wasn't even projected as an outside guy. And so the questions that we were asking here were fair. What I will say is, and love Dave, I think Dave does a great job. I think Dave got a little clunky in his question today. I think he tried to cram two questions into one >> and gave Brad this opportunity to kind of be combative about it, to set up straw man arguments, repeating, "Are you saying we should have done this?" [laughter] >> Brevin and the fact that you guys were able to bring him back and and how close is he to being able to contribute? >> Yeah, Brevin is very close. We expect Brevin to be out practicing next week. So, Brevin Brevin is definitely close. Uh, love Brevin. Ever since the first time I got here, I always speak highly of Brevin just because of the the joy that he brings, type of person that he is. Just love being around him. Love the worker that he is. He had he's had some unfortunate things happen when it comes to injury-wise, but man, there's no one with a better attitude and how you attack a day than Brevin Jordan. He's going to make a play with it. So, I'm always pulling for Brevin and I was happy to get him back on our team. >> Like um to follow up on Brevin and T to a similar extent, um it seemed like when guys suffer catastrophic injuries, you guys are fairly patient with them and giving them grace to have the the the time to come back. I understand that how everybody just kind of leaves you to the side, forgets about you. It's a it's a lonely lonely moment. It's a lonely process of working yourself back. So, for me, always have a heart for those guys. I'm always going to give those guys the time that they need to recover. It's going to look a little different when you have injuries. And guys just have to understand that. So, I'm going to stick with them and support them as best as I can. Going back to the process of the 53, what's the biggest difference in attacking that year four versus year one when I'm sure it was probably even more overwhelming than it is now? >> The attacking the 53 is is for me it's not overwhelming. It's always comes down to three, four, five guys you got to make a decision on. And there are some tough decisions to make every year, right? And it's been that way for me ever since I've been in this position. Tough decisions to make this year. Again, I want to keep everybody. Can we increase the roster so we can have more players? That would be a great thing for everyone around the league. But it's uh you know, these guys, we we've get guys who are made of the right stuff. And if they don't make it here, you I'm very confident these guys will go and impact another organization in a big way. I think a lot of work went into designing the uniforms. A lot of thought went into it. Just making it, you know, Houston. And that's the that's the cool part about it, right? Seeing Houston, my wife gives me a hard time always on the Houston blue. I didn't understand it, but now I understand how important the Houston Blue is and uh what it means to the city. So, I mean, they're really, really cool uniforms. I'm pretty sure those the best rivalry uniforms that have came out to date. And so, great job. Great job, Houston. And I'm just, you know, it just gives you more pride for your city, for the team to see everybody excited about the uniforms come out. My kids are, they were crushing me on like, "Daddy, have you seen the uniforms? Have you seen them?" like, "No, I have not seen them. [laughter] They didn't show me. I didn't I didn't get a sneak peek, but my kids were fired up about them, and so we was able to get them a little gear." So, they're they're fired up. >> Your wife's from Houston, right? >> She is from Houston. She is from Houston. So, those uniforms mean a lot. So, thankful that we were able to execute it in a really great manner. >> All right. Appreciate it, guys. Thank you.
