text: How did you find out find out uh you made the team? Um and were you initially nervous after kind of getting hurt u and kind of missing that that next couple weeks? >> Um yeah, I think for me especially I think this is obviously everybody knows how stressful camp is. Um every day we're being evaluated, every little thing we're doing being evaluated. So me not being out there, obviously I was a little I was a little concerned but but I think I I came to peace with what I did show. um everybody, the staff, my players, my teammates, um everything I could do and I just left it up to God and and and luckily I was blessed and I'm blessed to still be here. >> How did you find out your reaction? >> Um I actually found out on the Texans Instagram. Uh I didn't really I didn't really hear anything all day, but I I've also heard on on on days like this, no news is good news. So, um, it hit about 3 4:00 and and from what I understood, I was like, "Okay, I know by 5:00 everything would be out." And so, I didn't hear anything then. And then I figured, um, I figured I was okay. And I found out on social media like everybody else did. So, it was a cool experience. Got to got to celebrate that with my family. It was awesome. >> When you look at what you did and stacking lots of days, we made a lot of plays. We talked about in camp. How proud are you of the ability to be consistent? because a lot of times for a younger player that might be the hardest thing. >> Um yeah, I mean I think for me that's something I've tried to carry out throughout my whole career. Um coming from college, coming here I think that's the lifestyle I the lifestyle I try to live. Um try to be consistent with everything I do relating to game, how I watch film, how I eat, um how I take care of my body, try to do all those things. And and for me luckily I think obviously being able to trust those things is is is what makes you better on the field. and um I was able to have a lot of a lot of successful days make some plays and and luckily that worked in my favor. What are some of the things that you learned from Coach Dino and also being around players like >> I think hunting the ball. I think that's obviously the number one thing. Uh takeaways, you you you you kind of make your living off takeaways in the league and for me as a young player. Um I think Dino teaches it a different way. Um, and he's taught me in a way that I I never been taught before and and just to to to always think about the ball um, every every moment, which is allowed me to to make some of the plays that I did make during training camp. And I think um, just just being able to watch guys like Ste, Kamari, um, JRock, Trey, everybody in the room, like everybody's attacking the ball every play, it kind of made me want to elevate my game and try to get there. >> Follow up to Sergeant's question. What's the biggest thing or the biggest difference for you at this that you've noticed at this point, the biggest change and the biggest thing you have to learn how to do? >> Yeah, for me I I think speed of course. Uh guys are a lot faster, guys a lot more athletic, great route runners. So I think it it becomes more more the small things in the game. Um trying to study the receivers splits, where they lined up, how's his body language, does he take any false steps? Um things like that to try to give you that advantage. Um I think everybody we play is athletic. Um everybody we always see every day is athletic. So, um, it's really trying to find those small those those small things that that are going to make the difference. >> And you had that cheering section and your family there probably every day. What was it like when you're able to give them the call and say, "Hey, I made or they know just like you cuz they're probably maybe hitting refresh on some things." >> They knew just like me. So, they actually they actually told me we have a we have a small family group chat and uh they ended up sending me um the report and I was like, "Okay, wow." And then I ended up getting getting a phone call from them and then uh then found out. But it was it was awesome. Um I I never imagined it imagined it playing out this way and and just to be be here with with my entire family has been unbelievable. Um I'm extremely blessed with the organization giving me a chance to to come show my talents and opportunity to keep going. >> When they had that local day that you were a part of, did you kind of have like a feeling like, hey, maybe I'll be back. uh you know by whether it's via being drafted or undrafted. >> I didn't really know what to expect honestly. Um I I did a lot of stuff in the pre-draft with a lot of different teams, but um definitely coming back here and coming home, I think seeing this this side of the Texans um obviously being outsider looking in my entire life um it was a lot different than I expected, but um it was also um a lot better than than I I also expected. Um, so I think just being able to learn from Dino early on, preaching, getting the ball as much as you can and doing those things, it it left me a good uh left me a good taste to just be able to take as much as I can. >> Another local guy up at Stanford, Andrew Luck. Uh, was he seems like he's pretty hands-on. Was he a resource through this process? Did he get you prepared? What did he teach you during your time there? >> Um, yeah. I think uh Andrew's Andrew's words to me before going through the process is just never lose your your your hard work. Obviously, nobody ever is going to give get give anything to you. So So for me, that's kind of how I treated this whole process. Um I have to work hard. Um drafted, undrafted, um it doesn't matter. You have to be consistent. Try to keep keep growing every day and uh got to keep giving yourself a chance. From the outside looking in, what was it about this this defense when you looked at it that you knew that, hey, I'm going to have to put in some real work in order to, you know, be a part of this top ranked defense. >> I think kind of like I said, takeaways at all different levels. And I think obviously the physicality. Um, I think this this this team in general is just built on on being the more aggressive, the more dominant, the more physical team. Um, so for me coming in, I think we have so many great leaders that instill those standards every day um, on on all sides of the ball. So just being able to to listen those guys talk about it and also be about it every day as well. Um, I think it it raises everybody's standard as well. >> A lot of ticket requests. >> A lot of ticket requests. We gonna have to we have to figure it out. But, uh, [laughter] it's going to be awesome. I'm looking forward to it. >> Did you go to any games when you were running? >> I did. Um, I went to a couple in the Gary Kubak uh era. Um, I don't remember too too well, honestly. I I do remember it was a game against the Browns that I went to that I really remember, but I went to a couple, not not too many. I was always playing youth youth sports um on on on Saturday, Sunday, so I didn't catch too many, but I remember being in NRG as a as a kid or not NRG, I was in Reliance as a kid. So, uh, yeah, it's it's crazy to crazy to be back. Um, just crazy to walk in the same same stadium that I' I've drove past my entire life. >> Do you still keep up with uh Manville football and what do you think about the overall local talent in Houston? >> It's awesome. I think there's no place like it. Um, shout out to Manville. Shout out to all the guys still playing. I I watched that game this past week. Guys killed it. Um, I'm I'm very in tune with with with what's going on and I still I still keep up with a lot of with a lot of kids that go there and just keep supporting them on their journeys. Um, I I've heard from all my Manville coaches um over the past 3, four months. Um, even in college like I'll hear from them frequently. Definitely extended family of mine and um I support them all the way. everything that's [clears throat] kind of going on with college sports right now. Did you have any kind of weird conversations like do you want to come back to school if this doesn't work out? Any of your friends going through that? Like what's that process like for someone that actually lives it? >> Um I didn't really have uh any of those any of those thoughts or concerns. I I did have a couple friends that were considering it and I think have they might be there now. Um for me that's not anything I wanted to do. Um, I think I've always wanted to be a pro and I I want to just keep striving to to try to be the best pro I can. And I think my time in college expired and I was just ready to ready to move on. >> All good. >> Thanks, guys. >> Appreciate it. Thank you.

Um, everybody, the staff, my players, my teammates, um, everything I could do and I just left it up to God and and and luckily I was blessed and I'm blessed to still be here. >> How did you find out? What was your reaction? >> Um, I actually found out on the Texans Instagram. Uh, I didn't really I didn't really hear anything all day. But I I've also heard on on on days like this, no news is good news. So, um, it hit about 3 4:00 and from what I understood, I was like, "Okay, I know by 5:00 everything would be out." And so, I didn't hear anything then. And then I figured, um, I figured I was okay. And I found out on social media like everybody else did. So, um, it was a cool experience. Got to got to celebrate that with my family. It was awesome. when you look at what you did and stacking lots of days where you made a lot of plays and we talked about in camp, how proud are you of the ability to be consistent? Because a lot of times for a younger player, that might be the hardest thing. >> Um, yeah, I mean, I think for me that's something I've tried to carry out throughout my whole career. Um, coming from college, coming here, I think that's the lifestyle I the lifestyle I try to live. um to try to be consistent with everything I do relating to game, how I watch film, how I eat, um how I take care of my body, try to do all those things. And and for me, luckily, I think obviously being able to trust those things is is is what makes you better on the field. And um I was able to have a lot of a lot of successful days, make some plays, and and luckily that worked in my favor. >> What's some of the things that you learned from Coach Dino and also being around? >> I think hunting the ball. I think that's obviously the number one thing. Uh takeaways, you you you you kind of make your living off takeaways in the league. And for me as a young player, um I think Dino teaches it a different way. Um and he's taught me in a way that I I never been taught before and and just to to to always think about the ball um every every moment, which is allowed me to to make some of the plays that I did make during training camp. And I think um just just being able to watch guys like Sting, Kamari, um JRock, Trey, everybody in the room, like everybody's attacking the ball every play, it kind of made me want to elevate my game and try to get there. >> Follow up to Sergeant's question. What's the biggest thing or the biggest difference for you at this level that you've noticed at this point? Biggest change, the biggest thing you have to learn how to do? >> Yeah, for me, I I think speed of course. Uh guys are a lot faster, guys are a lot more athletic, great route runner. So I think it it becomes more of the more the small things in the game. Um trying to study the receiver splits where they lined up. How's his body language? Does he take any false steps? Um things like that to try to give you that advantage. Um I think everybody we play is athletic. U everybody we always see every day is athletic. So um it's really trying to find those small those small things that that are going to make the difference. And you had that cheering section. You had your family there probably every day. What was it like when you're able to give them the call and say, "Hey, I made her." Or do they know just like you? Cuz they're probably maybe hitting refresh on some things. >> They knew just like me. So they actually they actually told me we have a we have a small family group chat and uh they ended up sending me um the report and I was like, "Okay, wow." And then I ended up getting getting a phone call from them and then uh then found out. But it was it was awesome. Um, I I never imagined it imagined it playing out this way and and just to be be here with with my entire family has been unbelievable. Um, I'm extremely blessed with the organization giving me a chance to to come show my talents and opportunity to keep going. >> When they had that local day that you were a part of, did you kind of have like the feeling like, hey, maybe I'll be back uh, you know, if I whether it's via being drafted or undrafted? >> I didn't really know what to expect, honestly. Um I I did a lot of stuff in the pregraft with a lot of different teams, but um definitely coming back here and coming home, I think seeing this this side of the Texans, um obviously being outside of looking in my entire life, um it was a lot different than I expected, but um it was also um a lot better than than I also expected. Um, so I think just being able to learn from Dino early on, preaching, getting the ball as much as you can and doing those things, it it left me a good uh left me a good taste to just be able to take as much as I can. >> Another local guy up at Stanford, Andrew Luck. Uh, was he seems like he's pretty hands-on. Was he a resource through this process? Did he get you prepared? What did he teach you during your time there? >> Um, yeah. I think uh Andrew's Andrew's words to me before going through the process is just never lose your your your hard work. Obviously, nobody ever is going to give get give anything to you. So, so for me, that's kind of how I treated this whole process. Um I have to work hard. Um drafted, undrafted, um it doesn't matter. You have to be consistent, try to keep keep growing every day and uh got to keep giving yourself a chance. From the outside looking in, what was it about this this defense when you looked at it that you knew that, hey, I'm going to have to put in some real work in order to, you know, be a part of this top ranked defense. >> I think kind of like I said, takeaways at all different levels. And I think obviously the physicality. Um, I think this this this team in general is just built on on being the more aggressive, the more dominant, the more physical team. Um, so for me coming in, I think we have so many great leaders that instill those standards every day um on on on all sides of the ball. So just being able to to listen to those guys talk about it and also be about it every day as well. Um, I think it it raises everybody's standard as well. >> A lot of ticket requests. >> A lot of ticket requests. We have to have to figure it out. But uh it's going to be awesome. I'm looking forward to it. >> Did you go to any games when you were running? >> I did. Um, I went to a couple in the Gary Kubak uh era. Um, I don't remember too too well, honestly. I I do remember it was a game against the Browns that I went to that I really remember, but I went to a couple, not not too many. I was always playing youth youth sports um on on on Saturday, Sunday, so I didn't catch too many, but I remember being in NRG as a as a kid or not NRG, I was in Reliance as a kid. So, uh yeah, it's it's crazy to crazy to be back. Um, just crazy to walk in the same same stadium that I' I've drove past my entire life. >> Do you still keep up with Manville football and what do you think about the overall local talent in Houston? >> It's awesome. I think there's no place like it. Um, shout out to Manville. Shout out to all the guys still playing. I I watched that game this past week. Guys killed it. Um, I'm I'm very in tune with with with what's going on and I still I still keep up with a lot of with a lot of kids that go there and just keep supporting them on their journeys. Um, I I've heard from all my Manville coaches um over the past 3, four months. Um, even in college like I'll hear from them frequently. Definitely extended family of mine and um I support them all the way. everything [clears throat] that's kind of going on with college sports right now, could you have any kind of weird conversations like do you want to come back to school if this doesn't work out? Any of your friends going through that? Like what's that process like for someone that actually lives it? >> Um I didn't really have uh any of those any of those thoughts or concerns. I I did have a couple friends that were considering it and I think have they might be there now. Um for me that's not anything I wanted to do. Um, I think I've always wanted to be a pro and I I want to just keep striving to to try to be the best pro I can. And I think my time in college expired and I was just ready to ready to move on. >> Thanks, guys. >> Appreciate it. Thank you. messed it up. >> Yeah. >> Yeah. Quan, >> trade and you thanked the Patriots for sending you an organization you said you wanted to be a part of. What was it about this place and how do you feel like it's going so far? >> Um, obviously we know the Texans are a tough team. um last year with the Patriots coming into the playoffs. So, we knew that that was one of the top teams we would have had to face on our path to get into the Super Bowl. But, um you know, I always did believe this team had potential. They a great team on offense and defense. And I think uh just with this year, we got another chance to get back to that. So, that's the goal. >> What do you think that you bring to this offensive side of the ball? >> Um just big playmaking ability, you know. Um whether it's short routes, mid routes, deep routes, uh go ball, you know, uh I'm gonna always build that trust every day with CJ. So, >> what's that been like uh you know, building uh in getting to know CJ in these first few days? >> Oh, it been great. We get together after practice, kind of start building that timing, you know, um different quarterback for me, a different receiver for him. So, as long as we on the same path, that's the goal at the end of the day. Is that is that the um probably biggest challenge just finding chemistry, finding timing with receiver? >> N I mean I I feel like from a receiver standpoint, chemistry is not really a tough thing to do. Um like I say, it's all about the effort you put in with the quarterback. >> What is the difficulty in learning the playbook coming here so late, you know, after after training camp? >> Uh it's not really bad. It's uh half of it is carryover from what we kind of ran in New England, but at the end of the day, it's all about how much you put into it, too. You know, uh you got to study outside the building. Uh knowing the playbook is a part of your job. You know, if you don't know what to do, then you can't play. So, >> praise in New England for your mindset and staying locked in even when it the conversation was you might not be there this year. What about you allowed you to stay locked in with all the outside noise and stuff going on on the roster? uh just being a pro, you know, uh when I was 20 years old coming in, I could tell you that I maybe would have handled that whole situation differently, but uh what I experienced the past three years going on year four, uh learning how to be a pro professional about it and that's the way I carried myself throughout the whole process. >> You talk about your um just your relationship with Digi Junior and if that if you guys talked at all that helped coming here. >> Uh we talk every day since I've been here. Uh cool relationship. We go back to college. We played two years together. So, um, that's something that's something that was cool for me, seeing familiar faces in the building. We got a couple LSU guys. Uh, so it's good being back. >> You look at trade and they were complimentary of you when they made it, uh, Mike Bra specifically, but he also said the role he envisioned for you would be a role that you would have liked. When did they kind of communicate with you? And do you use it at all even with [clears throat] no hard feelings that you said? Is it motivational fuel just that, hey, well, they didn't see me as the guy that was going to be heavily targeted up on game day? >> No, I mean, you know, uh they did pay two guys to come in and do that job. Uh sadly, it is the way it is. You know, uh being that it's a contract year for me, I seek a bigger role. Uh I feel like what Rave said in his media uh interview, it wasn't it wasn't nothing bad. I wouldn't say I used that as fuel. You know, at the end of the day, he sat down. It was an honest opinion. He sat there, talked, speak his truth, and uh pretty much moved forward from it. >> Talk about what you like most about this Texans offense from what you saw before you got here and what you seen. >> A lot of playmakers, you know, uh whether it's the running backs, the receivers, Nico, uh he bigger than I thought. So, it's a little taller than I thought. But, uh just kind of getting a familiarity with everybody. um how they play they play styles, but whether like I say it's the deep ball ability, the short uh short routes, being able to take that to the house 20 yards. Uh just being here a week, I've been kind of getting familiar with the schemes, the program, but I love everything so far. >> What are your early thoughts on CJ, both the player and the leader person? >> He been great so far. Um the player, I would say, uh playmaker ability. He able to do anything for real. I trust that he'll get the ball anywhere on the field and he trust that we going to be in the spot whenever he need us. >> Uh I say I ain't been here long enough so still figuring out that process but just doing whatever they ask of me. So >> this is a contract here for you. How much do you feel like you being here is um something that you can put on tapes for other teams to see but really for this team who actually wanted you to come here? I think it's always good when the team wants you to come here. You know, they um truly believe in your ability, big playmaking ability. And I would just say for me, just doing just doing what I always do, you know, not overthinking it, you know, uh try to catch everything that come my way at the end of the day. I know it's a big year for me, so make the most of my opportunities. >> Said when you were 20 years old, you may not have handled the situation now back then like you did now, that maturation process for you going going through that. At what point did did you realize the NFL is a game I love to play, but it's also a business? >> Uh, I would say I think when I was 20, still a little childish, you know, young coming out of college. Uh, I think my second year was still a little that it was more 50/50, but I think uh at the beginning of last year off season when Varel and them came in was kind of when my mindset my mindset shifted. So, um, I think that was big for me. >> What about just defense and going up against them? what has that been like and talk about how that obviously helps your game. >> I mean it been great on great. We know Stingley one of the best quarterbacks in the league. Uh Lass are great himself, you know. So going against those guys every day, you know, that's kind of the guys you see on Sundays. I always did say uh coming from LSU, you know, you play a lot of those guys, the Certain, the Stingleys, a lot of the top guys in the league. So uh you really seen that every day. So I mean uh just going against those guys every day is only going to make us better on Sundays. question for you. When it comes to going up and getting the ball and some of the one-handed catches, things we're watching, including on Derek Stingley Jr., what's kind of the mentality? What allows you to make that type of play? If you could kind of take us through some of those moments in detail. Thank you. >> Uh, I'll say when it come to big plays, it's really something that's not predetermined. Like it kind of just happened. Like not every ball gonna be perfect. Like you gonna have to make plays sometimes. Whether the ball behind you, you got to adjust. what this in front of you. You just got to make a play. But um like I said, it's all about adjusting. >> You had a quote before the divisional round last year basically like I'm excited to face this defense. Kind of got some attention here. Do you feel like you fit in with what the defense brings? I guess do calls it swarm. Is that kind of the mindset that you have too? >> Uh yeah, I kind of like the uh Texan swarm thing, but like you said, um yeah, it's pretty much pretty much the mindset. I feel go ahead. >> As you I don't know if you even consider this as you head into your fourth year that you're about to play your fourth different head coach. Is that anything that matters to you each year or proving yourself each year? >> No, I didn't even I didn't even think about that. But uh now that you say that that is that is a thing, but you know that don't got nothing to do with me. Uh like I said, they believe they trust in my ability. They brought me here for a reason. So I'm I'mma do that. >> Off the field. How good does it feel just to be closer to home? I would say it do feel good, man, being in Boston. Uh it's 4-hour flight back home, but uh Louisiana, it's three hours right up the road. LSU play this weekend, might go back home, watch them play Clemson, uh Saturday night, Death Valley. So, feel good. Uh even though I'm not really home, it's the people make it feel like home. So, shout out to them. >> Appreciate y'all. when you were out there against Carolina, were you kind of think like, hey, this is it. I've got one last chance to make this impression to try to stick. >> Yeah. So, obviously, you know, uh struggling with a little bit of an injury there, uh that first preseason game, so I wasn't in for that. So, um, I kind of already knew that that was kind of like my last shot, like those two last preseason games. So, um, I thought it was really important to try and go out there, go as hard as I can every single play and, uh, at the end of the day, like I didn't have no regrets. So, >> yeah. >> What are some of the things that you um learned from Rob since you've been there? Yeah, I think just his mindset being relentless every single day, whether it's how you attack the game mentally and physically. Um, spiritual shot of the game, uh, just getting closer with my faith, too. So, um, I think just having him as a coach and being a leader for us in the Dline room, like, um, it's probably one of the best things I could ask for, you know. So, >> in high school, you played on the offensive side of the ball as well. How much how much does that help you um you know playing on the defensive side of the ball? >> Yeah. So, I think sometimes like it's kind of weird to explain, but um say maybe like I I notice there's a little bit more space on the inside gap and I I I might be able to bait that guy into running into the gap that I want him to. So, I think just kind of understanding what the mindset is of someone who's running the ball, someone who's throwing the ball, like you might be able to pick up on kind of maybe a hunch or an instinct on where they might step to. So things like that >> is complimentary of your motor and you know one thing coaches always say you don't want to have to ever have to coach effort. Uh how has that kind of carried you from being a walk-on Wyoming then going up to NC State and then making this team? >> Yeah. So I think at the end of the day like no matter what something coaches shouldn't have to ever harp on is effort. um you know, you can be intentional with how you work, be precise, all that kind of stuff, but if if you're not trying your hardest every single time you're on the field, like none of that stuff really matters, you know. So, um yeah, I think I think them emphasizing that right from the very beginning, like that is our standard. That's who we are. Um I think that was the one thing that stuck out to me from the very from the very beginning. So, >> follow up on what Sarge asked you about the room. Talk about being in a room with guys like Will and Denil and you know Ed, talk about that. >> Yeah, I I mean, in our room, like we got guys that are so knowledgeable about not only the position, but even just the game, how it works, the flow of the game, um how you need to pick up intensity on the the back end of the game, that kind of thing. So, I think just being able to ask Will and Denil questions, uh even D Horton, uh Drov, like ask all those guys questions about um how they see the game at a certain position or, uh whether it's a certain look on the offense that they're giving us. Um, I think it's just amazing like to be in that room and be able to anything I need to ask them. Like I got a full encyclopedia on everything like hundreds, thousands of different reps that they've taken, you know, and so um I couldn't be more thankful and more grateful for those guys. >> Going back to Wyoming, how much of a role did Craig B have in you being here right now? >> Yeah, so he was kind of the first coach that ever gave me a chance like um I had no division one offers coming out of high school. I had a couple D2s, but Coach Bowl, he he talked to me and was we kind of set up a deal like come come over here and uh you know, if you do everything the right way school-wise and and on the football field, like we'll give you a scholarship and and I think I can turn you into a really good man. And so, um yeah, I fully trusted him, took him up on that offer, and he was a man of his word. and uh after five five years there and um even after his retirement too like uh we still talked you know he'll send me a text here and there and congratulate me and stuff like that. So I think just having him as kind of that uh first person to kind of give me that chance like um always be you know really thankful for him. >> Is there anything truly meaningful about being able to get 54 back now that you're on the team that you were in both spots in college? Yeah, I for a second I was kind of thinking of just staying with 74 just kind of a reminder like to keep working, but uh yeah. Yeah. Uh but even the the uh equipment room guys were like, "Nah, man. Like not for an edge. Like you can't have that." I was like, "All right, bet." So I think just being able to get back in my old college number like it it feels really comfortable and um I think my parents really like it too. They like it probably the most. So, >> what's the balance of like walking into a room with Will and Denil and then and then Clowny joins and like leaning on them, but being able to do what you do and be being confident enough to do what you do with what could be an intimidating intimidating room to walk into. >> Yeah, I can see how it would be really intimidating. I mean, obviously at the very start, like it was, you know, like I'm I'm seeing these guys and I'm just coming into this new system. Like, I'm a rookie, man. Like, I don't know nothing. And so, um, just kind of trying to grab onto their coattails and take a ride with them. So, um, obviously, you know, like they're these huge guys, huge names. Um, I think at the end of the day, like just trying to do my best to emulate what they do. Um, you know, if they crush it, crush it on the edge, like I'm I'm going to go and do my my stuff and then crush it on the edge, you know. So, um, I think they set a really high standard in the room. Um, and I mean it doesn't matter if you're, you know, scout or what, like coach, coach wants it done the same way every single time. And so I think, you know, Denil and Will, like they do a really good job of staying on guys about um, doing stuff the right way. So >> on the other side of that though, how close have you and Kate McDonald got, especially, you know, both being rookies coming in here, coming into that type of room, that type of situation, especially, you know, on this And also you seeing these guys how competitive they are, how professional they are. But >> what does it mean to you to also have them be able to embrace you because they're also like a big friendly group and they accept accept if you're on a team they accept you as a brother. >> Yeah. I think I think that is such an awesome thing. Um, especially like being super far from home, like I'm sure, uh, Kaden can attest to it too. Like, um, coming from Ohio State, you know, like it's it's kind of like you're going into a whole new thing and you don't really know nobody. So, um, it's kind of awesome to to know that you have a brotherhood in that room, like people who really care about you, uh, more than just what you're doing on the football field. Like, if something's like we're that close to where in the room, you know, if something's going on, like we can talk to each other about it. like, you know, we're not scared to uh talk about our feelings or something that might be going on at home. Like, and I think just to have something like that, like it's even more important because it makes you play even harder for them like when you're on the field. So, um yeah, I I think that that part is really important. >> Thank you guys. Appreciate y'all.

title: Fast chemistry: Texans WR Kayshon Boutte, QB1 C.J. Stroud off to 'great' start
text: Texans a tough team um last year with the Patriots coming into the playoffs. So, we knew that that was one of the top teams we would have had to face on our path to get into the Super Bowl. But, um you know, I always did believe this team had potential. They a great team on offense and defense. And I think uh just with this year, we got another chance to get back to that. So, that's the goal. >> Into the preparation. Coach McDaniels has been working with him since we were back in Carolina. So, he's been dialed in to his preparation, getting himself ready to go. He's out there running routes, lining, getting his plays done today. So, he'll he'll be ready to go on game day. >> Hey guys, Aaron Wilson at Reliance Stadium. The Texans introduced formerly new wide receiver Kan Booty. Been a little bit of a delay since the trade talking with him. They wanted to let him get acclimated to the offense, to his new teammates, and some familiar faces for him. Obviously, Derrick Stingley Jr., fellow LSU football alums. And what he's been doing, he's been trying to build timing and chemistry with Texans quarterback CJ Strad, who's extremely happy to have Kahan here in the wake of losing Jaden Higgins for the season to a torn ACL. So, what Booty brings to the table? obvious contested catch ability. A proven pinch hand for being able to go up and make the big catch. An ability to create separation and a physical wide receiver. Not that tall but very strong and someone with strong hands, a good route runner, and a dangerous big play threat. And one of the things that we asked him about was the timing that he's been building with CJ. You look at what happens here. That means that they have to get on the same page. they have to spend some time together. He says that's not that tough and you'll hear from him. Of course, we have a press conference with him. But, you know, when you think about what you need to know, the timing is vital and the co quarterback has to be able to trust that he can put the football up to you and that you're going to come down with it and that you're going to make that critical pivotal catch as he did in the playoffs for the Patriots against Derek Stley Jr., a spectacular touchdown catch. That's not the only reason he's here. So, when you think about Kahan Booty, he can block. He can do it all. And what do I expect from him in the first game? We're going to get into that in a moment. But one thing that I think about when it comes to him is the carryover from the playbook. Because Josh McDaniel system is something that Nick Kaye has borrowed heavily from. His Patriots roots, they run deep. And the branches, they go all the way from New England to Houston, Texas. And that's something now with a Patriots receiver, someone that caught six touchdowns last year, it's uh going to help them, I believe, because he knows the system, he knows the verbiage, and he knows what Nick Haley wants to run. So, he played for a Bill Bich and a Mike Vrabel, and then they move on. They didn't foresee this big role for him. As you guys know, they added AJ Brown and Romeo Dobs, very accomplished receivers, and they like what they've seen from Kyle Williams. Where that left Kahan is as an odd man out. And it's no secret that Mike Vrabel hasn't really had really been enamored of the Bill Bich personnel and he wants to put in his own guys, whether they were with him with the Titans or if they're new players that he's bringing in and putting his stamp on the organization. They still haven't paid Christian Gonzalez. So with this being a contract year, it's a pivotal year for Kan. And like I said, we'll hear from Kahan. But you know, thinking about this offense and what he'll bring to the table, that was my first question to him. And he says he'll bring big playmaking ability, short routes, seven routes, deep routes, goal line stuff. And he says that the process with CJ, it's going well. He called it great. And it doesn't feel like the chemistry is that tough, as I said. So that's something and they have the carryover. One thing that I really felt like uh wanted to hear from him. There were comments from Mike Varel that kind of gotten circled, underlined, put in red ink. And Mike, as he always will, he's a bluntspoken, tell like it is type. And I didn't think that he was being disrespectful at all to Kan Booty. I mean, he took it that way. I didn't take it that way. I took it as a nuance thing. He said that he would have been inactive. Okay. You could still, if you're a receiver, take that as a little bit of motivational fuel. So, I specifically asked Kan about that. We'll hear from him in a moment on that topic. But he said that, you know, they were not going to, you know, have that role for him, but he said, you know, sadly, use the word sadly with it being a contract year, he wants that bigger role. And he did handle the whole trade process with maturity. He didn't make waves. He asked for a trade, politely requested it through his agent, Drew Rosenhouse, and eventually it was accommodated in exchange for some good, you know, a good player in Jaylen Reed and of course for a, you know, late round draft pick. So you look at what he's done. He said, "Hey, Vable spoke his truth." And they move forward. Fair enough. Absolutely. So, let's hear from him now on that topic and a little bit about him building the timing, building the chemistry with Texans quarterback CJ Stout and much more. We're going to also talk about and hear from Texans coach Demo Ryan's. So, uh, keep it locked. I've got a lot more to say, a lot more insight onto what I anticipate from his role. In fact, why bury the lead? I I'll tell you right now. I think the starting receivers possibly for the first game that you've got, of course, Nico Collins, the Pro Bowl wide receiver, and then you've got Jaylen Null, Xavier Hutchinson, and there's still a chance that he can ascend to that number two receiver role, but they're not going to just hand it to him. So, if they feel good about it, how these practices are going, sure, they won't hesitate. But with this being his first game against the Buffalo Bills for the Texans, he plays the Bills twice a year when he's with the Patriots. Just uh would temper the expectations. I think they'll have a specific vision for him with a bunch of plays that are really tailored to him. Jump ball, deep ball, some short stuff, but they're not going to just have this entire route tree and build the whole game plan around him. Remember, it's about Nico Collins. It's about Dalton Schultz. It's going to be about throwing to the backs and handing off to the backs. David McGomery, Woody Marks. So, this offense, they already kind of had, you know, a direction, but they felt a need for a big play guy. And remember, he had six touchdowns last year, the exact same amount as Jaden Higgins. So, let's hear from Kan Booty. It's Booty, not Bout. He is not Kinjun per se, at least in his pronunciation, but he is from Newir, Louisiana. and doesn't have like a thick from the boot type accent. Definitely loves playing here and being with Derek Stingley Jr. again. So, that's something that's pretty cool for him. Neil Hunter, another LSU guy. I think we only lost one guy to a waiver claim and guys also had the decision to go other places which is you know their choice but for us to get a lot of our young guys back I'm very happy about that because we continue to we get the opportunity to continue to work with them and continue to develop them and that's what they need they need that growth they need that development they need that time of being in the same system hearing the same verbiage they need that for a year so they can see the growth >> what does it say about you and your coaching staff that they will reject other other offers from other teams to come back here. >> We're a good salesman and the fact that you guys were able to bring him back and and how close is he to being able to contribute? >> Yeah, Brevin is very close. We expect Brevin to be out practicing next week. So, Brevin Brevin is definitely close. Uh, love Brevin. Ever since the first time I got here, I always speak highly of Brevin just because of the the joy that he brings, type of person that he is. Just love being around him. Love the worker that he is. He has he's had some unfortunate things happen when it comes to injury-wise, but man, there's no one with a better attitude and how you attack a day than Brevin Jordan. And when he gets the football in his hand, I'm still thinking of the Cleveland Browns game. When he catches a short pass and he houses it down the sideline, it's like that's the Brevin that I remember and that always sticks with me like can we find a way to get the ball in Brevin Jordan's hands? He's going to make a play with it. So, I'm always pulling for Brevin and I was happy to get him back on our team. >> Like um to follow up on Brevin and T to a similar extent, um it seemed like when guys suffer catastrophic injuries, you guys are fairly patient with them and giving them grace to have the the the time to come back. Some teams, some situations, you're not ready to play, they move on and just kind of kick them to the curve. It seemed like you guys have created this environment to where if a guy suffers a catastrophic injury, especially a younger guy, you guys tend to be patient. Where where does that um I guess approach come from? >> There's no one that hurts more for a guy that when he suffers a catastrophic injury than myself. I've been there. I've had those injuries that your season is over. It's tough to get back. So, I've been there. I've been in those guys shoes. So I understand that how everybody just kind of leaves you to the side, forgets about you. It's a it's a lonely lonely moment as a lonely process of working yourself back. So for me, always have a heart for those guys. I'm always going to give those guys the time that they need to recover. And I think it's only right because here in Houston, we truly care about our our guys, right? And care about them getting back on the field if that happens. If not, still want those guys to be great young men. How can I find a way to impact them in another way? Right? And they can still be impactful outside of football if you don't come back from the injury because every injury happens. You're never going to be the same as you once were, right? It's going to look a little different when you have injuries. And guys just have to understand that. And I'm here to support all of our guys who go through the most difficult time in their life of not having football due to injuries. So, I'm going to stick with them and support them as best as I can. Going back to the process of the 53, what's the biggest difference in attacking that year four versus year one when I'm sure it was probably even more overwhelming than it is now? >> The attacking the 53 is is for me it's not overwhelming. It's just it's a it's a process like anything else, right? And it always still comes down to a handful of guys at the end that hasn't changed, right? It's always comes down to three, four, five guys you got to make a decision on. And there are some tough decisions to make every year, right? And it's been that way for me ever since I've been in this position. Tough decisions to make this year. Again, I want to keep everybody. Can we increase the roster so we can have more players? That would be a great thing for everyone around the league. But it's uh you know, these guys we we've get guys who are made of the right stuff. And if they don't make it here, I'm very confident these guys will go and impact another organization in a big way. What do you think about the rivalry uniforms? >> The rivalry uniforms. Everybody loves them, huh? Coach loves them, too. They're sweet, man. They're really nice. I think a lot of work went into designing the uniforms. A lot of thought went into it. Just making it, you know, Houston. And that's the that's the cool part about it, right? Seeing Houston, my wife gives me a hard time always on the Houston blue. I didn't understand it, but now I understand how important the Houston Blue is and uh what it means to the city. So, I mean, they're really, really cool uniforms. I'm pretty sure those the best rivalry uniforms that have came out to date. And so, great job. Great job, Houston. And I'm just, you know, it just gives you more pride for your city, for the team to see everybody excited about the uniforms come out. My kids are, they were crushing me on like, "Daddy, have you seen the uniforms? have you seen them? Like, no, I have not seen them. They didn't show me. I didn't I didn't get a sneak peek, but my kids were fired up about them. And so, we was able to give them a little gear, so they're they're fired up. >> Your wife's from Houston, right? >> She is from Houston. She is from Houston. So, those uniforms mean a lot. So, thankful that we were able to execute it in a really great manner. All right. Appreciate it, guys. Thank you. Anderson coming off the edge. title: Analyzing the Minnesota Vikings Initial 53-Man Roster
text: The Minnesota Vikings roster is set for the 2026 season as kickoff is just days away. I'm Tatum Everett inside TCO Studios alongside voice of the Vikings Paul Allen and Vikings radio analyst Pete Bercich. And we're here to break it all down. Several moves being made by new general manager Nolan Teasley. He sat down and spoke to the media about his overall roster philosophy. >> There's no finish line. It never stops and this is another example of that. So, this is just really us trying to establish a landscape an initial iteration of the Minnesota Vikings for this season and then we're going to continue to to build as often as possible to to try to combine the the you know, league talent to to build a uh a deep talented roster as as as as much as we can. Um We really view this as 70 over over 53. Um And so, we use some roster mechanisms that and some tools in our toolbox to you know, to to again to to build that um that holistic roster that we we believe can be competitive in this in this league and that's always the goal. >> All right. Well, Nolan taking over on June 1st. Guys, I wanted to ask you a little bit about what you took away from the presser as far as his roster building philosophy goes. Paul. >> Right. It you know, to to look at the active roster at 53 and then the practice squad at 17, we get to 70 as a collective unit. And it just triggers the the the reality that the practice squad for NFL teams has changed so much since Pete played and coached and actually was on a practice squad. >> was on the practice squad in 1994 and there were six of us, right? There were only six guys and you you had to be a year zero guy or a rookie. You couldn't have any experience cuz once you did, you were no longer available. >> Yeah. >> It's amazing to see how the NFL we've added games, we're adding international games, they want to go to 18. So, they're expanding the season side of it. They're also allowing the teams to expand kind of the personnel base cuz the teams know if we're going to play 18 games, we're going to play 17 games, we need more bodies. >> Right. >> And so, the practice squad is no longer just a place to park young guys who might need a year or two to develop. This is a way to bring in veterans to get them ready to play that to bring in anyone that you want to look and have and and take a good hands-on view of. So, as GMs evolve, as the practice squad evolves, the rules evolve, it's all about who manages this process the best. And it was very interesting to hear Nolan talk about that and how he views it because that landscape has changed dramatically over the last 15 years. >> Yes, he may be short and sweet, but he is to the point and you can glean a lot of his overall views from what he said. He also talked about Kyler Murray and that debut will happen against the Packers on September 13th. When they take the field and they unveil this offense we haven't really seen just quite yet, Paul, what do you expect to see from number one? >> Well, it's it's an interesting question and here's why because in fairness, when calling Vikings-Arizona games, okay, whether it's Flores defense, Donatell's or whatever, I mean, Kyler had some success but would lose the game. So, not having been around him or watched him as closely as I have a training camp and in the joint practices, that's really like a lot of people what I knew about Kyler is he'll run around you, he can throw over you, but he's not winning the games in a team sport, I understand. Having watched him all summer, I just I cannot possibly share how excited I am to watch him play the role here because I know you're going to talk about the running game coming up here in a little bit, but in my 25 years of calling Vikings football, I've never been next to somebody who legitimately runs the way he runs, and it's a threat. It's a legitimate threat. And he's never worked with anybody like Justin. He's never worked with anybody like Christian Darrisaw. So, I've kind of gone from uh, you know, what do we have here? What exactly do we have here? I'm not sure. To I can't wait to watch him play. >> Yeah, I think we What we do know about Kyler Murray is exactly that he's an unbelievable athlete. He's also a very accurate passer, and he has a very good short passing game. Those are his strengths that he's brought over from Arizona. I think part of the key to his whole thing is knowing that he It's not him. Arizona, he was the guy. He comes to Minnesota, he has tools all around him. This is where the running game, I'm just anxious to see that, too. Uh, because the ability to hand the ball off and have a defense have to make accommodations, have to respect the run, is going to open up so much more for him in the passing game. So, the stars that are around him, uh, that That's a pressure that's not on him. But, that pressure to win, to win playoff games, to get to the postseason, yeah, that's what everybody wants to see. And I think it's it's all I know this. Guys who are as talented as he is, it's he'll be as good as he wants to be. If he really wants to turn things around and get that next contract and be, you know, just resurrect his career in a way I for lack of a better way of saying it, uh, I think he can do that absolutely here, and I can't wait to see him go about his business. >> But, when you're the first overall pick in the draft, and then you win the Rookie of the Year, and and you are charged with carrying this whole thing for 7 years or whatever it was. But, when you get here and you're surrounded by the coaching staff and the players, you know, I'm not saying, you know, like like a racehorse that came from the farm after being good and now all of a sudden is counted on to do different things and has to be broken, but that they're that's pressure on Kyler to change. I have to adapt to all I've known. And to talk to people about how well he's done with it and kind of his will versus the will or he the will that he knows versus the will of what wins here. To see that come together over the course of two or three months, I've seen a lot over a lot of years. I've never seen anything like that and I'm just super excited for what's next. >> He doesn't have to just wake up and look out the window to realize he's in a different state and an entirely different type of team, right? As soon as he walks into this facility. >> We're excited. >> The whole front office, the coaching staff, I mean, the way this this franchise operates, he he he's he's absolutely thrilled. >> Like for lack of a better description, it's almost like a sense of giddiness because you're like, okay, I just want to see >> Yes. >> what it's going to look like. >> And one other Viking ready to make his debut, he's probably pretty giddy about that, is fullback C.J. Ham, who was the Viking's fifth-round draft pick this season. You see C.J. Ham retire, you're not sure what will happen with that position and now you have a starting fullback making the roster with no doubts whatsoever. What have you observed from C.J. Ham and how this team will use him? >> Well, um he's very physical and he really enjoys the contact of mashing on man and not everybody is is made that way. But, um Pete and I have talked about this several times. There was a little snapshot in the Giants preseason game. Very first drive, you got the first Minnesota Moving Company Darrisaw over to O'Neill. You had everybody but Jefferson. Bradison's in the game, so is Juwan Jennings. Aaron Jones had like a 17-18 yard run. The in this day and age, you can't show the choice plays in training camp because people are taking video and putting it on social media. So, whatever little snapshot you get, you have to know what you're looking for. On that 54-yard driver, they got points. 44 came on the ground. And there were probably 1 2 3 4 running plays that we're going to see during the season that were really good. Breida's had a lot to do with it. >> Yeah, he absolutely did. And and as a his brothers played football. Uh one of his brothers still plays football, I believe with Baltimore. Buccaneers. Buccaneers. I'm sorry. The Buccaneers. Yeah. Um he was a walk-on at the University of Michigan. You know, the whole his whole story is one of just overcoming adversity. And that's why he's tough. That's why he loves to hit and it makes sense when you see him. His ability though to insert himself in an offense and what he's doing is complex. It may seem like all he does is run through brick walls. No, he's got the motions. He's got the shifts. He's got a lot of mental that H-back {slash} tight end {slash} fullback position is very very important with pass protection and all the running game and everything else. There's a lot for him to think about. He's absolutely embraced that. >> Yep. >> And being that he's a fullback, the first play of his NFL career, you don't have to throw him the ball or hand him the ball. You just say, all right, first play we're going to run lead iso. >> That thing's going to open up and you just knock the cobwebs out and all the all all you know, all the bubble guts and everything out >> That's so great. >> go run that guy over and then play two. Well, we'll consider maybe a dive or something. >> [laughter] >> Well, it's time to talk the defensive side of things. The Vikings making a move uh between the deadline a couple of days ago. They signed veteran Kyle Van Noy, a linebacker who everyone's pretty excited to add, especially GM Nolan Teasley who said that the way that he rushes is the way that the Vikings rush. And that they're very lucky to have a caliber of a player signed to this roster, you know, just before we get going. Now, he is on the practice squad as of right now. Uh what do you expect about the impact? I mean, to get weaned in, you know. >> For sure. Knock off the cobwebs. >> In fact >> Just have Breida's hit >> and he'll be ready game two. >> Uh yeah, but but having Kyle Van Noy as a part of part of this disruptor uh that that I mean he's experience with Brian Flores is awesome, too. Pete, what do you like about him? >> Um he is he's the Jonathan Gernard type of a guy and and I want to build this in this way. >> [clears throat] >> Um just more yeah, just physical, more of a defensive end than say an outside linebacker. Early on in training camp uh Brian Flores talked about Dallas Turner and Jonathan Gernard and said they're not the same guy. Right? They're not the same player. They're going to And that was to me I was like, "Fantastic." They're you know, use use Turner to his strengths. Van Noy is Jonathan Gernard. He's physical. He can wreck things. He can run the inside stunts on on the offensive line. That's where I think he you know, he's going to fit. He had unbelievable success in 2024. He's a two-time Super Bowl winner. Went to the Pro Bowl two seasons ago. Last year played a lot. May not have put up put up the numbers per se, uh but he's familiar with Flores. He brings that attitude, that physicality. He's exactly the type of guy that I would see Flores, Teasley, uh Coach O'Connell wanting in this building. I mean, the guy is 35 and he's on the practice squad and he's like, "Yep, let's do it. Let's go." And you know and you >> I saw him at lunch. He looks ready to go. I did not I I know. He was just ready to go. >> Once he has played all his games and it's prudent, right? To get him just to get him going. I who knows how he's been working out. I'm sure he's in perfect shape, but it's a prudent thing to do and and I expect him as the season goes on, he will be more and more part of this defense. >> And and your edge rushers for Brian Flores' defense are obviously so important. That that's why Van Ginkel has all of these touchdowns. Too bad for Tyler Badie who tore his ACL at Denver. And this This no slight at all on Ty Ingram Dawkins, who's going to play that role sometimes, too. But, the team from a pa- true veteran pass-rushing standpoint is better right now than it was a couple of days ago. >> And when you think about the pass rush, and you add the fact that Dallas Turner is going into year three, what excites you about his emergence in this defense? >> Well, it's when people say that he was unblockable during the Ravens joint practices, the majority of it comes from the Raven side, where they were like, "Hey, we knew you hit on one, but wow, holy cow." And then you watch it, and it's just different. I don't know what he's done this off-season, but he's naturally growing up. I think he's 23 years of age. Uh but this that's another exciting uh component of what should be an exciting season is with Dallas, how real is this when we start playing games? >> Yeah, you can If you want to take an elite athlete and turn him into an average athlete down the field, you just give him too much to think about. Right? So, Dallas Turner comes into here, who played about half the time at Alabama. He wasn't on the field all the time. Very simple schematically, comes here to this. Wow, holy cow, everything's changing, right? They had him off-the-ball linebacker, remember, his rookie year against Detroit. He played off the ball. So, they got him in his spot. Now, the game has slowed down, and you're seeing it you're seeing it on the field. >> The sack against the Giants, I know it was pre-season, but that proves to me he's turned the corner in that the blitz came from up and underneath, and he knew when the pressure's coming from the middle, I just keep contain. When they flush the quarterback, I just come off and make the sack. That's productivity. Well, at the end of the year, you don't say, "Well, that one was a lay-down sack, and that one was it." No, you got 15, 20 And he led the team in sacks last year, by the way. He got 15, 20, whatever sacks, then you got him. Who cares how you get him? But it's just the the caginess is starting to show up in his game, and I think that is what's going to take him. And I think this defense will be as good as offenses need to accommodate for Dallas Turner. If he becomes a guy where they have to start game planning for him, counting for him, turning the protection his way, look out. >> Yeah, if I'm an offensive coordinator, I still double Andrew Van Ginkel. I mean, I don't, you know, at 31 years of age or whatever he is, I just don't want people to forget [music] what we got from Andrew Van Ginkel when he was healthy. It's It was nearly an historical season in a lot of different ways, and he wasn't healthy last year. Super healthy now. If I'm an offensive coordinator, I got to double Gank to make 15 show me it's real, and he should do that in short order. >> Well, the defense expects to also get some impact from younger players. There are quite a few rookies on the roster this year, both in the trenches and out in space for these Vikings. Defensive linemen Caleb Banks and Dominique Orange, linebacker Jake Golday, safeties Jaylen Jones and Josh Metellus, and corner Charles Davis or Chuck D as everyone likes to call him. So, Caleb Banks is going to play quite a bit. Dominique Orange, after going back and kind of rewatching him, wow. >> Dominique Orange is If you turned on his film from Iowa State to where he is today, he has improved immensely, and he's going to get a lot of snaps. You got to replace, you know, all the Jonathan Allen snaps. There's a lot there that you have to do. So, those two guys, side by side, pushing each other. Jake Golday will be the next man up. So, no matter what of the four linebackers I think goes down, I think they'll if they have a week to get him ready, Golday will be in there, so I think you're going to see a lot of him. Uh and then Charles Dimings could start against Green Bay. So, uh those four you're going to see quite a bit of and I'm uh I'm very excited. I have I got to be patient, right? You got to you can't fly off the handle. You got to be patient. >> But, yes. Well, especially with the D-linemen. >> Payton picked four, so why don't you try one of them? >> mine's easy because um I know what he's talking about with 97. Uh and there were moments during the Ravens joint and I reference those a lot because those two days were every bit as important as every minute of every preseason game we just watched. And uh the the Ravens first-round guard uh Ya- Ya- Ya-noni? >> I Yeah, Ione. >> Yeah, Ione. Okay, they're really high on him. He's going to start. He's probably going to play a lot. I mean, Dominic Orange threw him around no fewer than five times and and just caught him off guard one time and buried him. So, that kind of opened the eyes right there. Uh but, see, it's kind of like with Turner, old schooler goes to Van Ginkel and kind of just say, "Hey, let's not forget this." With citrus, I just don't want people to forget that there are some elite football minds in this building, maybe even Brian Flores, who really wanted Caleb Banks. All right? Now, Banks has played four games since 2024. Basically, his conditioning, as he said, was way down up to training camp as he recovered from a foot injury. So, now where he's not completely where he needs to be and everybody in this building knows it. And and he's going to get there. So >> And Orange and Banks are playing two completely different positions. >> Right. So there's a whole different learning curve for Caleb. >> Banks is the Caleb Williams spot, Citrus is the Pat Williams and I'm not saying Caleb's going to be Kevin Williams, but he's 6-6, a lot of deflected passes nobody wants to talk about. title: General Manager Nolan Teasley on Setting the Minnesota Vikings 53-Man Roster
text: All right. You hear me? Okay. Yeah. Um yeah, roster evolution. Um you'll hear me reference it's there's no finish line. It never stops. And this is another example of that. So this is just really us um trying to establish a landscape uh an initial iteration of the Minnesota Vikings for this season. And then we're going to continue to to build um as often as possible to to uh try to combine the the you know league talent to to build a uh a deep talented roster as as as as much as we can. Um we really view this as 70 over over 53. Um, and so we use some roster mechanisms that and some tools in our toolbox to, you know, to again to to build that um that holistic roster that we we believed can be uh competitive in this in this league and that's always the goal. Um there are some hard conversations that come through that process when you first reduce from 90 to 53. We try to handle those with care. Um KO and I sat with with each and every player during that process. Um, you try to handle those conversations again with with care, with with empathy, with appreciation and and and encouragement. Um, but then there's some positives, too, because you get to see the energy and you get to see people's dreams come true and and that really resonates with you. And um, so that's just it's it's a little bit of a roller coaster of a day, but we got through it. Um just grateful and appreciative to everybody who was involved. Um scouting, football administration, uh FQM, which is our research and analytics department, team ops. Uh shout out to KZ. I gave her a shout out yesterday, too. Um she's been uh amazing since I got here. Medical player performance, player development, and and every everybody else that's involved. It's truly a collective and a collaborative effort. um if I could just kind of take a moment um to tell you guys about like the process of acquiring a player and where it really starts. So when we acquire a player at this waiver wire, it really actually started when that player was in college, right? And we had an area scout that went to the school. Um we went through the draft process. We collected all that information and we maintained that information to to make those decisions. And then the pro department uh evaluates them through the previous season, even into this uh the previous regular regular season into this preseason and recommends that player of oh this is somebody who we might be interested in acquiring and and bringing onto our roster. Okay. and then you bring them to the coaching staff and then you you you get the coach's uh vision for that player and you talk to uh FQM and you you try to find that alignment with the data and we're really hitting those pillars and then the player comes in the building and you you have a physical and um the onboarding process with um with our with our player engagement and all that is to say everybody has a a role that allows us to build this football team and uh it started a long time ago and it's never going to stop. So with that um really excited about where we are, excited about where we're headed and uh I'll open it up to questions. >> Nolan, throughout the process of the quarterback competition, what [clears throat] did you learn about Kyler that maybe you didn't know when you were competing against him in Seattle? >> Yeah, that's a good question. Um, I think Kyler has really has really grown in his ability to to manage the line of scrimmage. I think we've seen constant improvement throughout uh throughout the preseason um throughout training camp. And again, I I've said this from the from the beginning. I'm really bullish on where he's headed in playing in this system with this level of coaching um you know, from KO to Josh Macau and everybody else on on that side of the ball. What do you do as JJ McCarthy's role right now on your role? >> JJ McCarthy's role is to continue to develop, to improve, and to support his teammates. And he's done an excellent job of that from the the moment that I've that I've been here and from my understanding since he walked through the door. >> You expect him to be on the roster for week one? >> I do. >> Is he the backup quarterback? Yeah, I wouldn't really necessarily comment on on depth immediately, but um yeah, I'm just I'm I'm pleased that he's he's part of our present version of the Minnesota Vikings and excited about his future. >> Well, just the process of bringing in Kyle Vanoi, like what what did that look like and and how do you kind of see him fitting in? >> Yeah, veteran presence at a at a premium position um fits well into the system because of the way that he rushes and the way that we rush. It's really a a team component to that, you know, from that standpoint. Then he brings again experience and leadership. So really really lucky to have a player of his caliber uh join us. >> How much did his experience with Brian Flores play into the decision? >> Uh I mean that's always a component of it, but really the at the foundation is just he's a good player. >> Kevin's talked a lot about just his communication. I think last week he mentioned talking to Harrison Smith. Do you want Harrison back for the 206 season? >> Yeah, I know that KO and him have a have a unique relationship and they they keep in touch and um I've always had a high high level of respect for the player. Um heard great things about the person. Um never met him formally, but um yeah, high level of respect of of what he's done in this league. >> Do you want him back? >> Do I want him back? >> 2026. >> I mean, that's really up to up to Harrison ultimately. and um but uh we're always open to adding good football players. >> How do you feel about the depth at safety independent of whether he decides to return or not? >> I think it's it's one of our deeper positions. You're really excited. We all saw Jacob Thomas play. It was good to see uh Jacobe Thomas come back into the into the Denver game. You know, Theo, it I can go on and on. And then Josh Matelis.
