title: ILB Jacob Rodriguez, WR Chris Bell, and QB Kyle McCord meet with the media | Miami Dolphins
text: Have you heard from him? Yes, I think it just comes with being in the NFL.  You have to be a professional and do your job, and it's good that you can build relationships with them, to see how they do it and understand why they are the best.  So you simply imitate and emulate them, and you get others to follow you.  That's why, especially with all the newcomers who arrived, we all have a very good relationship with each other.  So we'll be together on the field and we'll spend a lot of time off the field, to do things right and try to be the best we can be . Have you spoken to Zach Thomas this week ? Yes, I sent her a text message for her birthday.  I think he's a great guy and a great mentor, so I hope to see him again soon.  Did Zach know you got the job? Did he congratulate you? No, he didn't know.  He's minding his own business .  He's a busy guy.  He'll be around here soon.  He always supports me, but going back to Texas Tech and having him come to say hello and meet me was incredible. He watched a lot of videos.  How big of an appetite do you have, a voracious appetite for analyzing videos? Did you do it late at night on Tech? Yes. Yes, 100%.  I think that, especially at university, it's more like an obligation.  So you get used to it anyway.  I know that when they were talking about Zach here, he had to stay until 9 or 10 at night.  Well, fortunately we now have it on our iPads.  So we can take it home and watch it there. That's what I do, I lie down on the sofa and instead of watching a program, I watch the video, I analyze it and see what interests me. Now it's a little easier to go home, watch it, and study that way, instead of having to be here until the early hours. Jacob, I know this is a dream you've been pursuing for a long time. How does it feel? What would you say to your 10 or 12-year-old self, Jacob Eason, now that you're just days away from your NFL debut? Yes, I think he would be proud.  Uh... But what I've told myself almost all my life is that you simply have a job to do.  You keep doing it, you don't really look...I'll put it this way.  The less you see, the more you see.  You know, the more you look, the less you see.  So, both on and off the field, I think it's the same.  And if you limit your vision to what you have in hand and focus on what you must do, later in life you will be able to look back and reflect on it.  But right now, it's more about you having a job to do .  You have to keep doing it. One more, Marcel. Jacob, not only in your position, but also at running back and wide receiver, they totally opted for youth over veteran experience.  You said that this class of newbies is very close-knit.  What kind of responsibility do you feel coming here to set, I suppose, a new standard for Baltimore? Yes, I think that coming from university we are all fresh, we want to do things well and we are very close.  We want to unite and try to play the best football possible.  But , well, there's a lot of responsibility involved .  As I mentioned before, you have a job to do, you must be a professional, arrive and do the right thing ;  If you can establish a routine, maintain it, and continue doing what's necessary, you'll have no regrets.  So, if you love football and not so much what football can do for you, you're here all the time, having fun and enjoying the people around you. I think you can start having fun with this and start playing well. What would you say to Chris Bell at 8, 10, or 12 years old, now that he's just days away from making his NFL debut? Oh man.  I would just tell him, you did it, you achieved it.  I always had this dream, you know, a lot of people have that dream but don't believe in it.    I always believed I was part of the one percent and I'm proud that all my hard work paid off.  I've been doing this since I was ignored until I was finally taken into account, and I never stopped striving.  It's something that has always been with me, my effort, my work ethic and that inner fire, I love this sport.  I'm just trying , I'm happy to be back, you know what I mean?  The eight months were difficult, but as I said , it's all part of God's plan. Chris, there will be times when the team has three rookie receivers on the field, maybe also a rookie tight end, all at the same time. What do you think will be the key for you to make that work? Be focused on what the team decides in the plays, align well and execute;  We've been working hard. We continue to improve every day.  All the newbies who have been practicing have done a very good job.  I just have to be on their level.  I haven't been there in the thick of things with Malik yet, but I'm still learning and growing every day. What do you think about being one of only three rookie picks at wide receiver on the team, which is extremely rare? Wait, wait, can you repeat that? That you are one of the three rookie picks at the wide receiver position .  It's very, very rare for a team to have three rookie players in that position Mhm. When you think about that, what goes through your mind? It's something great.  They expect us to arrive and perform.  We weren't recruited for no reason.  So I'm glad they took a chance on the three of us.  And I know Caleb and Kevin have been playing incredibly well.  I just have to keep up with the team.    I know it took a lot of work to get to this point.  What would you say is the number one thing, the number one attribute, that helped you get to this exact moment? Uh, first of all, my mindset. Simply waking up every day and doing the same thing over and over again.  You know, you have to come and lift weights, even if I 'm not practicing or anything like that .  I feel that the most important thing is mindset.  You know, coming off a knee injury—well, I tore my labrum in college and it was a lot quicker than this—but, you know, you might feel like you can go out and play, but you can't, it's not the time , you know?  You just have to wait. So, I would say mindset is the first thing, you know, you have to keep working and keep believing that whatever the coaches and strength team have planned is going to work.  So yes. Let's talk about that mindset, shall we? Because you have to fight against those negative thoughts, right? Will I be able to recover? Will I be the same as before? What do you think is the most important thing to be able to persevere through this? The most important thing is God.  You know, believing in God;  It happened for a reason, but if I wasn't going to recover and be healthy, then I wouldn't be here.  And you know, like everyone used to say , it was a career-ending injury , but with the passage of time, technology and all that, you know what I mean?  It's something you can recover from.  So I try to block out the negative.  I know that negativity sometimes comes, but I block it out, I work hard, and I trust in God. How do you set statistical goals for yourself? Can you repeat that? for yourself?    I just want to have a great year, you know, do whatever it takes to help my team win right now At this stage of your career, what do you consider to be your strengths? I think my processing, being able to know what we've marked and then see what the defense is doing, and passing the ball to the right player on time, allowing the playmakers to do their job, and also my accuracy.  I think those two things really stood out in the preseason and are probably a big reason why I'm here. You've been behind good quarterbacks like Carson Wentz.  What did you learn from those experiences? Yes, I mean, obviously their playing styles are a little different, but they are both great quarterbacks.  And being a young guy, being able to be on the team with two people like that at the beginning of your career helps a lot.  And besides that, being with Tyrod in Green Bay, heading into his 16th year, I think he's a perfect example of how to do it at a high level for a long time.  So they have all helped me.  They've all been in my position before, being a young guy in the league.  So yes, I am very fortunate to be surrounded by very good players so early in my career. What are the benefits of having Kevin Petullo, with whom you worked last year in Philadelphia, on board? Yes, as soon as I got the call that he was coming here, that was one of the first things I thought of, that KP was here.  So having a familiar face on the coaching staff is huge.  And you know, similar to Malik, with some of the things we implemented on offense last year in Philadelphia, it's definitely helped.  So yes, I'm excited.  I have a very high opinion of him as a coach.  And being able to meet with him here is something very special. There are many differences between Green Bay and Miami.  Are Green Bay or Miami more about power or speed? I guess summers in Green Bay probably weren't for me, but once the cold weather arrives, I definitely prefer Miami.  I remember going there to sign last winter, I got off the plane and it was -10 degrees. So we won't have that problem here, but both are great places.  They're as different as can be, but yes, my friend. I'm excited to be here. I heard that you once led Syracuse to a surprising victory against Miami. That's how it is. What do you remember about that game? Yeah, well, that was uh probably my favorite, my favorite game of my entire college career.  Uh, being able to say goodbye like that and beat a great Miami team was a lot of fun.  So now I hope to make those same fans happy instead of upset.

That's just the the way that I read the roster right now. It's hard to ever know where they rank in terms of the 53, whether they're players 52, 53, 51, I don't know. I think they're they're pretty comfortable. And Howie Roseman said this in April the of keeping four quarterbacks. And when you're saying that in April, it's like, okay, there's a ways to go here. I expect you to say that. But as the summer wore on, and as you know, cutdowns have come and went, you know, I I I that there's a realistic possibility that they enter the season with four quarterbacks. There and I mean, there's always the option of a team offering, you know, you know, proposing a trade, but I don't know that Andy Dalton or Tanner McKee really did enough to warrant a team to want to to seek them out in a trade. And because of that, you're not able to keep maybe another maybe other players that you like. So, we'll see how it goes. I think right now it's hard to ever look at the roster as a finished product. So, I certainly trust John Schneider and Joey Lane and all of them; they're much better at this than I could ever be.  That's why I trust whatever they decide. title: Keionte Scott & Sean Murphy-Bunting on Defensive Growth | Press Conference | Tampa Bay Buccaneers
text: Good, uh, this previous ankle I've been dealing with, so it's kind of like situation where it rolls sometimes and so I'm feeling better. Trainers staff doing a good job keeping me healthy, so I feel good. >> You got through preseason with the helmet off and you got some live action. Now you're getting ready for week one of the regular season. Does it kind of set in for you yet that, "Okay, here it comes, my first NFL game?" >> Yeah, honestly, just focus, real focus on just preparing and being in the moment right now, just continuing to learn as much as I can, soak up all the game and then ultimately getting ready to, you know, play in the first game. >> Could be you see my preseason like they were double repping you, like they had whatever would get you more snaps. How much does that help you just to have that? >> Yeah. Yeah, very appreciative of that, you know, just to get the time in there to get the reps. Obviously, you know, in this league it's more so about what you see and how many times you've seen it. So, to get those reps has been super helpful for me to just slow things down and be able to, you know, have some more film time, extra film time of looking at things and seeing where I did right, where I did bad and, you know, ultimately helping me change and create and critique myself. >> Where where do you see the awareness the most clearly where you are now versus where you were like in May? >> Uh, ultimately just the small little details, you know, you come in, you know, um, you know, off of a decent year, you know, thinking thinking you're the hot shot, you know a lot and then you get into a scheme and it's it's total small small detail things. So, just focusing on those smaller detail things is my biggest thing where I'm focused on now. >> You have the ability to play multiple positions and and has looked that way. How how difficult is that? It's hard enough to be a rookie, but then now you're being told to kind of cross train. >> Yeah, ultimately just goes back to my mindset coming in, just being ready and being open to any opportunity I was given. So, I feel like, you know, in that mindset now it's just talking about, "Okay, if it's this position, what is, you know, the needs and the wants out of that position?" And just breaking all those things down and kind of just, you know, trying to break things down and slow it down for myself is the biggest thing. >> Where are you comfortable and you'd probably be going to safety, corner in order? >> Yeah, yeah, in that order, yeah. That's a good call. >> How has Todd Bowles been with you communicating and and what have you learned the most from him so far? >> Yeah, ultimately, yeah, I would say ultimately he's been a super great experience, you know, I'm I'm loving the scheme, you know, just ultimately a super big football guy. So, to get in and be at the professional level and just see how many different changes in the smaller detail things are inside of the game is just ultimately like a a big challenge for myself. So, you know, Coach Bowles has been super calm and just small little things of being able to correct and pull me to the side and be able to talk about it then. So, you know, that's just the biggest thing just building our relationship and then understanding what he wants out of the defense, what he the looks he's trying to give off and different things like that. So, just constantly communicating with him. Bucky, he's my dog. >> Do you like getting sent on those blitzes? Like when Todd is putting in there and you get told that, is that something that's you have to decide to get down there on the line? >> Yeah, that's definitely something I I prioritize in my game, especially being a DB. You know, you know, sometimes when you get sent, you know, you your guys are behind you. You know, you know, I'm holding it down. So, you know, my goal is to just get back there, try to, you know, create cause a mess, you know, just help those guys out back there, too. >> Okay, man. With the pretty heavy class with Reuben and Antoine and those guys who are lighting it up as well. What's it like to be part of that that group and how the defense and impact all you guys can make together? >> Yeah, I think that's one of the the big things we did this year is you know, all the rookies just got close. You know, rookie academy every day the vets are going home at 12:00 and we're still in here. So, we just got cool, man. So, we're just super excited for each other, you know, pushing each other's, you know, every day just continuing to get better every day. So, to see everybody in here, you know, the rookies that we have now will continue to grow as a rookie class and just push everybody to be better. >> All right. Thank you. >> Appreciate it. No problem. A lot of cameras. >> It's a familiar face. >> Look good still? How you doing? How y'all doing? Thank you. >> Obviously, you're, you know, playing history here with this team. >> And what's it like to come back in the building now and and be reunited with some some of the guys that you won the Super Bowl with? >> Yeah, there's a there's a handful. Um so, I was able to see them, say what's up. It was cool. Um obviously, they embraced me well and um and that goes for everybody in here. They embraced me well, coaches. Um familiar faces with the coaches, too. So, it feels uh feels comfortable. Feels home. It feels right. So, we're just going to, you know, stick to what I can do what I can and, you know, be ready and available for whatever the team needs. >> When you talked to Jason Licht, he mentioned this is, you know, coming back here is something that you wanted to do. >> Mhm. >> What was the process like coming back here to Tampa? >> Um honestly, the process was pretty pretty seamless. Uh you know, when I was speaking with my agent as far as, you know, destinations and places to go, um Tampa was really I I want to say first on my list, but um well, it was, so I'm saying it anyway, but But, um you know, just like like you said, uh just being familiar, uh knowing the staff, knowing some of the players, um knowing the culture and what and what it brings, um and knowing the standard that, you know, wearing a this logo on this uniform, the the standard that it holds. So, um it means a lot to me, a lot to my heart. Um and so, yeah, I'm here and like I said, I'm happy to be here. I'm blessed to be here. Um and whatever situation that is and, you know, I'm looking forward to the season and and forward to what I can do to help, you know, however they may need it. >> What was that first conversation like with uh with coach Bowles? What did he express to you? >> Uh he he started off saying, "What's up, old man?" So, I said it back to him cuz, you know, we've both been I guess we've both been pretty pretty old in this league, but um you know, it it was really natural. It felt like we picked up conversation from the last time we spoke. Um nothing was forced. Um you know, he talked about, you know, how good this team is and how how good of a position they're in and and the players that they have, um and how I can just be, you know, a part of uh of the of the puzzle. So, I think the the first conversation obviously went well, um but again, it was very natural, very seamless. Um and that's the same with Jason and and same with everybody that the relationships that I built here, um obviously are still going strong. So, um that's obviously a test to them bringing me in and that's a test to, you know, just myself of just being the person that I am all the time, you know, nothing's ever changed no matter the circumstance or the situation. So, um like I said, blessed for those people in my corner and and blessed to be a part of, you know, this this program. Yeah. I'm a DB. So, however you take that as, that's that's that's what I am. But, um you know, I I I I feel like I can play pretty much anywhere in the secondary. Um I'm obviously most comfortable, you know, being closer to the line of scrimmage. So, corner, nickel. Um but, I did play a bit of safety in the in the role where I was in Arizona. So, um like I said, whatever they need, I feel like I can do. Yeah. Yeah, absolutely. Um when I came in, there was Carlton Davis, MJ Stewart, uh Vernon Hargreaves. So, different obviously learning from those guys in that position. Um Carlton obviously was a big reason and and and mentor for me, too. Um just meshing. Same with Vernon, the same with MJ. You know, everybody kind of gives you their their uh two cents in in in many different ways. So, um it was cool, you know, coming back obviously being around Zay. My locker's back right back next to Zay. So, uh you know, he was he was one of my young guys. So, it's just been pretty cool to be, you know, around him again and they're a really young room. So, um however I can, you know, kind of give my two cents in in I've played in different systems. I've been around different teams. Um I've been in this system. I've had success in this system. Um and everybody's had failures as well. So, I feel like I've dealt with a lot, you know, given the situation that I've been in. So, I told them uh earlier today, however I can help them in that mindset of as far as being, you know, mentally strong for or physically strong for, whatever it may be. I'm just I'm I'm I'm a conversation away. >> You went on an historic run >> at DB through the playoffs. Three interceptions, very few players ever have to that. Take us back to that that time >> the ball was finding you and and the biggest moments of the biggest games. >> [snorts] >> What was that like? >> Man, you taking it back, huh? Uh Yeah, it's been a while since I've been down memory lane. Uh I mean, you know, from from what I remember, you know, I think as far as just our mentality was in the secondary, right? Uh you had Bruce Arians who challenged us every day. Um he didn't really let us be complacent, same with Bowles, and so we took that mentality every day and we took it from here to the field. So, um I feel like when I got out there, and obviously just feeding off the guys that I played with, all of us were were pretty talented. And so, we didn't or never wanted to be a weak link. Not me, not Dean, not Carlton, so um just having that mindset every time you step on the field, I guess that's what really put me in a position to be successful. Um obviously Bowles calling the plays that he called. Um but just us as players and knowing how he wants it to be played and and how we need to play it. Um and and and what the guys were looking for as far as uh you know, concepts and passes, I just I felt like you know, I was just being a player. And so, that that's really how I got it. Obviously, the the ball found me, I found the ball, the pass rush got there every time, and so it we just it all worked it uh at the right time that it needed to. >> Just kind of a couple more questions about relishing that opportunity to be that older elder statesman in that in that in that DB room, just kind of mentoring the young guys. >> Yeah, I mean, um you know, I've been like I said, I was in a room with some young guys in Arizona. Um I was in a room with some young guys in Tennessee. So, um obviously, this is a lot different cuz I've been here before. Um but yeah, I mean, the mentality stays the same, you know, you always got to stay prepared and stay ready for any opportunity. Um and at the same time though, you want your guys to know that they can lean on you in any situation they need. Uh especially as young guys, you want to be able to have a older guy that you can kind of count on and lean on and be able to talk to things about that you don't necessarily want to talk to a coach about if if that's the case. Uh then as far as, you know, the playbook and everything goes, I've I've played in a system. Um it's going to take a couple days to just get back familiar with it, but um looking to put my standpoint on and and blueprint on that. However, like I said, they need. Um, so you know, I'm I I told them guys earlier, I'm I'm an open book. Uh, conversation, technique, anything that you want to work on on the side, I'm I'm there for. Um, cuz I'm always working and I'm always competing. So, I want to push every guy in that room, you know, to be doing the same and have that same mentality. Um, and just continue to just be a pro and be be a you know, exceptional about it. So. >> What do you think is the biggest thing you've learned, either physically or mentally, from your at the end of your first stint in Vegas or where you are now? >> The biggest thing that I've learned physically and mentally? >> Or mentally? I mean, um you know, I feel like when you play DB, you got to have a uh a next play mentality all the time. And I know guys talk about it all the time, but it's a real thing. Um, confidence. You got to always have that confidence staying high. Um, because the moment your confidence goes down, your play can go down as well just because of that. So, um, you know, I've been real uh, deliberate on you know, where I put my energy, where I put my time, my focus. Um I'm a dad now, you know, so that's different too. You know, I wasn't I wasn't back then, so uh, a lot of things have changed in that aspect of it, but man, I'm I'm so blessed and so proud to be where I am. Um just being present, being where my foot is, and it's been a while since I even done media. So, just being in front of these cameras means a lot to me. Um, talking to you guys, familiar faces that I've seen over the years, so um, yeah, I'm appreciative of the opportunity and I'm blessed to be here, and however I can help this team, I will. So. >> All right, thank you, Damon. >> Appreciate y'all. Thank you. Thank you.

title: Todd Bowles on Understanding the System | Press Conference | Tampa Bay Buccaneers
text: Afternoon. >> I ask you this too early every year, but how how close you being captain? >> Uh, Monday. >> Do you know will you go Monday practice Tuesday off next week like a normal week? >> Yes, >> that's the plan. You It was a while there where you guys had guys that were even third year in practice squad. Now, I think everybody on this the 17 on the practice squad are here from the beginning of last year or or less. Was there an effort to to keep it kind of fresh, if you will, and and churn out some of those depth spots? >> Well, you want to try to keep it fresh, but at the same time, you know, everybody's playing with the same guys. They understand that they got to go out and run a little bit and do some of those things while they take it easy cuz when we come back, it's time to go. And some of them will watch film and get a head start like they have this week. And those are pretty much leisure things. Other than that, they have their time off. Todd, it seems like every practice you're over on the sideline kind of just sharing a story with Danny, having a laugh with him, aside from his football IQ, what has his energy done to just what has it brought to the coach's room? >> I think Danny shares more stories with me than I do with him. Danny, I might get a if and or a butt in there, but Danny Danny kind of takes control of that conversation, but they have been outstanding. He he has so much football knowledge, not just special teams all the way around. and you know he worked with coach Gibbs as well and I played for coach Gibbs so we have a lot of stories to share that way but his knowledge of the game and how he sees players and how he can use players and just how he can help players has has been outstanding. It's been an uplift in the special teams room and very happy we got him. >> How many games can a good special teams unit win for you sometimes? >> Three to four. Todd, we saw Benjamin Morris get active there the late into, you know, training camp, the joint practice with the Jaguars. How confident are you in his full availability to begin the season? >> He's healthy, so that's that's a good thing. He's healthy right now. You got to stay healthy, obviously. So, you know, but that's a good thing. He played special teams and he played defense last game for a half, so that was very encouraging. He looks fresh, knock on wood, that he stays that way and, you know, he gets time at the position and he gets the rust off of him. ain't going to really help us. >> Since you came here in in 2019, uh, your defense, they've always been among the leaders in in in blitz percentage, you know, number of blitzes, blitz percentage. Is that part of your DNA or could that change depending on whether you feel you can get the rush with with four? >> It can definitely change and hopefully it can and it will change. You know, if we can get there with four, that allows us to do a lot of things coverage-wise. you have it in your back pocket if you need it, but hopefully if the four guys are humming, I don't need it. >> Was that sort of your idea going into the that Super Bowl game against the Chiefs where you didn't really blitz inordinately? >> If if you looked at the first quarter, we showed about three or four of them and they were kind of from a different angle where you couldn't tell we were blitzing, but we showed it. And then once you show it, the threat of the blitz is more dangerous than the blitz itself. So, I mean, the Super Bowl game was a while ago, but those guys started humming up front and I didn't have to. >> Okay. Thank you.

title: Jalon Daniels & Caden Fordham: Ready to Work | Press Conference | Tampa Bay Buccaneers
text: What's good y'all? What's up? >> Feels great. I mean, blessing. Um, great great like I continue to keep saying, great to be here. Great to be a part of the Buccaneers organization and look forward to being able to continue to keep getting better here. >> How was the communication from Zack Robinson and Todd of going through that process of competing for the Q12 job and eventually? Yeah, I mean, um, just being able to to be able to see the growth, being able to, you know, very big on not trying to be able make the same mistake twice. And I think that that's something that I harp on a lot. Um, once I'm coached about doing something, I try my best to not be able to try to make that same mistake. And, um, I think that's what continues to allow me to be able to keep growing within offense. >> How much more does that already I mean, uh, you got to love that. Honestly, as as especially for a UDFA guy, um, like I've been saying since since getting here, this this coaching staff has done nothing but show me love since since getting here. And, um, that that goes not just with being able to help me be able to pick up the offense, be able to get acclimated to the NFL, but um, I think that their coaching on me has continued to be able to help me grow in a lot of different aspects. And, um, I'm truly grateful for that. >> Was it feeling like leaving that meeting knowing you are this? >> Great. like like I keep saying, it's truly a blessing. Um, but I know that this is just the beginning. I know that there's still a lot of work to be done and um though I was be I was able to be now QB2, I know that there's still a lot a lot more that I need to be able to improve on, especially um if I want to keep on being able to get better. >> How impactful was Chandler Weber with you and your development and what were some things that he wanted you to work on just arriving in Tampa? truly truly impactful. Um, when it comes to being able to work on footwork, when it comes to be to being able to to understand little different things within the the within the offense, you know, he's always been someone who says like if you have a question, ask those questions. And I'm someone who wants to ask every single question there is, even if I'm getting those scout team reps for the for our defense. Like even today in practice, I was able to ask Coach Fitz about, "All right, bet. When do you want this motion sent? Like, what type of progression you want me to go through?" I'm someone who is very big on asking those questions because if you don't ask those questions, closed mouths don't get fed. >> Where were you when you got the call or learned and who who was your first phone call? >> Uh, not going to lie, [laughter] I finished the team run and Tess Johnson was the first person to tell me. So, um, after that, I I kind of made that call to my mom, made that call to my pops, and I was like, "Hey guys, I don't know if you guys know." And they like, "Yeah, we just seen it." I was like, "Yeah, >> you were the last find out." >> Almost. [laughter] Almost. You're at UVFA and Ken Forum and a guard also made the team. You guys kind of talked about how cool it was to go from that spot and to be where you guys are. >> Absolutely. I mean to be able to come in rookie mini camp with those guys. Um we've continued to to keep our heads down and continue to keep working and that's something that you know me and AG have communicated about. Especially Kay Forom, we've been somebody we've been close since we've gotten here. Being able to hang out with those guys outside the building. I think that within this game of football, you have to be able to know that person more than just the athlete. And I think that with this group of rookies, we've been able to do a a good amount of that. >> Is that just what you have to do as a UDF? Just keep your head down knowing that tomorrow kind of isn't guaranteed for, you know, summer. >> Um, I think that that's something you have to do in this game in general. Like that's just more than just being a UDFA. I think if you're a draft pick, um, you still have to be able to come in with that chip on your shoulder and be able to be ready to work with your head down because at the end of the day, it's the NFL. Um, you have to be ready to compete no matter what day it is. It could be the beginning, the end of the season, middle of the season. You have to be able to be able to go out there and be able to compete when your number's called. They said after the Jets game, you were out there and the way you performed, they kind of figured that, you know, you could be our number two. Did you have that feeling, too? Was it was a game very important? >> Um, I I don't look too much into that. I I know that I'm I I like to be able to stay where my feet are. Um, every, like I keep saying, every single play that coach Zro calls, I treat it like it's the greatest play ever because it's another down of football that I'm able to get to play. So, um, being named QB2 is great because I get the chance to be able to continue to keep playing football at this level. >> How much have you leaned on Baker and is a relationship like with him? >> I've leaned on him a lot. Um he's also somebody when I have a question, he has no problem with answering it. And if he does not have the answer at the time, he's going to be able to do everything that he can to be able to give me that answer. And um when we're talking [laughter] when we're talking about football, um on the field, if I have a question about a play where I need more understanding on a read, more understanding on a progression, or more understanding just protection wise, he's someone who I'm able to lean into and he's able to give me those answers. you all started to really like grow in your relationship like, "Hey, it's it's us, you know, like let's get going. Let's start this thing." >> Um, I mean, yeah, I think that's something that we've been able to continue to keep growing on. Um, it's not like we didn't talk at all when I first got here. We've continued to be able to grow that relationship since I've got here in Tampa. >> It's been a while since the Kansas >> a lot. Coach Lipold, Coach Z, Coach Sleeve. Um, that they were one of the first people who I who hit my phone up through text message when I was able to look at my phone afterwards. >> Jaylen, there's another rookie with you, Ted Hurst, and you got to work with them a little bit there in camp and then he got a lot of work with the ones. What do you think Bugs fans are getting with a guy like first? >> You have a guy who's explosive. He's going to go out there and make plays. Uh, not scared to be able to go out there and stick his nose into a block and he's also going to be able to go up there and make those one-on-one plays. I mean, you guys have gotten a chance to be able to see those clips in practice and um hopefully you guys are going to be able to see that in a game soon. >> Appreciate y'all. Go >> Bucks. on the team, man. >> Yeah, first I'd like to just give the glory to God. You know, it wouldn't be possible without him and then also my family. You know, I'm so grateful for everything they've done for me throughout this journey and I just couldn't be more blessed. You know, it's been a dream of mine since I was young and just putting in the work, you know, every day coming off injuries, you know, just knowing at the end of the day the good Lord's got me and he's got a plan for me and being able to see it come into action now. I'm very blessed and excited for the opportunity. >> How much do you think special? >> Yeah, a lot. I mean, that's that's pretty much one of the reasons I believe I'm here, you know, and whatever this team needs me to do, that's what I'm going to do. And I I'm excited to go out there and play on special teams. Whatever they want me to do, I'm going to do it. Yeah, I mean, you know, I always have a crazy belief in myself. That's something I believe you have to do as a player if you want to make it at this level. But, uh, I would say coming off of that last break after OTAAS, really getting that time to, you know, kind of dive into the playbook and and learn stuff. And it it started to slow down for me when I came back, I could I could tell when I was out there on the field, you know, and I started to play faster and really really gain that confidence back to be a ball player on this team. and and I started to see some things coming to fruition and I just kept believing and kept showing up every day and being the same guy and and I believe it helped me. >> Find out by the absence of the call everybody else getting when did you know? >> Yeah. Um really after the cut date uh or cut time uh Duke text me like 30 minutes after and kind of you know congratulated me and let me know and I was very excited to receive that text. take us back post draft. >> Do you have other offers? What were your options? Was that the only >> Yeah. Um, so I really got the call from the Browns and the Raiders for mini camp invites and then shortly after my agent called me and said that Tampa Bay wanted you to sign me as a free agent and I obviously, you know, took that opportunity and wanted to come here and be part of the Bucks and what they got going on. So, >> so Todd said, you know, you're not you're not the fastest, you're not the biggest, most athletic, but you are athletic. Um, >> you've kind of done this your whole career, right? Tackles. I mean, >> yeah, it's great of an accomplishment. It is. I think you're not really surprised that you're able to pull this off. >> Yeah. Yeah. No doubt. Like I said, you know, I've always kind of been seen as someone who's might be a little less athletic, but, you know, at the end of the day, when I get out there on the field, you know, it's ball for me. And I believe as far as my knowledge goes and seeing things and being able to digest plays, I think uh you know I got plenty enough ability to do that. And um I'm just going to keep believing in myself, believing in what God gave me and keep putting it to work. >> Your dad brother? >> Yes, sir. Yeah. >> Uh no, that's it. My little sister plays basketball, but other than that, that's it. Yes, sir. >> All right. Thank you. Yes, sir. Appreciate you. Thank you.

title: Todd Bowles on Preparation For Week One | Press Conference | Tampa Bay Buccaneers
text: Morning. >> Coach, your decision to go with Jalen as your number two quarterback, when did that become the most apparent to you and and just what is it that you think you know, he'll be able to function without any experience in that role? >> I mean, we started seeing it in camp. Once he played the first preseason game, when he had a very good game there, it wasn't so much as the plays he made, it was the poise he showed and the learning got better every week and day by day and you know, basically beat him out. >> This is your first chance out there on the field to kind of see the team as it will be. Obviously, you kind of know who the pieces are, but uh can you appreciate the identity of this team yet or is that still to be determined? >> Still to be determined. I mean, we haven't played a game yet. That won't come till about four or five weeks in. >> Uh undrafted rookies, obviously people get excited about guys beating the odds, but when we've talked a lot about Jalen, but let me ask you about Caleb Ford and just what he showed you guys as a linebacker. Didn't have a lot of offers coming out of the draft. What he's done. >> Well, once we put the pads on, I mean, he's not the most athletic, but he is a good athlete. Once he put the pads on, just knowing where to be and striking linemen and making plays and being in the right spot every time, he wasn't getting fooled. He played well on teams. Um he was just an instinctive good football player, you know, and he got better every day and every week. He didn't make the same mistake twice and he beat the rest of the guys out. >> The team added Shawn Murphy-Bunting to the practice squad. Can you talk about just having him back in the organization? >> Means I'm getting old. Uh No, it was great. We talked yesterday. It'd be great to have him because he can play corner, nickel and safety. Need be to get him back in the fold. Obviously, we've changed some few things since he's been here, but you know, having a guy with that kind of experience always helps you. >> We saw Jalen out there doing good in the practice today. Uh are you stopping missing if they could on the field for week one or what's the >> Uh, I'll feel better when I see next week. Uh, right now they're day-by-day, week-by-week. We'll see how they come along next week. >> How about Roseboom's out again? We haven't seen him in a while. I I didn't know he's not on IR, so I'd be safe and not too serious. But what's he dealing with and how far away might he be? >> He's dealing with a foot injury. Uh, he's doing some running. I don't know how far away he'll be. He'll be close. We'll see if he makes it. >> Todd, what was the the thought process in carrying only three safeties and how do you plan to manage that entering the the regular season? >> Well, we can bring somebody up. I mean, we have some guys on the practice squad. It was good for the numbers thing, you know, if he wasn't eligible to be picked up by another team. So, you know, actively he'll be probably on the roster and somebody we're looking to elevate. >> Todd, in terms of you guys had the chance now you kind of had the first week of waiver claims across the league. Is that something you guys were okay with, didn't see a need to go out and get anything else to to fill in what might be a a weak spot anyway? >> I mean, you always look at guys, you know, everybody's kind of letting go the same guys. You know, it's either signing the guys back that's been in your system unless you see somebody that you really want to go out and get. Maybe one or two guys, but not a total overhaul as far as what we saw. >> From the the player that quarterback Baker Mayfield was at the beginning of training camp to now, what areas have you seen growth in? >> Uh, obviously mentally. Just grasping the system even more and understanding and telling guys where to go. He had a good grasp of it at the end of the spring, but he looks very comfortable, even more comfortable than he was right now. Understanding what Zach wants and him and Zach and Chandler have great communication there. So, that's probably the most area he's grown in. >> He talked um, about, you know, Chandler just being a real stickler for footwork. Um, and all the great quarterbacks really are. But but trying to hone in on that and then also really trying to make sure he's getting kind of back into rhythm. Have you seen What what have you seen in those those particular department? >> I've seen both. You know, when he sets his feet he can throw with anybody and he sets them pretty well right now. Challen's going to done a great job staying on him. Baker's done a great job working at it. >> Todd, do you depth you have an edge rusher about as good as you've had since you've been here in your opinion? >> I think it is, yes. >> Todd, to bring in obviously with a young backup you want to have an experienced third quarterback. Just want to see what Easton Stick and and how much his history with Zach helps in there. >> It helped him a lot. You know, he doesn't turn the ball over a lot. He's a good athlete. He can run with the ball. He has championship pedigree from college. Uh he he's a very accurate passer and he's a very smart quarterback to learn. So and he's athletic as well. So with our system as far as half rolls and boots and stuff like that, he was a good fit. You know, it's just a matter of getting him down the system and see how good he can really be. >> The decision to keep Daniel's obviously there's, you know, you see the enormous promise out there in the preseason. But then also making the transition from the the wristband to the the headset, that's not always a smooth one for everybody. And then also I know there were some botched quarterback center exchanges. How do you kind of weigh in some of those hiccups versus some of the good things that you saw on the field? >> I mean, he's a rookie. That's going to happen. I don't think anybody rookie's going to go through preseason unscathed. He's going to learn some things that way. But he's a very bright guy. He understands what he has to do to get better. He works at the things he needs to do to get better even when he's on the scout team. So we see a lot of promise there and he's just got to continually get get better and I'm we think he will. >> Does the fact that he has some of the skill sets, he's almost the exact same size as Baker but can throw off platform, make plays with his feet. Does Does that help from an offensive standpoint if there is a transition at some point? >> I mean, it helps his escapability and familiarity to Zach. But at the same time, he's a very bright guy. He's not just a uh roll out and run around passer. He can sit in the pocket and throw the ball. He can direct traffic very well. He just needs time on task. >> Have you heard about coaches some coaches don't like rookies as much or like trusting veterans more. You'll have a lot of rookies all over this defense this season. Do you Do you even think of it that way or what You don't seem to have a lot of hesitance to to throw these guys out right away and ask them to make plays? >> There's no age limit on when you can play. You know, once you come in the league, if you can learn it fast enough and you're a good football player, you're going to play here. >> Every season teams have different identities. What What do you feel like is a strength this team that it can really lean on? >> I believe we're mentally tough. Again, we haven't played a game yet. Our identity is yet to be revealed, but I I think we are very mentally tough and we have more leaders overall than we've had in the past. >> And to that point, do do you see an area on this team that is your biggest strength? >> I think all areas right now we're going to be better. That'll determine itself. Well, we feel like we got a lot of depth in some areas. We feel like we got a lot of front line strength. So, if we can stay healthy, hopefully every area is a strength on this team. >> How do you feel about these two practices? Obviously, they're shorter practices. Is it just getting guys in the rhythm of this is your room, this is what you'll be working with this year? >> Well, it gives us a head start on Cincinnati. It gives us a jump start, you know, you can't get into too much, but we we got to get in shape and we got to go from playing eight to 10 plays to 60 to 70 plays. So, that part that's part of it as well. So, we got to get in the rhythm and they got to get used to the grind of the season. >> Jason had told us um when he spoke to us this summer that he had never seen Baker so focused. Have you Have you picked up on that as well? >> I believe he's the same since he's been here. You know, he's always focused when he goes out there. He's always in the building early. He's always studying to be better. That's just him, whether it's this year, last year, the year before. Uh he probably has a better grasp of things, especially the offense, after being in one similar a couple years ago. So, he probably has a better grasp of things. >> Todd, we saw Reuben Foster out there participating. AC joint sprain, was his recovery a little bit faster than expected? >> Uh I don't think so. We were expecting him to play. Uh he said he's feeling good, so we're going to roll with that. But, he feels good and we're going to play with it. >> Anything else? Thank you. >> Yep. >> Thank you.

title: Jason Licht on Team Outlook For 2026 Season | Press Conference | Tampa Bay Buccaneers
text: Good morning, Jason. >> All right. [snorts] Fire away. >> Jason, talk about the decision to make Jaylen Daniels your number two quarterback. Undrafted rookie, hasn't played a snap in the NFL. Big year for you guys, obviously. What was it that gave you the confidence that he could step in there and get to week one? >> Well, that's a it's an incredible accomplishment for an undrafted rookie to get that position. Um I can't think in the last decade another time it's happened. And but the the number one thing is he earned it. Um he wasn't just give it given to him. You don't get that honor by just being lucky or or having somebody pull strings for you. He um he earned it, like I said. He earned the trust of his teammates, his coaches. You guys have seen him out here practice during camp. Did some really great things in the game and you know, you can go back and forth with the experience um argument, but we'd rather have a very talented, prepared inexperienced quarterback than going with experience just for the sake of saying that the guy's experienced. So, he's like all rookie quarterbacks, whether you're the number one overall pick or undrafted, um you're going to there's going to be a learning curve, there's going to be ups and downs, but we feel good about where he's at, his trajectory, and and uh we're excited. >> Did it probably happen in some stages where like you realized like wow, he he has to be on the 53 now. And then you go from that to wow, could he be the two? Was there Was there like a a clinching moment or a a reinforcing moment for you to where he gave you the confidence to do what what most teams don't do with their backup quarterback? >> Todd and I have a lot of conversations after during practice, before practice, after practice, uh at night. in his case early in the morning and um I think it was we before our first preseason game, we loved what we were seeing out here the the what we were getting from uh Zach and Chandler and T.J. Um and then I think after the first preseason game with the Jets I think that uh that started to the conversation started going towards well, I mean he's got to prove that he can't be the number two more so than he's got to prove that he can be. >> What about Britain Gardner? He's a guy that every single day it seemed like he was coming out here and making plays. >> Well didn't seem like he was, he was. >> True. >> Um it yeah, every day was making a play on the ball, interception or multiple plays on the ball. He's He's got excellent instincts. He's tough. What I liked about him and I was talking with some of our players about this that he he didn't have a I'm not saying cocky air to him, he just had a very confident air to him and he he knows he's good and in he kind of carried that with him and at that position, you have to have a lot of confidence. So, he's got that going for him too. He's also a rookie, so still got a ways to go here, but we were very excited about him as well. >> But like every time that that room had an injury or somebody had a a day off he he stepped in and it didn't really matter the competition that he was going up against. It could have been a Mecca Abuka, you know, it could have been Ted Hurst. Like those are all really talented players. It seemed like he held his own. >> Yeah, he that's you've nailed it. He doesn't care who he's going against. He sees them all as the same. He doesn't have any bias. >> Can you talk about the running back the situation? I see that you decided to keep Sean Tucker, do a little different, you know, with his deal then also bring Josh onto the practice squad and then combine with Gainwell and Bucky Irving. >> Love that group, that entire group. And just the way that you can construct your roster and keep guys on the practice squad and elevate them. You can, you know, do that whole thing and there's the roster management, the puzzle. It's It's We feel very, very fortunate that we can keep all four cuz we like all four, but you know, Sean's done some really good things for us in the past. He's an explosive runner. He's He's got very good speed and I think it's a nice compliment with uh running backs that we have, including Josh. >> What was the toughest position group to side on when building this roster? >> Well, I don't want to know toughest The one, you know, the first thing comes to mind is we have really good depth, as good as I can remember or have had here uh in my tenure at outside linebacker. And um very, very feel very good about that. I had to make a couple decisions on whether or not we were going to keep extra there. But that was That was tough. That's a good It's a good position to be in, though. >> Jack Stoll had a couple big moments in the preseason. You know, obviously as you said, it's a loaded position group, but and uh people have been talking about him obviously with the college situation, but he was locked in on trying to get a spot. How difficult was that decision to cut him? >> It was Yeah, it's it's hard. None of these decisions are are easy for us. Uh it was tough. You know, he did a He did some really good things, but so did some other guys that we decided to keep on the 53. Um We would love to have him on the practice squad. Would have been great. But, you know, you you don't always get what you want. You can't always have your cake and eat it, too. So, uh wish him the best of luck. He did a great job for us and and uh has a chance to be a a pretty good player. >> Jason, edge rusher has been that position you've been trying to solve the last couple of years now and you just kind of mentioned you have depth at that position now. How much of a relief is it that not just depth but the talent you have at that position now? >> Yeah, it feels good. Now, we haven't played a game yet but it feels very good from what we've seen so far and from all of them. Uh, I want to name all of them. I mean, you guys know what's on the roster. So, I I mean, I'll just go down to Anthony Nelson who also had a strong preseason and he's been Mr. Clutch for us over the years. So, feel very, very good about that that position. >> Jason, one of the tricky parts with with cutting the 53 is is wanting to get the the 16 17 guys to the practice squad the way you want. And you guys kind of went against like the traditional norms in terms of positional lines to carry seven D-linemen to have only three safeties. How how well Hyburn is gone but how well other than that did this go in terms of you being able to keep the depth you wanted to have both between the roster and the practice squad? >> I I think we I think we the the plan that we had, you know, it's it went into effect in being able to keep like uh, you know, the safeties and the ones that we wanted in the practice squad and we think can line up and play on Sunday on next Sunday. So, because of the uh, rules that we have, elevations and things like that, it's obviously this roster is not set in in stone. It can be fluid. It could be fluid today, tomorrow, next week leading up to the game. So, we're always going to be looking for ways that we can upgrade depth at all positions. but it we were happy with the way it turned out. >> You have some pretty young corners on this team. To to be able to get Shawn Murphy-Bunting back even on the practice squad, how how reassuring is that? >> Yeah, they're No, that was great. He He really wanted to be here, too. He had a lot of opportunities and um, I went down to talk to coach about it yesterday and you know, he was obviously all in and you know, he's done some really good things for us. And you know, it could be a player to watch for us and you know, he's going to add to the to the group and provide a lot of competition there. So that's that's that's what you want. >> Is there one thing that stands out about now you got the 53 man roster. You wanted to get tougher. I know on defense based on everything you brought in Bain. What's the one thing that you think this roster this team is better now than since last year? >> We already had a lot of competitive mature win at all costs types of players. We wanted to bring in more and we think we accomplished that and just the vibe at practice, the vibe in the building meetings, all those things just because of the the more that we added, it's really increased and I just I really like this team. I've been in this business long enough to know that I can't come up here and give you predictions. But I just know that I really like the way that Todd is leading this team and what we've what we've added and [clears throat] uh it's it you know, it's pretty apparent. >> It's always great to have a team to have a go-to receiver, the guy that's going to make the big play in the big moment. You have to replace the guy but it may be in the aggregate with your receivers. Who is that guy among this group that you know, that emerges now or is it just there's so many that you know, you just let things take their course? >> We We have a lot of options at that but I mean, I can't I'd be remiss if I didn't mention Chris Godwin for all that he's done for this organization and talk about being a consistent steady Mr. Clutch player, that's That's him and he looks very, very good out there right now. >> Jason's sticking in the wide receiver realm. Your thoughts on Te Herron growing as a wide receiver. title: How the New England Patriots leverage the stadium video screen | Pro Football Talk | NFL on NBC
text: I saw this from Ryan Paganetti, a former and possibly future analytic specialist with teams like the Eagles, the Jaguars, and the Raiders. He's currently independent and available for consulting opportunities. And he found something that is fascinating. And as he calls it diabolically clever. As it relates to messing with kickers who are trying to make a field goal when playing at Gillette Stadium not for the Patriots. The placement of the video boards. And I'd love to know if this was engineered into the into the construction and design of the stadium or whether it just kind of fell into their laps, but the placement of the video boards allows for the creation of an optical illusion. When the kicker is lining up and he sees the two goal posts Paganetti went back to years of TV copy. And he found that when the opposing team is kicking the field goal at the video board that is in the background of the two goal posts they'll have a shot from the back of the kicker looking at the same goal posts. So, what you end up with is four goal posts. And and they're off-center. So, you see fake one, real one, fake one, real one. And then if the wind is blowing and actually the shot is facing toward the kicker. So, you're going to have if the wind is blowing the real goal posts, the flags at the top are going that way. In the shot the other two goal posts, the flags are going that way. And when the Patriots kick, according to Paganetti, he saw at least 52 instances in the games that he reviewed, when the Patriots are kicking, that image is not projected on the video board. It's just a perfect little example of the Patriots' commitment and ability to identify every possible advantage they can muster and use it in their effort to make those little margins go their way. Look at that. Look at that. You're trying to line up the kick. It's one thing if a fan down in row five has a sign with an arrow on it, and the arrow is pointing left or right. You're lining up, and you're looking at those goal posts, and you see four of them. It really is, as Paganetti said, diabolically clever. And I saw in one of his response tweets, because his tweet about the situation sparked conversation and interaction, I got the impression it's not currently legal. I need to get clarity on that, but regardless of what is or isn't legal, the Patriots are the masters of finding the things within the rules that allow them to do whatever they think they need to do to get that little edge. And it's an accumulation a little edge here, a little edge there, a little edge here, and you stack them up, and you put yourself in a position where the things you can't control, the stuff that's going to happen over the course of the game, you overcome the things you can't control by over-controlling the factors that the other team can't or won't. They haven't even thought about it. It just shows how you get that little edge, just a little edge. Goes all the way back to SpyGate from 19 years ago. A little edge, not much, didn't help much, it's a little edge. Just a little bit. You never know when it's going to make a difference. You never know when that little edge is going to manifest itself in knowing what play is coming at the end of Super Bowl 49 so that Brandon Browner can stop the pick Malcolm Butler can jump the route and make the interception and take a Super Bowl victory away. And the Seahawks, legitimate. I'm not saying there was anything wrong with that. My point is it's a combination of perfectly legitimate and maybe things that get close to the line and maybe things that can arguably cross the line, but it's all about stacking up little advantages, as many as possible to the point where the big picture result is what you're looking for week after week, game after game, and ultimately one round after another in the postseason.
